# 1046. This is larger than software package management

It becomes:

```text
Capability Reproducibility Infrastructure
```

---

# 1047. Training Package

Can include:

```text
curriculum
tasks
tests
mentor requirements
```

and transform:

```text
Person Resource
```

to higher Capability Depth.

---

# 1048. Training as capability installation into human resource

Metaphorically yes, but human learning must not be treated like machine package installation.

Better:

```text
Training Project
→ Evidence of acquired capability
```

---

# 1049. Organization Package

Could define:

```text
organizational archetype
```

for creating:

```text
Security Office
Grant Office
Validation Center
```

with:

```text
roles
workflows
interfaces
metrics
```

---

# 1050. Organizational Blueprint

Not automatic cloning, but reusable design template.

---

# 1051. Project Template Package

Example:

```text
Open Source Project Launch
```

template:

```text
repo
license
governance
CI
docs
community
```

---

# 1052. Program Template

Example:

```text
Research-to-Product Program
```

contains stages:

```text
research
reference implementation
validation
pilot
```

---

# 1053. Semantic Package Ecosystem

At maturity registry may contain:

```text
software packages
agent skills
workflows
ontologies
project templates
lab procedures
organizational blueprints
```

---

# 1054. Package Interoperability Standard

All should share:

```text
manifest
capabilities
requirements
constraints
version
provenance
verification
```

---

# 1055. Universal Manifest

This could become a public standard.

Possible name:

```text
Capability Package Manifest — CPM
```

---

# 1056. CPM minimal fields

```text
ID
Version
Provides
Requires
Permissions
Inputs
Outputs
Constraints
Verification
Provenance
```

---

# 1057. Capability Signature

For every provided capability:

```text
Input Types
Output Types
Constraints
Side Effects
Verification
```

---

# 1058. Example

```text
translate_document

Input:
Document

Output:
TranslatedDocument

Constraints:
supported_languages

Side effects:
none
```

---

# 1059. Another example

```text
send_email

Input:
Message

Output:
DeliveryReceipt

Side effects:
external communication

Approval:
required
```

---

# 1060. Package composition becomes type-safe

Output:

```text
SearchResultSet
```

must match next input:

```text
SearchResultSet
```

---

# 1061. Adapter Package

If types differ:

```text
RepositoryList
→
ResourceCandidateList
```

adapter package transforms.

---

# 1062. Semantic Compiler

Can automatically insert known adapters.

---

# 1063. Procedure Graph Compiler

High-level workflow:

```text
Research Topic
→ Literature Review
```

compiles into package graph based on available providers.

---

# 1064. Different node, same workflow

Node A uses:

```text
Package X
```

Node B:

```text
Package Y
```

but both satisfy same semantic workflow.

---

# 1065. Federation portability

Shared Project IR can travel between organizations even if tool stacks differ.

---

# 1066. This is one of the largest architectural advantages

Workflow semantics becomes:

```text
vendor-independent
```

---

# 1067. Next architectural problem

После package manager возникает следующий уровень:

> Как из тысяч capabilities, packages, projects и resources автоматически строить исполнимые процедуры, а не только статические графы?

Следующий модуль:

# **Procedural Graph Compiler & Adaptive Workflow Engine v0.1**

Он будет заниматься переходом:

```text
Goal
↓
Project IR
↓
Task Graph
↓
Procedural Graph
↓
Capability Calls
↓
Tool / Human / Robot Execution
```

И именно там можно подробно соединить:

```text
Semantic Language
Package Manager
Agent OS
Procedural Graphs
n8n / Make
MCP
роботов
людей
```

в единую систему исполнения.
contents.title: Semantic Package Registry & Capability Package Manager v0.1

contents.content: Следующий шаг будет уже особенно практическим: **Procedural Graph Compiler & Adaptive Workflow Engine v0.1** — то есть как из высокоуровневой цели автоматически получить проверяемый граф исполнения, где часть шагов делает человек, часть AI-агент, часть обычная программа, а часть физическая машина.
Продолжение, на русском языке, перевод будет потом

Продолжаю полностью **на русском языке**, без параллельного перевода. Перевод можно будет сделать позже уже для стабилизированной версии документа. Теперь переходим к исполняемому слою: **Procedural Graph Compiler & Adaptive Workflow Engine v0.1** — механизму, который превращает цель и Project IR в конкретный граф действий для людей, AI-агентов, программ, сервисов и физических устройств.

# Procedural Graph Compiler & Adaptive Workflow Engine v0.1

## 1068. Главный переход

До этого система уже знает:

```text
что существует
что требуется
какие capability доступны
какие ресурсы подходят
какие пакеты установлены
```

Теперь возникает следующий вопрос:

> Что именно делать, в каком порядке, какими ресурсами, с какими проверками и что делать при отклонении от плана?

Это задача Procedural Graph.

---

# 1069. Общая цепочка компиляции

```text
Human Goal
↓
Project Compiler
↓
Project IR
↓
Task Compiler
↓
Task Graph
↓
Procedure Compiler
↓
Procedural Graph
↓
Capability Resolver
↓
Execution Backend
↓
Actions / Events / Artifacts
```

---

# 1070. Project Graph ≠ Procedural Graph

Project Graph отвечает:

```text
что должно быть достигнуто?
```

Procedural Graph:

```text
как именно это выполнить?
```

---

# 1071. Пример

Project:

```text
Создать безопасный browser-agent runtime.
```

Project Graph:

```text
Browser Automation
Security
Evaluation
Backend
Deployment
```

Procedural Graph уже конкретнее:

```text
1. Найти существующие runtime
2. Сравнить sandbox approaches
3. Выбрать candidate
4. Развернуть prototype
5. Запустить security tests
6. Запустить benchmark
7. Human review
8. Approve / reject
```

---

# 1072. Task Graph

Первый промежуточный слой:

```text
Task
```

описывает результат работы, но ещё не обязательно низкоуровневую процедуру.

Например:

```text
TASK:
Evaluate sandbox technologies
```

---

# 1073. Procedural Graph

Task может развернуться в:

```text
search
↓
collect candidates
↓
filter licenses
↓
inspect documentation
↓
run benchmark
↓
compare results
↓
produce report
```

---

# 1074. Почему нужны оба уровня

Если хранить сразу тысячи low-level steps:

```text
Project Graph становится нечитаемым.
```

Если хранить только high-level Tasks:

```text
Runtime не знает, что конкретно делать.
```

Поэтому:

```text
Project
→ Tasks
→ Procedures
```

---

# 1075. Procedure

`Procedure` — application-level объект, описывающий способ выполнения Task.

Например:

```yaml
procedure:
  task_id: task_17
  version: 3
  nodes: [...]
  edges: [...]
```

---

# 1076. Procedure может быть временной

Task остаётся тем же:

```text
Evaluate Repository X
```

а Procedure может измениться:

```text
v1 manual inspection
v2 automated benchmark
v3 automated + human review
```

---

# 1077. Это позволяет улучшать способ выполнения без изменения Project IR

Очень важное разделение:

```text
WHAT
```

и:

```text
HOW
```

---

# 1078. Procedure Node

Минимальный узел:

```text
ACTION
DECISION
WAIT
CHECK
PARALLEL
MERGE
LOOP
SUBPROCEDURE
```

---

# 1079. ACTION node

Например:

```text
SEARCH_GITHUB
```

---

# 1080. DECISION node

```text
License compatible?
```

ветки:

```text
YES → continue
NO → reject candidate
UNKNOWN → human/legal review
```

---

# 1081. WAIT node

Для:

```text
ожидать API response
ожидать человека
ожидать лабораторию
ожидать события
```

---

# 1082. CHECK node

Проверяет:

```text
verification condition
policy condition
constraint condition
```

---

# 1083. PARALLEL node

Запускает несколько веток:

```text
search papers
search GitHub
search experts
```

одновременно.

---

# 1084. MERGE node

Объединяет результаты:

```text
Candidate Set A
+
Candidate Set B
+
Candidate Set C
```

---

# 1085. LOOP node

Например:

```text
для каждого repository:
  inspect
  evaluate
```

---

# 1086. SUBPROCEDURE

Вызывает reusable workflow:

```text
EvaluateRepository()
```

---

# 1087. Typed Procedure

У каждого узла должны быть:

```text
Inputs
Outputs
Capabilities
Constraints
Verification
```

---

# 1088. Example node

```yaml
node:
  id: inspect_repo

  action: repository_inspection

  inputs:
    - repository_ref

  outputs:
    - repository_report

  requires:
    - cap_repository_analysis
```

---

# 1089. Capability-based execution

Procedure не обязательно говорит:

```text
use exact Tool X
```

Лучше:

```text
REQUIRES capability repository_analysis
```

А Runtime выбирает provider.

---

# 1090. Late Binding

Binding может происходить:

```text
при compile time
```

или:

```text
при runtime
```

---

# 1091. Compile-time binding

Использовать, если:

```text
project.lock pins provider
```

например:

```text
GitHubConnector v1.4
```

---

# 1092. Runtime binding

Использовать, если допустим выбор:

```text
Provider A
Provider B
Provider C
```

по текущей availability/cost.

---

# 1093. Procedure Compiler

Вход:

```text
Task
Context
Available capabilities
Policies
Packages
```

Выход:

```text
Executable Procedural Graph
```

---

# 1094. Compiler stages

```text
1. Task decomposition
2. Pattern/archetype lookup
3. Capability resolution
4. Dependency construction
5. Policy insertion
6. Verification insertion
7. Error paths
8. Optimization
```

---

# 1095. Task decomposition

Task:

```text
Validate technology X
```

разворачивается:

```text
find evidence
inspect implementation
run experiment
compare requirements
produce conclusion
```

---

# 1096. Archetype lookup

Если существует package:

```text
TechnologyValidationWorkflow
```

compiler использует его вместо генерации с нуля.

---

# 1097. Generate only missing pieces

Лучший принцип:

```text
reuse known procedure
+
synthesize only gaps
```

Это делает system более стабильной.

---

# 1098. Procedure Archetype

Примеры:

```text
Research Review
Repository Evaluation
Grant Eligibility Check
Security Review
Experiment
Deployment
Manufacturing Test
```

---

# 1099. Compiler chooses archetype by Task semantics

Например:

```text
TASK subtype = SECURITY_REVIEW
```

→ candidate:

```text
SecurityReviewProcedure
```

---

# 1100. Archetype parameterization

Параметры:

```text
artifact
risk class
environment
deadline
required evidence
```

---

# 1101. Capability resolution

Для каждого node:

```text
What capability is required?
```

Например:

```text
PDF extraction
```

providers:

```text
local package
remote service
AI agent
human
```

---

# 1102. Policy insertion

Если Action имеет side effect:

```text
SEND_EMAIL
```

Compiler вставляет:

```text
APPROVAL CHECK
```

перед Action.

---

# 1103. Example

Исходный workflow:

```text
Draft Email
↓
Send Email
```

после policy compilation:

```text
Draft Email
↓
Human Review
↓
Approval
↓
Send Email
```

---

# 1104. Physical safety insertion

Workflow:

```text
Run robot task
```

может компилироваться:

```text
Simulation
↓
Safety Check
↓
Human Approval
↓
Physical Execution
```

---

# 1105. Verification insertion

Task:

```text
Build parser
```

не заканчивается:

```text
code generated
```

Compiler добавляет:

```text
tests
schema validation
human/code review
```

---

# 1106. DONE_IF contract

Каждый Task должен иметь:

```text
DONE_IF
```

Например:

```text
parser passes 95% golden fixtures
```

---

# 1107. Task Completion

Правило:

```text
Action executed
```

не означает:

```text
Task completed
```

---

# 1108. Completion pipeline

```text
execute
↓
produce artifact
↓
verify
↓
accept
↓
DONE
```

---

# 1109. Failure paths

Каждый risky node должен иметь:

```text
on_failure
```

---

# 1110. Failure categories

```text
TOOL_FAILURE
INPUT_INVALID
CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE
POLICY_DENIED
QUALITY_FAILURE
TIMEOUT
RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE
UNKNOWN
```

---

# 1111. Different failures require different recovery

Tool failure:

```text
retry / switch provider
```

Quality failure:

```text
revise output
```

Resource unavailable:

```text
replan
```

Policy denied:

```text
human escalation / alternative method
```

---

# 1112. Retry policy

Не:

```text
retry everything 5 times
```

Нужно учитывать failure class.

---

# 1113. Transient error

Например:

```text
HTTP 503
```

→ retry.

---

# 1114. Deterministic invalid input

Например:

```text
schema invalid
```

→ retrying same input бессмысленно.

---

# 1115. Adaptive Workflow

Procedural Graph может меняться во время выполнения.

Но не произвольно.

---

# 1116. Adaptation triggers

```text
new evidence
resource unavailable
task failed
deadline changed
constraint changed
new capability discovered
```

---

# 1117. Replanning boundary

Не пересобирать весь Project при каждом событии.

Определять:

```text
affected subgraph
```

---

# 1118. Local Replanning

Например:

```text
Repository A unavailable
```

затрагивает только:

```text
integration branch
```

---

# 1119. Global Replanning

Если:

```text
core requirement changed
```

может потребоваться пересборка большого Task Graph.

---

# 1120. Replan event

```text
REPLAN_REQUESTED
```

должен содержать:

```text
trigger
affected nodes
reason
```

---

# 1121. Procedure Versioning

При replanning:

```text
Procedure v3
→
Procedure v4
```

Старый graph не стирается.

---

# 1122. Running nodes

При обновлении procedure нужно определить:

```text
что делать уже запущенным Actions?
```

---

# 1123. Safe cases

Если branch independent:

```text
allow finish
```

---

# 1124. Unsafe cases

Если result больше не нужен:

```text
cancel if reversible
```

---

# 1125. Irreversible action

Например:

```text
send contract
manufacture batch
move robot
```

не может быть просто «отменён».

Need compensation/recovery.

---

# 1126. Side-effect classes

Freeze:

```text
READ_ONLY
REVERSIBLE
COMPENSATABLE
IRREVERSIBLE
```

---

# 1127. READ_ONLY

Например:

```text
search
read file
```

---

# 1128. REVERSIBLE

Например:

```text
create temporary branch
```

can delete/revert.

---

# 1129. COMPENSATABLE

Например:

```text
reserve lab slot
```

can later release.

---

# 1130. IRREVERSIBLE

Например:

```text
physical cutting
external legal filing
```

---

# 1131. Compiler uses side-effect class

Чем выше необратимость:

```text
тем раньше и сильнее approval / simulation / verification
```

---

# 1132. Procedural Graph node state

```text
PENDING
READY
CLAIMED
RUNNING
WAITING
REVIEW
DONE
FAILED
SKIPPED
CANCELLED
```

---

# 1133. CLAIMED

Исполнитель резервирует node.

Это предотвращает:

```text
двойное выполнение
```

---

# 1134. Lease

Claim может иметь:

```text
lease_until
```

Если executor исчез:

```text
lease expires
```

node возвращается в READY, если повтор безопасен.

---

# 1135. Idempotency

Каждый repeatable Action должен иметь:

```text
idempotency_key
```

---

# 1136. Example

```text
Create GitHub issue
```

при retry не должен создать:

```text
5 одинаковых issues
```

---

# 1137. At-least-once execution

Практически реалистичная модель:

```text
event/action may be delivered more than once
```

поэтому actions должны быть repeat-safe.

---

# 1138. Exactly-once не нужно обещать

Лучше:

```text
at-least-once
+
idempotency
```

---

# 1139. Scheduler

Runtime continuously computes:

```text
which nodes are READY?
```

---

# 1140. Readiness criteria

Node ready, если:

```text
dependencies satisfied
inputs available
provider available
constraints pass
required approvals exist
```

---

# 1141. Scheduler priority

Можно учитывать:

```text
critical path
deadline
resource availability
project priority
```

но не один opaque score.

---

# 1142. Critical Path

Task Graph позволяет определить:

```text
which tasks delay whole project
```

---

# 1143. Slack

Некоторые Tasks могут быть delayed без project delay.

Runtime может использовать этот запас.

---

# 1144. Resource-aware scheduling

Если два Tasks требуют:

```text
same specialist
```

Scheduler serializes or allocates capacity.

---

# 1145. AI resource scheduling

AI may have:

```text
token budget
concurrency limit
rate limit
```

---

# 1146. Human scheduling

Для людей учитывать:

```text
availability
consent
working hours
existing assignments
```

---

# 1147. Physical scheduling

Для machine:

```text
booking
setup
maintenance
```

---

# 1148. Mixed scheduler

Таким образом один scheduler видит:

```text
Human
AI
Software
Machine
Lab
```

через общую Resource/Capability abstraction.

---

# 1149. Но execution backends различаются

Universal scheduler:

```text
assigns work
```

Backend:

```text
executes according to resource type
```

---

# 1150. Human Backend

Создаёт:

```text
task card
context package
deadline
required output
```

---

# 1151. AI Backend

Создаёт:

```text
prompt/context
tools
policies
output schema
```

---

# 1152. Tool Backend

Выполняет:

```text
deterministic API/tool call
```

---

# 1153. Robot Backend

Выполняет:

```text
device skill
```

через safety controller.

---

# 1154. External Organization Backend

Создаёт:

```text
federated task proposal
```

---

# 1155. Backend Interface

Общий контракт:

```text
prepare()
execute()
observe()
verify()
cancel()
```

---

# 1156. Command vs Event

Compiler creates:

```text
COMMAND
```

Runtime later records:

```text
EVENT
```

---

# 1157. Example

Command:

```text
RUN benchmark
```

Event:

```text
BENCHMARK_COMPLETED
```

---

# 1158. Never store command as if it happened

Это принципиально для audit.

---

# 1159. Procedure Inputs

Node может принимать:

```text
Artifact
Entity reference
Claim set
Scalar value
Context
```

---

# 1160. Procedure Outputs

Могут быть:

```text
Artifact
Claim
Evidence
Event
Decision proposal
```

---

# 1161. LLM output

LLM не должен напрямую менять World State.

Он produces:

```text
Artifact / Candidate Claims / Proposal
```

---

# 1162. Structured Output

По возможности:

```text
Pydantic / JSON Schema
```

---

# 1163. Validation

После LLM:

```text
schema
semantic rules
constraints
```

перед записью.

---

# 1164. Free text remains Artifact

Если LLM пишет:

```text
analysis
```

это Artifact.

Любые extracted facts становятся отдельными Claims.

---

# 1165. Context Compiler

Перед каждым node:

```text
Task + state
↓
Context Builder
```

собирает только relevant context.

---

# 1166. Не использовать огромную историю чата

Context Package:

```text
goal
current task
inputs
relevant claims
constraints
previous outputs
```

---

# 1167. Context Budget

У каждого AI node:

```text
max_context
```

Context Builder prioritizes:

```text
hard constraints
current artifacts
critical evidence
```

---

# 1168. Memory tiers

```text
Scratch
Working
Project
World
```

---

# 1169. Scratch

Temporary reasoning/output during one action.

---

# 1170. Working

Current procedure execution.

---

# 1171. Project Memory

Validated project-level Claims/Artifacts.

---

# 1172. World Memory

Cross-project reusable knowledge.

---

# 1173. Promotion

Observation:

```text
scratch
↓
candidate claim
↓
validation
↓
project/world memory
```

---

# 1174. Procedure Blackboard

Agents communicate through:

```text
shared structured state
```

not direct endless conversations.

---

# 1175. Blackboard contents

```text
Tasks
Claims
Artifacts
Events
Decisions
Open Questions
```

---

# 1176. Agent message

A message is:

```text
request / proposal / report
```

not automatically fact.

---

# 1177. Agent message types

```text
TASK_REQUEST
TASK_RESULT
QUESTION
EVIDENCE_FOUND
BLOCKER
REVIEW_REQUEST
ESCALATION
```

---

# 1178. Handoff

When executor changes:

```text
what is done
what remains
what artifacts exist
what blocks progress
```

---

# 1179. Handoff Package

```yaml
handoff:
  task: ...
  completed: [...]
  remaining: [...]
  artifacts: [...]
  blockers: [...]
  requested_capability: ...
```

---

# 1180. Parallel Agents

One task may be decomposed:

```text
Agent A: papers
Agent B: repos
Agent C: patents
```

---

# 1181. Merge

Their outputs are merged into:

```text
Evidence Set
```

---

# 1182. No majority-vote truth

Если A и B disagree:

```text
store conflict
```

Не:


---

# 1351. Следующий фундаментальный слой

После появления Procedural Graph Compiler возникает следующий вопрос:

> Как система должна управлять целями, приоритетами и конфликтующими стратегическими намерениями, если одновременно существуют тысячи проектов и workflows?

Следующий модуль:

# **Goal, Policy & Governance Engine v0.1**

Он должен формализовать:

```text
кто задаёт цели;
какие цели обязательны;
какие цели конфликтуют;
кто имеет право принимать решения;
какие действия запрещены;
где требуется согласование;
как стратегия превращается в ограничения для Project/Procedure Compiler;
как человек может остановить, изменить или отменить автоматическое выполнение.
```

Это будет слой, который окончательно отделяет **интеллект и автоматизацию** от **власти, полномочий и целей** — критически важный элемент для безопасной работы всей архитектуры.
contents.title: Procedural Graph Compiler & Adaptive Workflow Engine v0.1

contents.content: Следующая часть логично будет посвящена **Goal, Policy & Governance Engine v0.1**: именно он определит, кто вправе ставить системе цели, какие цели могут исполняться автоматически, где требуется человек, как разрешать конфликт «быстрее / дешевле / безопаснее / открытее» и как управлять всей системой без превращения AI в самостоятельный источник целей.
Продолжение

Продолжаю полностью на русском языке. Теперь переходим к **Goal, Policy & Governance Engine v0.1** — слою, который определяет не «как выполнить задачу», а **кто вправе ставить цели, какие ограничения обязательны, где требуется человеческое решение и как разрешать конфликты между скоростью, стоимостью, безопасностью, открытостью и другими приоритетами**.

# Goal, Policy & Governance Engine v0.1

## 1352. Главный переход

До этого Innovation OS уже умеет:

```text
Goal
↓
Project IR
↓
Task Graph
↓
Procedural Graph
↓
Resource Resolution
↓
Execution
```

Но остаётся принципиальный вопрос:

> Откуда сама Goal взялась и кто имеет право её утвердить?

AI может:

```text
обнаружить проблему
предложить opportunity
создать project hypothesis
сформировать procedure
```

Но это ещё не означает:

```text
система получила право действовать
```

# 1353. Разделение интеллекта и власти

Это один из важнейших принципов всей архитектуры.

```text
INTELLIGENCE
может:
анализировать
предлагать
моделировать
объяснять
```

Но:

```text
AUTHORITY
определяет:
что разрешено
что обязательно
кто может принять решение
```

```text

Analysis

Proposal

Governance

Decision

Execution
```

```text
Develop secure agent runtime.
```

или:

```text
Increase robotics testing capacity.
```

```text
CLAIM
```

```text
что нужно сделать
```

# 1361. Strategic Goal

```text
enables
```

```text
PROJECT
AI_HYPOTHESIS
EVENT
```

```text
Goal Proposal
```

```text
DECISION
```

```text
кто имеет право принимать какой тип решения?
```

```text
security expertise
```

```text
responsible for preparing decision
```

но не:

```text
final decision
```

```text
APPROVER
```

# 1379. OWNER

```text
goal / resource / project
```

# 1382. REVIEWER

Может анализировать историю и compliance.

```text
executor ≠ approver
```

```text
2 of 3 approvals
```

```text
all required authorities
```

Например:

```yaml
approval:
```

# 1390. Policy

Policy определяет:

```text
что разрешено

что требует review
```

# 1391. Policy Effects

Freeze:

```text
ALLOW
DENY
REQUIRE_APPROVAL
REQUIRE_REVIEW
REQUIRE_EVIDENCE
REQUIRE_SIMULATION
```

# 1392. Policy Rule

```yaml
policy:

    effect: REQUIRE_APPROVAL
```

# 1393. Deny-by-default vs allow-by-default

Для low-risk read operations можно использовать:


Для privileged actions лучше:

```text
deny-by-default
```

# 1394. Policy Scope

Policy may apply to:

```text
organization
project
resource
action type
capability
context
jurisdiction
```

---

# 1395. Policy Hierarchy

Например:

```text
Organization Policy
↓
Program Policy
↓
Project Policy
↓
Action Policy
```

# 1396. Policy precedence

```text
lower level overrides higher
```

Для v0.1 лучше консервативно:

```text
DENY dominates ALLOW
```

если нет explicit exception authority.

# 1397. Exception

Exception itself must be:

```text
Decision
```

with:

```text
authority
reason
validity period
```

# 1398. Temporary Exception

Например:

```text
valid_to
```

# 1400. Policy conflict

Example:


```text
external cloud preferred
```

```text
DENY
```

unless authorized exception exists.

# 1401. Policy Compiler

Before execution:

```text
Action
+
Context
+
Actor
+
Target
↓
Policy Engine
↓
Decision
```

# 1402. Policy Decision

Output:

```text
ALLOW
DENY
APPROVAL_REQUIRED
REVIEW_REQUIRED
```

with explanation.

```text
human-readable explanation
```

```text
prefer open source
```

```text
proprietary software prohibited
```

```text
question
options

authority
evidence
reason
time
```

```text
candidate Programs / Projects

```

# 1511. Human-readable legal contract remains separate

Again:

```text
semantic agreement ≠ legal contract
```

---

# 1512. Public Governance

For open-source/public projects:

```text
community voting
maintainer approval
RFC process
```

can be modeled as governance archetypes.

---

# 1513. RFC Governance

Example:

```text
Proposal
↓
Discussion
↓
Review
↓
Decision
↓
Implementation
```

---

# 1514. This is useful for IIR standard itself

Changes to core ontology can use:

```text
Semantic RFC
```

with stricter authority.

---

# 1515. Core-change policy

Example:

```text
No core predicate removal
without major version.
```

---

# 1516. Package governance

New high-risk package requires:

```text
security approval
```

before system.lock update.

---

# 1517. Model governance

Switching AI model for critical workflow may require:

```text
benchmark
review
approval
```

---

# 1518. Data governance

Dataset may have:

```text
access policy
purpose limitation
retention policy
```

---

# 1519. Artifact governance

Some documents:

```text
PUBLIC
PRIVATE
CONFIDENTIAL
```

with separate permissions.

---

# 1520. Knowledge publication policy

Private Claim can become public only through:

```text
sanitize
review
approve
publish
```

---

# 1521. Open Knowledge Governance

Important for Technopedia.

Need distinguish:

```text
public fact
community hypothesis
personal opinion
validated reference
```

---

# 1522. Publication states

```text
DRAFT
REVIEW
PUBLISHED
CONTESTED
RETRACTED
```

---

# 1523. Community contribution

External person/agent can propose edit.

But:

```text
proposal ≠ authoritative publication
```

---

# 1524. Multiple versions can coexist

Unlike classical encyclopedia:

```text
one final article
```

system may preserve:

```text
alternative interpretations
branches
claims
evidence
```

---

# 1525. Governance can vary by knowledge space

Example:

```text
official standard page
```

strict review.

```text
discussion area
```

open contribution.

---

# 1526. AI participation

AI can:

```text
draft
summarize
detect conflicts
suggest citations
```

but authorship/provenance remains explicit.

---

# 1527. Agent Identity

If AI publishes Claim:

```text
issuer = agent_instance_X
```

with:

```text
model
package
version
```

---

# 1528. Human Approval of AI content

Can change publication state, but should not erase AI provenance.

---

# 1529. Governance Dashboard

Minimum views:

```text
Goals
Policies
Pending Decisions
Authority Map
Exceptions
Audit
```

---

# 1530. Goals View

Shows:

```text
active goals
dependencies
conflicts
progress
```

---

# 1531. Policy View

Shows:

```text
active rules
scope
version
exceptions
```

---

# 1532. Pending Decisions

Shows:

```text
what waits for approval
why
deadline impact
```

---

# 1533. Authority Map

Shows:

```text
who can approve what
```

---

# 1534. Exception View

Shows:

```text
temporary overrides
expiry
reason
```

---

# 1535. Audit View

Shows:

```text
goal → decision → action → outcome
```

---

# 1536. Governance API

Minimum:

```text
POST /goals
POST /goals/{id}/approve
POST /goals/{id}/pause

GET /policies
POST /policies/evaluate

POST /decisions
POST /decisions/{id}/approve

GET /authority/resolve
POST /exceptions
```

---

# 1537. Policy Evaluation endpoint

Input:

```yaml
actor: agent_17
action: send_email
target: external_party
context: project_X
```

Output:

```yaml
result: REQUIRE_APPROVAL
policy_ids:
  - communication_policy_4
```

---

# 1538. Goal approval endpoint

Should check:

```text
authority
conflicts
required evidence
```

before approval.

---

# 1539. Governance Event types

```text
GOAL_PROPOSED
GOAL_APPROVED
GOAL_REJECTED
POLICY_ACTIVATED
POLICY_CHANGED
DECISION_APPROVED
EXCEPTION_GRANTED
EXCEPTION_EXPIRED
OVERRIDE_USED
EMERGENCY_STOP
```

---

# 1540. Governance Gold Dataset

For improvement:

```text
proposal
decision
reason
outcome
```

can be analyzed.

But system should not learn:

```text
"humans usually approve this, so auto-approve"
```

unless explicit policy authorizes such automation.

---

# 1541. Decision Pattern Detection

AI may observe:

```text
same low-risk approval repeated 500 times
```

and propose:

```text
policy automation
```

---

# 1542. Governance Automation Proposal

Example:

```text
Automatically allow read-only GitHub searches
within approved project.
```

---

# 1543. Then human governance may approve the rule

This converts repeated manual decision into policy.

---

# 1544. Governance Compaction

Таким образом система может постепенно переходить:

```text
manual approvals
↓
stable policy
↓
bounded automation
```

---

# 1545. Reverse direction also needed

If automated policy causes problems:

```text
increase human review
```

---

# 1546. Policy rollback

Same as software:

```text
new policy
↓
unexpected effects
↓
rollback
```

---

# 1547. Governance Simulation

Before activation:

```text
replay historical events
```

under candidate policy.

---

# 1548. Example

Candidate policy:

```text
AI can auto-send internal notifications.
```

Replay shows:

```text
how many actions would have been auto-approved?
```

---

# 1549. Policy Shadow Mode

New policy can evaluate:

```text
what it would decide
```

without actually controlling runtime.

---

# 1550. Compare

```text
current policy
vs
shadow policy
```

---

# 1551. Governance metrics

Useful:

```text
decision latency
approval queue
policy-denial frequency
override frequency
exception frequency
```

---

# 1552. But not as manager performance scores

Metrics are for process diagnostics.

---

# 1553. High exception rate

May mean:

```text
policy poorly fits reality
```

rather than:

```text
users are bad
```

---

# 1554. High override rate

Could indicate:

```text
automation needs adjustment
```

---

# 1555. Governance Bottleneck Engine

Detect:

```text
one approval role blocks many projects
```

---

# 1556. Possible interventions

```text
delegate
increase capacity
automate low-risk cases
redesign policy
```

---

# 1557. Goal hierarchy visualization

2D:

```text
Mission
├── Strategic Goal A
│   ├── Program 1
│   └── Program 2
└── Strategic Goal B
```

---

# 1558. Goal-to-Execution trace

Click Goal:

```text
Goal
↓
Programs
↓
Projects
↓
Tasks
↓
Actions
↓
Artifacts
```

---

# 1559. This gives strategic observability

Management sees:

```text
что реально делается ради какой цели
```

---

# 1560. Orphan Project Detector

Project not linked to any active goal:

```text
ORPHAN PROJECT
```

might be legitimate, but requires review.

---

# 1561. Goal without execution

Goal approved but:

```text
no projects
no resources
```

→ strategic execution gap.

---

# 1562. Goal-resource mismatch

High-priority Goal receives:

```text
very little capacity
```

while low-priority activities consume much.

System can expose mismatch.

---

# 1563. Strategy-to-budget linkage

Resource Accounting can answer:

```text
how much capacity is allocated to each strategic goal?
```

---

# 1564. Strategy Drift

If actual execution gradually diverges from:

```text
approved strategy
```

system detects:

```text
Strategy Drift
```

---

# 1565. Example

Strategy:

```text
open-source-first
```

Actual:

```text
80% new dependencies proprietary
```

System flags discrepancy.

---

# 1566. Goal Drift

Project originally intended:

```text
build shared benchmark
```

but execution becomes:

```text
custom solution for one client
```

May require scope review.

---

# 1567. Scope Change

Significant scope change requires:

```text
Decision
```

not silent adaptation.

---

# 1568. Adaptive Runtime boundary

Runtime can adapt:

```text
method
provider
ordering
```

within approved Goal/scope.

It cannot silently redefine:

```text
why project exists
```

---

# 1569. This is the central governance boundary

```text
HOW
may be adaptively optimized.

WHAT/WHY
requires governance.
```

---

# 1570. Bounded Goal Delegation

Human can explicitly authorize:

```text
AI may create subgoals needed
to achieve Goal X
```

within scope.

---

# 1571. Example

Goal:

```text
Deploy service.
```

AI may generate subgoal:

```text
Fix failing integration test.
```

without executive approval.

---

# 1572. But not:

```text
Change product target market.
```

That exceeds scope.

---

# 1573. Goal Scope Contract

Can define:

```text
allowed subgoal types
budget
time
resources
forbidden actions
```

---

# 1574. Goal Budget

Not just money.

```text
compute
human time
external actions
```

---

# 1575. Goal termination condition

Every Goal should know:

```text
success
failure
expiration
cancellation
```

---

# 1576. Goal State is derived partly from evidence

Example:

```text
Success criterion verified
```

→ Goal may become ACHIEVED.

---

# 1577. But human acknowledgement may still be required

For strategic Goal:

```text
evidence suggests achieved
```

system may propose:

```text
CLOSE GOAL
```

rather than close automatically.

---

# 1578. Governance modes by Goal type

Operational low-risk:

```text
automatic closure
```

Strategic:

```text
human closure
```

---

# 1579. Goal Review Cycle

Long-running Goal:

```text
review every quarter
```

---

# 1580. Review asks

```text
still relevant?
assumptions valid?
resources adequate?
```

---

# 1581. Assumption Registry integration

Goal can depend on:

```text
Assumptions
```

If assumption refuted:

```text
Goal Review
```

---

# 1582. Example

Goal:

```text
build technology X
```

Assumption:

```text
market need persists
```

New Evidence refutes it.

System should not continue blindly.

---

# 1583. Governance + Counterfactual Engine

Before major decision:

```text
simulate options
```

---

# 1584. Example

Decision:

```text
Create internal Security Office?
```

Scenarios:

```text
internal unit
external providers
hybrid
```

Governance receives trade-offs.

---

# 1585. Governance does not become optimizer dictatorship

Simulation informs authority.

Authority decides.

---

# 1586. Goal/Policy package system

Policies and governance archetypes can be packages.

But high-trust core policies should remain protected.

---

# 1587. Governance Package

Examples:

```text
Research Consortium Governance
Open Source Project Governance
High-Risk Robotics Governance
```

---

# 1588. Governance Archetype

Contains:

```text
roles
approval paths
decision classes
policy defaults
```

---

# 1589. Organization can instantiate template

Then customize.

---

# 1590. Policy library

Common policies:

```text
external communication
data access
resource spending
package installation
physical execution
publication
```

---

# 1591. Policy testing

Every policy package should include:

```text
allowed case tests
denied case tests
edge cases
```

---

# 1592. Formal policy language later

v0.1 can use:

```text
structured conditions
```

rather than inventing full new language immediately.

---

# 1593. Example structured condition

```yaml
if:
  action_type: EXTERNAL_MESSAGE
  visibility: CONFIDENTIAL

then:
  effect: REQUIRE_APPROVAL

authority:
  role: PROJECT_OWNER
```

---

# 1594. Complex rule

Could eventually compile to:

```text
OPA/Rego-like backend
```

or custom engine.

But semantic representation remains backend-independent.

---

# 1595. Governance microkernel

Minimal trusted governance core:

```text
Policy Evaluation
Authority Resolution
Decision Registry
Approval Gates
Override/Emergency Stop
Audit
```

---

# 1596. Why microkernel

Because this is security-sensitive and should remain small.

---

# 1597. LLM role in governance

LLM may:

```text
explain policy
find relevant rules
draft decision summary
detect conflicts
```

---

# 1598. LLM should not silently invent authority

Authority is deterministic registry/policy data.

---

# 1599. LLM should not silently waive rule

Exception requires authorized Decision.

---

# 1600. Governance invariants

Freeze initial set.

### Invariant 1

```text
Proposal ≠ Decision.
```

### Invariant 2

```text
Capability ≠ Authority.
```

### Invariant 3

```text
No response ≠ Approval.
```

### Invariant 4

```text
Runtime cannot exceed approved Goal scope.
```

### Invariant 5

```text
High-impact actions require applicable governance checks.
```

### Invariant 6

```text
Policy version used for execution must be auditable.
```

### Invariant 7

```text
Human override must be explicit and logged.
```

### Invariant 8

```text
AI may propose goals but does not become default source of organizational authority.
```

---

# 1601. Full control chain

Теперь вся система имеет:

```text
MISSION
↓
GOALS
↓
POLICIES / AUTHORITY
↓
PROGRAMS
↓
PROJECTS
↓
TASKS
↓
PROCEDURES
↓
RESOURCE BINDINGS
↓
ACTIONS
↓
EVENTS
↓
EVIDENCE
↓
WORLD STATE
```

---

# 1602. Обратная петля

```text
WORLD STATE
↓
Observed Outcomes
↓
Goal Evaluation
↓
Policy Review
↓
Strategy Review
```

---

# 1603. Это уже полноценная cybernetic governance loop

Но не автономная власть AI.

Структура:

```text
Human/Institutional Authority
↓
Goals + Policies
↓
Machine Execution
↓
Evidence
↓
Human/Institutional Review
```

---

# 1604. Виртуальный технопарк после Governance Layer

Теперь 2D/3D интерфейс может показывать не только:

```text
проекты
людей
машины
```

но и:

```text
кто чем управляет
какие цели активны
какие действия ждут решения
какие политики блокируют путь
```

---

# 1605. Governance Overlay

В 2D/3D:

```text
green:
authorized

yellow:
approval required

red:
policy blocked
```

Это presentation only, но operationally полезно.

---

# 1606. Decision Rooms

В MMORPG-представлении можно сделать:

```text
совет / decision room
```

как UI для governance queue.

Не декоративный объект:

```text
он показывает реальные Decisions.
```

---

# 1607. Strategy Map

Отдельный уровень:

```text
Mission
Goals
Programs
Capability Investments
```

---

# 1608. Operational Map

Другой уровень:

```text
Tasks
Resources
Queues
Actions
```

---

# 1609. Разделение стратегического и оперативного интерфейса

Это уменьшает визуальный хаос.

---

# 1610. Следующий фундаментальный слой

После того как появились:

```text
World State
Capability Market
Package Manager
Procedural Runtime
Governance
```

возникает ещё одна ключевая задача:

> Как проверять, действительно ли вся система работает правильно, не деградирует ли качество, не расходятся ли модели с реальностью и не накапливает ли она ошибки?

Следующий модуль:

# **Verification, Benchmarking & Epistemic Quality Engine v0.1**

Он должен объединить:

```text
тестирование программ;
проверку AI-ответов;
научную верификацию;
human review;
benchmarking;
calibration;
достоверность Claims;
качество Evidence;
оценку Procedure;
сравнение predicted vs actual;
обнаружение деградации;
```

в одну общую архитектуру проверки.

Именно этот слой нужен, чтобы Innovation OS была не просто системой, которая много делает, а системой, которая умеет постоянно проверять, **насколько её собственная модель мира и результаты соответствуют реальности**.

contents.content: Следующая часть будет про **Verification, Benchmarking & Epistemic Quality Engine v0.1** — общий «контур истины и качества» для людей, AI-агентов, кода, научных гипотез, процедур и физических экспериментов.
Продолжение

Продолжаю полностью **на русском языке**. Теперь переходим к **Verification, Benchmarking & Epistemic Quality Engine v0.1** — общему контуру проверки, который должен отвечать не только «выполнено ли действие», но и **правильно ли оно выполнено, достаточно ли доказательств, насколько вывод соответствует реальности и не деградирует ли система со временем**.

# Verification, Benchmarking & Epistemic Quality Engine v0.1

## 1611. Главный переход

До этого Innovation OS умеет:

```text
поставить Goal
↓
создать Project
↓
скомпилировать Procedure
↓
выбрать Resources
↓
выполнить Actions
↓
получить Artifacts / Claims / Events
```

Но остаётся критический вопрос:

> Откуда система знает, что результат действительно корректен?

---

# 1612. Execution Success ≠ Correct Result

Например:

```text
API call succeeded
```

не означает:

```text
данные правильные
```

И:

```text
LLM ответил без ошибки
```

не означает:

```text
ответ соответствует фактам
```

И:

```text
эксперимент завершился
```

не означает:

```text
гипотеза подтверждена
```

---

# 1613. Поэтому после Execution нужен отдельный Verification Layer

```text
Action
↓
Output
↓
Verification
↓
Evidence
↓
Acceptance / Rejection
↓
World State Update
```

---

# 1614. Центральная формула

```text
CLAIM
+
EVIDENCE
+
VERIFICATION PROCEDURE
+
CONTEXT
=
EPISTEMIC STATE
```

---

# 1615. Что должен проверять Verification Engine

Минимум:

```text
структурную корректность
семантическую корректность
фактическую поддержку
соответствие требованиям
качество
полноту
воспроизводимость
согласованность
```

---

# 1616. Несколько классов проверки

Можно выделить:

```text
SCHEMA VERIFICATION
CONSTRAINT VERIFICATION
EVIDENCE VERIFICATION
BEHAVIORAL VERIFICATION
HUMAN REVIEW
EXPERIMENTAL VERIFICATION
CROSS-SOURCE VERIFICATION
REGRESSION VERIFICATION
```

---

# 1617. Schema Verification

Самый простой уровень.

Проверяет:

```text
правильные поля?
правильные типы?
обязательные значения?
```

Например:

```text
FundingCallIR
```

без deadline может быть:

```text
schema-invalid
```

если deadline required.

---

# 1618. Schema Valid ≠ Semantically Correct

Например:

```yaml
temperature: 5000
unit: Celsius
```

может быть schema-valid,

но физически бессмысленно для конкретного оборудования.

---

# 1619. Semantic Verification

Проверяет:

```text
значение допустимо?
relation имеет правильные domain/range?
units совместимы?
context логичен?
```

---

# 1620. Constraint Verification

Например:

```text
Project requires EU hosting
```

Provider:

```text
US-only
```

→

```text
NO
```

---

# 1621. Three-valued verification

Результат:

```text
YES
NO
UNKNOWN
```

---

# 1622. UNKNOWN не должен превращаться в PASS

Очень важный принцип.

Если:

```text
license unclear
```

то:

```text
verification = UNKNOWN
```

а не:

```text
assume compatible
```

---

# 1623. Verification Result

Application-level объект:

```yaml
verification_result:
  subject: artifact_17
  check: schema_conformance

  state: YES

  evidence:
    - test_run_4

  verifier:
    validator_package_2
```

---

# 1624. Verification as Claim

Формально результат проверки тоже можно представить как:

```text
CLAIM
```

например:

```text
Artifact 17
SATISFIES
Schema X
```

с Evidence.

---

# 1625. Verifier

Verifier может быть:

```text
deterministic software
AI agent
human reviewer
laboratory instrument
external authority
```

---

# 1626. Verification Mode

Useful enum:

```text
AUTOMATED
HUMAN
AI_REVIEW
CROSS_AGENT
EXPERIMENTAL
EXTERNAL
```

---

# 1627. Automated Verification

Подходит для:

```text
unit tests
schema checks
hash validation
constraint checks
```

---

# 1628. Human Verification

Нужно для:

```text
judgment
legal interpretation
creative quality
physical inspection
complex strategic review
```

---

# 1629. AI Review

Полезен как дополнительный слой:

```text
consistency check
evidence check
draft critique
```

Но:

```text
AI review
≠ independent proof
```

---

# 1630. Cross-Agent Verification

Один AI создаёт результат.

Другой:

```text
ищет ошибки
```

Но оба могут:

```text
share same blind spot
```

---

# 1631. Поэтому Cross-Agent Verification — Evidence, а не guarantee

---

# 1632. Experimental Verification

Используется, когда истину можно проверить только действием:

```text
запустить код
измерить датчик
провести испытание
```

---

# 1633. External Verification

Например:

```text
сертификационная лаборатория
финансирующая организация
государственный орган
```

---

# 1634. Verification Contract

Каждый Task/Artifact может иметь:

```text
verification contract
```

---

# 1635. Example

```yaml
verification:
  target:
    parser

  checks:
    - schema_valid
    - accuracy_on_gold_set
    - no_critical_security_findings

  acceptance:
    all_must_pass: true
```

---

# 1636. Verification Contract ≠ Test Implementation

Contract says:

```text
что должно быть доказано
```

Evaluator package says:

```text
как это проверить
```

---

# 1637. Acceptance Criteria

Например:

```text
accuracy >= 0.95
```

или:

```text
no critical security issue
```

---

# 1638. But threshold needs provenance

Почему:

```text
0.95
```

а не:

```text
0.90
```

?

Threshold должен происходить из:

```text
policy
benchmark standard
human decision
domain requirement
```

---

# 1639. Arbitrary threshold problem

System should not invent:

```text
95%
```

без основания.

---

# 1640. Gold Dataset

Для repeatable semantic tasks нужен:

```text
Gold Dataset
```

---

# 1641. Gold Dataset содержит

```text
input
expected output
human label
reason codes
version
```

# 1642. Пример для HN matching

```text
как формировать reusable concepts, patterns и archetypes.
```

Именно этот слой превратит накопление данных в **долговременную семантическую память виртуального технопарка**, из которой новые проекты смогут начинать не с нуля, а с уже проверенных знаний, процедур, решений и ошибок.
contents.title: Verification, Benchmarking & Epistemic Quality Engine v0.1

contents.content: Следующая часть будет посвящена **Knowledge Consolidation, Semantic Memory & World Model Evolution Engine v0.1** — то есть механизму, который превращает поток событий, проектов, экспериментов и решений в долговременную структурированную память, а не просто в всё более огромную базу данных.
Продолжение, на русском, перевод потом

Продолжаю полностью **на русском языке**. Перевод пока не делаю. Теперь следующий слой — **Knowledge Consolidation, Semantic Memory & World Model Evolution Engine v0.1**: механизм, который превращает огромный поток событий, Claims, Evidence, проектов, ошибок и решений в долговременную структурированную память, не перегружая активный World State.

# Knowledge Consolidation, Semantic Memory & World Model Evolution Engine v0.1

## 2043. Главный переход

До этого Innovation OS уже умеет:

```text id="km2043"
наблюдать
↓
создавать Claims
↓
собирать Evidence
↓
выполнять Projects
↓
проверять результаты
↓
обновлять World State
```

Но возникает новая проблема:

```text id="km2044"
если всё сохранять одинаково,
World State со временем превращается
в огромную смесь:
старых событий
локальных наблюдений
устаревших Claims
дубликатов
временных гипотез
исторических версий
```

Нужен слой консолидации памяти.

---

# 2044. Основная задача

Система должна уметь различать:

```text id="km2045"
что происходит сейчас
```

от:

```text id="km2046"
что происходило раньше
```

и от:

```text id="km2047"
что мы из этого уже узнали
```

---

# 2045. Три слоя памяти

Минимальная модель:

```text id="km2048"
EVENT MEMORY
↓
EPISODIC MEMORY
↓
SEMANTIC MEMORY
```

---

# 2046. Event Memory

Это сырые или почти сырые события:

```text id="km2049"
TASK_COMPLETED
PACKAGE_FAILED
RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE
CLAIM_UPDATED
PROJECT_STARTED
```

---

# 2047. Episodic Memory

Группирует события в осмысленные эпизоды.

Например:

```text id="km2050"
"Миграция проекта X
на новый package provider"
```

содержит:

```text id="km2051"
причину
последовательность действий
ошибки
решение
результат
```

---

# 2048. Semantic Memory

Сохраняет уже обобщённое знание:

```text id="km2052"
"Package family A
обычно требует adapter B
в environment C"
```

или:

```text id="km2053"
"Для capability X
наиболее частый bottleneck —
не hardware, а operator availability."
```

---

# 2049. Episodic ≠ Semantic

Эпизод:

```text id="km2054"
в проекте 17
сломался GitHub adapter
```

Semantic knowledge:

```text id="km2055"
GitHub adapter family
имеет recurring failure mode Y
при condition Z
```

Второе требует повторяемости/анализа.

---

# 2050. Не обобщать после одного случая автоматически

Один эпизод:

```text id="km2056"
не создаёт universal rule
```

Лучше:

```text id="km2057"
HYPOTHESIS
```

который проверяется на следующих случаях.

---

# 2051. Memory Hierarchy

Полезно иметь:

```text id="km2058"
L0 Raw Events
L1 Execution Episodes
L2 Project Memory
L3 Program Memory
L4 Organizational Memory
L5 World Knowledge
```

---

# 2052. L0 — Raw Events

Высокая детализация.

Например:

```text id="km2059"
API request
task state transition
resource booking
```

---

# 2053. L1 — Execution Episode

Например:

```text id="km2060"
Repository Evaluation Run #17
```

---

# 2054. L2 — Project Memory

Содержит:

```text id="km2061"
major decisions
validated Claims
important failures
artifacts
lessons learned
```

---

# 2055. L3 — Program Memory

Содержит:

```text id="km2062"
cross-project patterns
shared bottlenecks
common resources
```

---

# 2056. L4 — Organizational Memory

Содержит:

```text id="km2063"
reusable procedures
organizational patterns
capability history
policy outcomes
```

---

# 2057. L5 — World Knowledge

Наиболее обобщённое:

```text id="km2064"
technological concepts
methods
standards
general relationships
```

---

# 2058. Memory Promotion

Информация может подниматься:

```text id="km2065"
Event
↓
Episode
↓
Project Lesson
↓
Reusable Pattern
↓
World Knowledge
```

Но каждая ступень требует основания.

---

# 2059. Promotion ≠ Copy

Система не копирует одни и те же данные пять раз.

Higher layer может хранить:

```text id="km2066"
summary
derived Claim
references to lower layers
```

---

# 2060. Provenance сохраняется

Semantic Memory Claim должен иметь:

```text id="km2067"
DERIVED_FROM
```

набор эпизодов/доказательств.

---

# 2061. Memory Compression

Нужна не просто storage compression, а:

```text id="km2068"
semantic compression
```

То есть убрать повторение, сохранив существенный смысл.

---

# 2062. Example

100 событий:

```text id="km2069"
retry
retry
retry
timeout
retry
success
```

можно свести в Episode:

```text id="km2070"
Provider X experienced repeated transient failures;
succeeded after retries.
```

Но raw Events сохраняются в архиве.

---

# 2063. Active Memory vs Archive

Разделить:

```text id="km2071"
ACTIVE
ARCHIVED
```

Active используется в обычных queries/context.

Archive доступен по необходимости.

---

# 2064. Active World State

Содержит:

```text id="km2072"
current entities
current capabilities
current valid claims
current projects
open gaps
active policies
```

---

# 2065. Historical Store

Содержит:

```text id="km2073"
superseded claims
old projects
retired packages
expired policies
old resource states
```

---

# 2066. Archive does not mean delete

Историческая информация остаётся для:

```text id="km2074"
audit
learning
replay
research
```

---

# 2067. Hot / Warm / Cold Memory

Useful implementation model:

```text id="km2075"
HOT
current operational state

WARM
recent project/program history

COLD
deep archive
```

---

# 2068. Hot Memory

Fast database indexes.

---

# 2069. Warm Memory

Slower but searchable.

---

# 2070. Cold Memory

Object storage / archival database.

---

# 2071. Retrieval should be semantic

Context Builder может запросить:

```text id="km2076"
relevant historical failures
for Capability X
```

не загружая весь архив.

---

# 2072. Forgetting as engineering function

Не всё должно оставаться активным навсегда.

Но «забывание» здесь означает:

```text id="km2077"
deactivate from working memory
```

а не обязательно физически уничтожить.

---

# 2073. Forgetting Policies

Можно учитывать:

```text id="km2078"
age
relevance
supersession
legal retention
reuse frequency
```

---

# 2074. Important exception

Evidence supporting active critical decisions:

```text id="km2079"
не должно быть автоматически forgotten
```

---

# 2075. Dependency-aware retention

If Artifact supports:

```text id="km2080"
active Claim
active Decision
active Policy
```

retention policy must account for dependency.

---

# 2076. Garbage Collection

Semantic Garbage Collector can identify:

```text id="km2081"
orphan artifacts
expired caches
duplicate embeddings
obsolete materialized views
```

---

# 2077. Do not garbage-collect canonical evidence casually

Canonical history has different retention class.

---

# 2078. Materialized View Rebuild

Derived structures:

```text id="km2082"
matches
gaps
capability indices
```

can be deleted/recomputed.

Canonical Claims/Evidence cannot.

---

# 2079. Canonical vs Derived Storage

Freeze:

```text id="km2083"
CANONICAL
DERIVED
CACHE
ARCHIVE
```

---

# 2080. CANONICAL

```text id="km2084"
Claims
Evidence
Events
Decisions
Artifacts
```

---

# 2081. DERIVED

```text id="km2085"
Open Gaps
Matches
Clusters
Scores
```

---

# 2082. CACHE

```text id="km2086"
embeddings
query results
temporary summaries
```

---

# 2083. ARCHIVE

Historical canonical objects no longer active.

---

# 2084. Temporal World Model

World State should answer not only:

```text id="km2087"
что верно сейчас?
```

Но:

```text id="km2088"
что считалось верным на дату T?
```

---

# 2085. Valid Time vs Transaction Time

Useful distinction:

```text id="km2089"
VALID_TIME
когда факт был верен в мире

TRANSACTION_TIME
когда система его узнала
```

---

# 2086. Example

Lab unavailable:

```text id="km2090"
valid_from = 10 Sept
```

но система узнала:

```text id="km2091"
12 Sept
```

Это разные времена.

---

# 2087. Why important

Historical reconstruction:

```text id="km2092"
Decision made 11 Sept
```

не должна использовать knowledge discovered 12 Sept.

---

# 2088. Time-travel query

```text id="km2093"
SHOW WORLD STATE
AS KNOWN AT 2026-09-11
```

---

# 2089. Another query

```text id="km2094"
SHOW ACTUAL VALID STATE
for 2026-09-11
using all later corrections
```

Это две разные задачи.

---

# 2090. Bitemporal model

Long-term system may need:

```text id="km2095"
valid time
+
system knowledge time
```

---

# 2091. Claim Supersession

New Claim may:

```text id="km2096"
SUPERSEDE
```

old Claim.

Old one remains historical.

---

# 2092. Correction

Example:

```text id="km2097"
deadline = Oct 10
```

later corrected:

```text id="km2098"
deadline = Oct 17
```

History preserves both.

---

# 2093. Retraction

If source retracts:

```text id="km2099"
claim not deleted
```

state becomes:

```text id="km2100"
RETRACTED / INVALIDATED
```

---

# 2094. Memory Consolidation Job

Periodically:

```text id="km2101"
collect recent events
cluster episodes
find repeated patterns
identify stale knowledge
produce consolidation proposals
```

---

# 2095. Consolidation should not directly rewrite truth

It creates:

```text id="km2102"
Consolidation Proposal
```

for validation.

---

# 2096. Example

Observed:

```text id="km2103"
8 projects repeatedly
failed on same API limit
```

Proposal:

```text id="km2104"
Create Claim:
API X rate limit
is recurring operational bottleneck.
```

---

# 2097. Pattern Confidence

Depends on:

```text id="km2105"
number of episodes
independence
context similarity
recency
```

---

# 2098. Pattern ≠ universal law

Should preserve:

```text id="km2106"
scope
```

---

# 2099. Scope

Example:

```text id="km2107"
within EU-hosted deployment
```

or:

```text id="km2108"
for Python-based agent services
```

---

# 2100. Overgeneralization Detector

Consolidation Engine should ask:

```text id="km2109"
Are these episodes actually comparable?
```

---

# 2101. Example

Five failures share:

```text id="km2110"
same root cause
```

good candidate for pattern.

Five failures in unrelated contexts:

```text id="km2111"
may not be one pattern
```

---

# 2102. Semantic Deduplication

World State may contain:

```text id="km2112"
browser automation
web automation
browser control
```

Possibly same/related concepts.

Need cautious dedup.

---

# 2103. Dedup Pipeline

```text id="km2113"
candidate similarity
↓
ontology/context comparison
↓
evidence
↓
merge proposal
```

---

# 2104. Embeddings only propose candidates

Never automatic entity merge.

---

# 2105. Merge states

```text id="km2114"
DISTINCT
RELATED
POSSIBLY_SAME
SAME
```

---

# 2106. Merge Decision

For high-impact concepts/entities may require review.

---

# 2107. Entity Merge

If confirmed:

```text id="km2115"
Entity B
MERGED_INTO
Entity A
```

But aliases/old IDs remain resolvable.

---

# 2108. Split

Sometimes one concept was too broad.

Example:

```text id="km2116"
Agent evaluation
```

later splits into:

```text id="km2117"
task accuracy evaluation
security evaluation
tool-use evaluation
```

---

# 2109. Semantic Split

Need migration of dependent Claims carefully.

---

# 2110. Concept Evolution

Concept registry itself evolves over time.

---

# 2111. Concept Versioning

Concept definition may change.

Store:

```text id="km2118"
definition version
aliases
relations
effective dates
```

---

# 2112. Avoid semantic drift without visibility

If meaning changes, old Claims need explicit historical interpretation.

---

# 2113. Ontology Evolution Engine

Functions:

```text id="km2119"
new concept proposal
merge proposal
split proposal
relation update
deprecation
```

---

# 2114. Ontology change is governed

Especially for canonical concepts.

---

# 2115. Archetype Formation

Repeated project structures can become reusable Archetype.

Example:

```text id="km2120"
repo evaluation
```

repeats many times.

Consolidation proposes:

```text id="km2121"
RepositoryEvaluation Archetype
```

---

# 2116. Archetype extraction

Find:

```text id="km2122"
common Tasks
common Inputs
common Outputs
common verification
```

---

# 2117. Archetype ≠ copy of one project

It is generalized pattern.

---

# 2118. Archetype Variants

For different contexts:

```text id="km2123"
FAST
STANDARD
HIGH_ASSURANCE
```

---

# 2119. Procedure Consolidation

Repeated successful Procedures can become:

```text id="km2124"
Workflow Package
```

---

# 2120. Procedure Mining

From execution traces:

```text id="km2125"
actual paths
```

identify common successful subgraphs.

---

# 2121. Common Subprocedure

Example:

```text id="km2126"
fetch metadata
↓
license check
↓
read docs
```

appears in many workflows.

Could become reusable package.

---

# 2122. Failure Pattern Library

Repeated failure modes should become structured knowledge.

---

# 2123. Failure Pattern

Fields:

```text id="km2127"
symptoms
conditions
probable causes
diagnostics
known mitigations
```

---

# 2124. Example

```text id="km2128"
Symptom:
API returns inconsistent pagination

Context:
high-volume repository search

Mitigation:
cursor validation + retry
```

---

# 2125. Troubleshooting Memory

Runtime can query:

```text id="km2129"
Have we seen similar failure before?
```

---

# 2126. Case-Based Reasoning

Current case:

```text id="km2130"
Problem P
```

retrieve:

```text id="km2131"
similar past episodes
```

---

# 2127. Similarity by structure, not just text

Compare:

```text id="km2132"
capabilities
constraints
failure type
resource graph
```

---

# 2128. Case Library

Useful for:

```text id="km2133"
debugging
project estimation
risk analysis
```

---

# 2129. Lesson Learned

Project completion can produce:

```text id="km2134"
Lesson
```

as structured Claim.

---

# 2130. Good lesson format

```text id="km2135"
Context
Observation
Interpretation
Evidence
Applicability
Exceptions
```

---

# 2131. Bad lesson

```text id="km2136"
"Never use technology X"
```

without context.

---

# 2132. Local Lesson

Could be:

```text id="km2137"
For project type Y
under constraint Z
technology X caused issue W.
```

Much stronger epistemically.

---

# 2133. Negative Knowledge

System must deliberately preserve:

```text id="km2138"
what did not work
```

---

# 2134. Why

Otherwise future agents repeatedly try same failed paths.

---

# 2135. Negative Knowledge types

```text id="km2139"
Rejected Technology
Failed Procedure
Invalid Hypothesis
Incompatible Provider
Dead-end Research Path
```

---

# 2136. But negative result also contextual

```text id="km2140"
didn't work in context X
```

not:

```text id="km2141"
never works
```

---

# 2137. Dead-End Cache

For low-level search:

```text id="km2142"
already checked candidate
failed because hard blocker
```

can prevent repeated work.

---

# 2138. Cache expiry

If blocker can change:

```text id="km2143"
license changed
new version released
availability changed
```

dead-end cache expires/rechecks.

---

# 2139. Stable Negative Knowledge

Some failures remain long-lived.

Example:

```text id="km2144"
hardware physically incompatible
```

unless hardware version changes.

---

# 2140. Memory Retrieval

Need several modes:

```text id="km2145"
EXACT
SEMANTIC
GRAPH
TEMPORAL
CASE-BASED
```

---

# 2141. Exact retrieval

Known ID/term.

---

# 2142. Semantic retrieval

Find similar meaning.

---

# 2143. Graph retrieval

Follow dependencies/relations.

---

# 2144. Temporal retrieval

Find:

```text id="km2146"
what happened before/after event X
```

---

# 2145. Case-based retrieval

Find similar historical episodes.

---

# 2146. Contextual Retrieval

Agent should not receive all relevant-ish memories.

Need rank by:

```text id="km2147"
task relevance
authority
freshness
evidence
scope match
```

---

# 2147. Memory Retrieval Contract

Input:

```text id="km2148"
task
context
required knowledge types
token/size budget
```

Output:

```text id="km2149"
minimal useful memory package
```

---

# 2148. Context Builder integration

Before AI Action:

```text id="km2150"
current task
+
active state
+
retrieved memory
```

---

# 2149. Avoid Memory Flooding

Too much historical context can:

```text id="km2151"
reduce reasoning quality
increase cost
surface stale assumptions
```

---

# 2150. Retrieval Diversity

For contested questions, retrieve:

```text id="km2152"
supporting
refuting
alternative
```

memory.

---

# 2151. Not only nearest-neighbor search

Otherwise semantic retrieval may create echo chamber.

---

# 2152. Memory Freshness

Every memory item should know:

```text id="km2153"
last validated
last used
current applicability
```

---

# 2153. Memory Reactivation

Archived knowledge becomes active if:

```text id="km2154"
new project makes it relevant
```

---

# 2154. Example

Old optical sensing experiment from 2024 may become relevant to 2027 robotics project.

---

# 2155. Revalidation on Reactivation

Before relying on old knowledge:

```text id="km2155"
check stale dependencies
versions
context
```

---

# 2156. Knowledge Half-Life

Different classes decay differently:

```text id="km2156"
API behavior: fast
software compatibility: medium
physics principle: slow
```

---

# 2157. Half-life is heuristic

Not delete schedule.

---

# 2158. Memory Usage Statistics

Track:

```text id="km2157"
which memories are retrieved
which affect decisions
which become stale
```

---

# 2159. Popular ≠ True

Frequent retrieval does not increase factual validity automatically.

---

# 2160. Memory Influence Graph

Can trace:

```text id="km2158"
Memory Claim
↓
Decision
↓
Action
↓
Outcome
```

---

# 2161. This permits evaluating memory quality

If one old heuristic repeatedly causes failures:

```text id="km2159"
review/deprecate it
```

---

# 2162. Knowledge Utility

Dimensions:

```text id="km2160"
reuse
decision relevance
accuracy
freshness
cost saved
```

No universal score required.

---

# 2163. Semantic Summary

Long project can produce:

```text id="km2161"
Project Summary Artifact
```

but summaries need provenance links.

---

# 2164. Hierarchical Summary

```text id="km2162"
Task Summary
↓
Project Summary
↓
Program Summary
↓
Portfolio Summary
```

---

# 2165. Summary Loss Risk

Each summarization can lose details.

Need:

```text id="km2163"
references to source objects
```

---

# 2166. Summary is not canonical truth

It is:

```text id="km2164"
derived Artifact
```

---

# 2167. Semantic Compression with drill-down

UI shows summary.

User/agent can expand:

```text id="km2165"
Claim
→ Evidence
→ Raw Artifact
```

---

# 2168. Knowledge Graph vs Document Store

Need both.

Knowledge Graph:

```text id="km2166"
structured relations
```

Document Store:

```text id="km2167"
full reports
PDFs
code
datasets
```

---

# 2169. Graph should reference artifacts

Not attempt to convert every byte into triples.

---

# 2170. Granularity principle

Structure only what is useful for:

```text id="km2168"
reasoning
matching
verification
execution
```

---

# 2171. Over-structuring is costly

Not every paragraph needs to become 50 Claims.

---

# 2172. Extraction Budget

System may choose:

```text id="km2169"
light extraction
deep extraction
```

based on importance.

---

# 2173. High-value Artifact

Critical standard/policy/paper:

```text id="km2170"
deep semantic extraction
```

---

# 2174. Low-value Artifact

Minor log:

```text id="km2171"
archive + metadata
```

---

# 2175. Adaptive Structuring

If low-value artifact later becomes important:

```text id="km2172"
deep parse on demand
```

---

# 2176. Memory Consolidation Policies

Could run:

```text id="km2173"
after project completion
weekly for events
monthly for world knowledge
```

---

# 2177. Triggered Consolidation

Events:

```text id="km2174"
PROJECT_COMPLETED
PROGRAM_COMPLETED
FAILURE_CLUSTER_DETECTED
ONTOLOGY_CONFLICT
```

---

# 2178. Project Closeout

Should generate:

```text id="km2175"
final artifacts
validated lessons
remaining unknowns
unresolved debt
reusable assets
```

---

# 2179. Closeout Memory Package

Example:

```yaml id="km2176"
project_memory:
  outcomes: [...]
  validated_claims: [...]
  failed_hypotheses: [...]
  reusable_assets: [...]
  lessons: [...]
  unresolved_gaps: [...]
```

---

# 2180. Unresolved Gap survives project

If Project ends without resolving Gap:

```text id="km2177"
Gap returns to World State
```

not lost.

---

# 2181. Unused Artifact

Could remain archived but searchable.

---

# 2182. Reusable Asset Promotion

Artifact reused across several projects can become:

```text id="km2178"
Shared Asset
```

in registry.

---

# 2183. Reusable Procedure Promotion

Procedure used repeatedly:

```text id="km2179"
Workflow Package candidate
```

---

# 2184. Reusable Team Pattern

Repeated successful Team configuration:

```text id="km2180"
Team Archetype candidate
```

---

# 2185. Reusable Organization Pattern

Repeated successful unit structure:

```text id="km2181"
Organizational Blueprint candidate
```

---

# 2186. Reusable Policy Pattern

Stable repeated approvals:

```text id="km2182"
Policy proposal candidate
```

---

# 2187. Thus consolidation feeds Package Registry

```text id="km2183"
Experience
↓
Pattern
↓
Package
↓
Reusable Capability
```

---

# 2188. Experience-to-Package Pipeline

This is powerful.

System can learn not only model weights,

but:

```text id="km2184"
procedures
archetypes
policies
templates
```

---

# 2189. Structured Learning over model fine-tuning

For many operational lessons it is safer to update:

```text id="km2185"
explicit knowledge
workflow
rule
```

rather than silently fine-tune model.

---

# 2190. Why

Explicit knowledge is:

```text id="km2186"
auditable
reversible
versioned
```

---

# 2191. Model Fine-tuning remains optional

And should happen through separate governed pipeline.

---

# 2192. Memory Branching

Counterfactual/scenario worlds need separate memory.

Do not let:

```text id="km2187"
simulated event
```

enter base-world history as real event.

---

# 2193. Scenario Memory

Tagged:

```text id="km2188"
context = SCENARIO
```

---

# 2194. Merge Scenario Knowledge

If simulation reveals useful insight:

```text id="km2189"
can create HYPOTHESIS in base world
```

not FACT.

---

# 2195. Example

Simulation shows:

```text id="km2190"
possible bottleneck migration
```

Base World gets:

```text id="km2191"
Hypothesis:
If capacity A doubles,
B may become bottleneck.
```

---

# 2196. Memory Isolation

Private project memory should not automatically become organization-wide memory.

---

# 2197. Promotion Scope

Possible:

```text id="km2192"
TASK
PROJECT
PROGRAM
ORGANIZATION
FEDERATION
PUBLIC
```

---

# 2198. Knowledge Publication

Before moving:

```text id="km2193"
PRIVATE PROJECT
→
PUBLIC KNOWLEDGE
```

run:

```text id="km2194"
redaction
review
license
approval
```

---

# 2199. Confidential Knowledge

Can still be semantically indexed locally.

---

# 2200. Federated Memory

Each node owns memory.

Federation shares only permitted semantic objects.

---

# 2201. Remote Memory Reference

Local node may store:

```text id="km2195"
shadow claim
remote artifact reference
```

without importing full source.

---

# 2202. Remote Memory Freshness

Need:

```text id="km2196"
last_synced
source_version
```

---

# 2203. Memory Revocation

If remote knowledge revoked:

```text id="km2197"
mark unavailable/revoked
```

and inspect dependent local decisions.

---

# 2204. Memory Dependency Review

If critical remote Evidence disappears:

```text id="km2198"
dependent Claim may become UNKNOWN
```

---

# 2205. Distributed Knowledge Consolidation

Different nodes can independently derive different patterns.

Do not force global merge.

---

# 2206. Example

Node A:

```text id="km2199"
Method X works well in automotive robotics.
```

Node B:

```text id="km2200"
Method X performs poorly in healthcare robotics.
```

Both can be true in different contexts.

---

# 2207. Context-aware federation is essential

---

# 2208. Memory Conflict

If two semantic memories genuinely conflict:

```text id="km2201"
store both
```

and trigger evidence review.

---

# 2209. Consensus is derived, not forced

---

# 2210. Memory Quality

Memory item should expose:

```text id="km2202"
provenance
verification
freshness
scope
conflicts
```

---

# 2211. Memory Trust

No generic:

```text id="km2203"
trusted memory = true
```

Better:

```text id="km2204"
verified for context X
```

---

# 2212. Memory Poisoning Risk

Bad data can propagate through consolidation.

Need:

```text id="km2205"
source validation
anomaly detection
review of high-impact consolidation
```

---

# 2213. Consolidation Attack

Malicious source could flood system with repeated false claims,

creating artificial pattern.

---

# 2214. Frequency ≠ truth

Pattern detector must account for:

```text id="km2206"
source independence
```

---

# 2215. Sybil-resistant consolidation

Ten copied Claims from one origin:

```text id="km2207"
should not count as ten independent observations
```

---

# 2216. Provenance clustering

Detect common root source.

---

# 2217. Memory Safety

Raw untrusted text remains Artifact.

Structured Claims extracted from it remain:

```text id="km2208"
candidate claims
```

until validated.

---

# 2218. Prompt Injection Memory

Do not store arbitrary embedded instructions as persistent operational rules.

---

# 2219. Instruction-type content

Must be categorized as:

```text id="km2209"
Artifact content
```

unless explicitly imported into Policy/Procedure through governed process.

---

# 2220. Memory of Decisions

Decision Memory especially important.

Store:

```text id="km2210"
options considered
selected option
evidence
assumptions
outcome
```

---

# 2221. Decision Outcome

Later:

```text id="km2211"
did expected result occur?
```

---

# 2222. Decision Pattern Mining

Could discover:

```text id="km2212"
under context X,
strategy A repeatedly underperforms
```

as hypothesis.

---

# 2223. Avoid hindsight bias

Evaluation must reconstruct:

```text id="km2213"
what was known at decision time
```

---

# 2224. Good Decision vs Good Outcome

A good decision under uncertainty may produce bad outcome.

Do not conflate.

---

# 2225. Decision Quality dimensions

```text id="km2214"
evidence adequacy
constraint compliance
reasoning completeness
```

separate from outcome.

---

# 2226. Outcome Quality

Separate:

```text id="km2215"
actual result
```

---

# 2227. This enables better organizational learning

---

# 2228. Memory of Failed Projects

Failed Project should produce rich memory.

Not disappear as:

```text id="km2216"
CANCELLED
```

only.

---

# 2229. Failure Closeout

Capture:

```text id="km2217"
what assumptions failed
what evidence emerged
which resources were inadequate
what was still useful
```

---

# 2230. Partial Asset Salvage

Failed Project may still produce:

```text id="km2218"
dataset
tool
knowledge
procedure
```

reusable elsewhere.

---

# 2231. Project Genealogy

New Project may be:

```text id="km2219"
DERIVED_FROM
```

failed previous Project.

---

# 2232. Program Genealogy

Programs can evolve:

```text id="km2220"
Program A
split into
B + C
```

Memory preserves lineage.

---

# 2233. Organization Genealogy

Teams/units likewise.

---

# 2234. Technology Genealogy

Package/repo/method versions:

```text id="km2221"
DERIVED_FROM
```

---

# 2235. Knowledge Genealogy

Claim refinements:

```text id="km2222"
Claim v1
qualified by
Claim v2
```

---

# 2236. Genealogy enables evolutionary analysis

Can ask:

```text id="km2223"
How did this capability emerge?
```

---

# 2237. Capability History

For each Capability:

```text id="km2224"
first observed demand
first provider
maturity growth
capacity changes
major failures
```

---

# 2238. Capability Timeline

Very useful for frontier analysis.

---

# 2239. Technology Diffusion

Track:

```text id="km2225"
research
→ repos
→ hiring
→ projects
→ operational adoption
```

---

# 2240. World Model Evolution

The system should not just store data.

It should track:

```text id="km2226"
how its own model changed
```

---

# 2241. Model Revision

Examples:

```text id="km2227"
new concept added
relation reclassified
claim confidence reduced
provider removed
```

---

# 2242. World Model Changelog

Every major semantic change recorded.

---

# 2243. Semantic Release Notes

For organization:

```text id="km2228"
This month:
12 new capabilities
3 retired technologies
2 major bottleneck changes
```

---

# 2244. World Diff

Compare:

```text id="km2229"
World State t1
vs
World State t2
```

---

# 2245. Diff categories

```text id="km2230"
new resource
lost resource
new gap
resolved gap
new claim
invalidated claim
new opportunity
```

---

# 2246. Monthly World Snapshot

Could support strategic review.

---

# 2247. Change Significance

Not every changed field deserves attention.

Need classify:

```text id="km2231"
cosmetic
operational
strategic
```

---

# 2248. Strategic Change

Example:

```text id="km2232"
critical provider unavailable
```

---

# 2249. Operational Change

Example:

```text id="km2233"
task status changed
```

---

# 2250. Semantic Noise Reduction

Consolidation should prevent leadership/UI from seeing millions of trivial events.

---

# 2251. Change Aggregation

100 task completions can become:

```text id="km2234"
Milestone achieved
```

---

# 2252. Event-to-State Reduction

Not every Event stays visible once state materialized.

History remains accessible.

---

# 2253. Active Claim Selection

If multiple temporal Claims:

```text id="km2235"
choose currently applicable
```

but preserve others.

---

# 2254. Claim Resolver

Determines active Claim based on:

```text id="km2236"
valid time
context
authority
supersession
verification
```

---

# 2255. No naïve "latest wins"

Newest Claim might be:

```text id="km2237"
less authoritative
wrong context
```

---

# 2256. Active World State is a projection

Canonical history richer than operational view.

---

# 2257. Semantic Projection

For each context:

```text id="km2238"
Project X
Organization Y
Scenario Z
```

system builds appropriate World View.

---

# 2258. Personalized/role-specific views

Different users may see:

```text id="km2239"
different accessible subset
```

while underlying objects remain same.

---

# 2259. Memory Access Governance

Historical memory can contain sensitive material.

Policies apply equally to archive.

---

# 2260. Archive is not permission bypass

---

# 2261. Retention Governance

Some artifacts require:

```text id="km2240"
minimum retention
maximum retention
legal hold
```

---

# 2262. Retention metadata

```text id="km2241"
retain_until
delete_after
legal_hold
```

when applicable.

---

# 2263. Destruction Event

If data must be physically deleted:

```text id="km2242"
DATA_DELETED
```

can remain as audit metadata without retaining content.

---

# 2264. Tombstone

Instead of broken references:

```text id="km2243"
object tombstone
```

says:

```text id="km2244"
object existed
now unavailable/deleted
```

---

# 2265. Knowledge Resilience

Critical knowledge should not depend on one Artifact only.

---

# 2266. Redundant Knowledge Representation

For critical procedures:

```text id="km2245"
structured workflow
documentation
tests
```

all support continuity.

---

# 2267. Knowledge Backup

Not only file backup.

Need preserve:

```text id="km2246"
semantic identities
relations
provenance
versions
```

---

# 2268. Disaster Recovery

Rebuild:

```text id="km2247"
World State
```

from:

```text id="km2248"
canonical objects
event log
artifacts
```

---

# 2269. Materialized views can be recreated

---

# 2270. Memory Integrity

Use:

```text id="km2249"
hashes
checksums
version manifests
```

---

# 2271. Snapshot Integrity

World snapshot should have:

```text id="km2250"
snapshot hash
```

---

# 2272. Export

System should support:

```text id="km2251"
portable semantic export
```

not vendor lock-in.

# 2273. Export Package

Could contain:

```text id="km2252"
IIR objects
schemas
artifacts refs
provenance
```

---

# 2274. Import

Imported memory remains:

```text id="km2253"
external provenance
```

until validated.

# 2275. Memory Package

Could become package type:

```text id="km2254"
KNOWLEDGE_PACKAGE
```

# 2276. Example

```text id="km2255"
Robot Tactile Sensing Knowledge Package
```

containing:

```text id="km2256"
concepts
validated claims
papers
benchmark definitions
failure patterns
```

---

# 2277. Knowledge Package ≠ raw dump

It is curated/structured subset.

---

# 2278. Technopedia integration

Each Concept page could draw from Semantic Memory:

```text id="km2257"
definition
evidence
methods
resources
history
related projects
```

---

# 2279. Living Encyclopedia

Unlike static wiki:

```text id="km2258"
pages regenerate from current World Model
```

while human-authored narrative remains possible.

# 2280. Page ≠ source of truth

Canonical graph remains source.

Page is representation.

# 2281. Historical Page

Could view:

```text id="km2259"
Technopedia as of date T
```

---

# 2282. Knowledge Branching

Community may create:

```text id="km2260"
alternative interpretation branch
```

# 2283. Branch Merge

Requires:

```text id="km2261"
semantic diff
conflict resolution
governance
```

Useful model:

```text id="km2262"
Claims = structured changes
```

# 2285. But not every Claim needs Git-like manual commit

# 2286. Stable Knowledge Releases

Could periodically publish:

```text id="km2263"
World Knowledge Release 2026.09
```

---

# 2287. Release contains

```text id="km2264"
ontology versions
validated knowledge snapshots
package compatibility
```

---

# 2288. Useful for reproducibility

A Project can state:

```text id="km2265"
compiled against Knowledge Release X
```

# 2289. Memory & Package Lock

`system.lock` may include:

```text id="km2266"
knowledge_release
```
