---

# 2290. Knowledge Drift

If current World Model substantially changed from project lock:

```text id="km2267"
review required
```

for long-running projects.

---

# 2291. Example

Project designed using:

```text id="km2268"
Technology X recommended
```

Later X deprecated.

Runtime should flag.

---

# 2292. World Model Compatibility

Project may specify:

```text id="km2269"
minimum semantic assumptions
```

---

# 2293. Assumption Invalidation

Already connected to Decision Review.

Memory Engine supplies historical dependency.

---

# 2294. Memory as Anti-Repetition Layer

One main benefit:

```text id="km2270"
не решать одну и ту же проблему с нуля
```

# 2295. Before new Project

System searches:

```text id="km2271"
similar projects
similar failures
reusable artifacts
existing procedures
```

---

# 2296. Project Bootstrap Package

Input:

```text id="km2272"
new goal
```

Output:

```text id="km2273"
relevant previous knowledge
assets
risks
templates
```

# 2297. Memory-assisted Project Compiler

Compiler can reuse:

```text id="km2274"
validated archetypes
```

instead of hallucinating plan from scratch.

---

# 2298. Memory-assisted Resolver

Resolver remembers:

```text id="km2275"
providers previously failed hard constraint
```

---

# 2299. Memory-assisted Simulation

Historical data calibrates:

```text id="km2276"
cost
lead time
failure rates
```

# 2300. Memory-assisted Governance

Past policy outcomes inform:

```text id="km2277"
policy review
```

but do not automatically determine authority.

# 2301. Memory-assisted Verification

Past failures become regression cases.

---

# 2302. Memory-assisted Opportunity Engine

Repeated unresolved patterns become:

```text id="km2278"
opportunity hypotheses
```

# 2303. Memory-assisted Frontier Engine

Historical trend provides context for new signals.

---

# 2304. Memory-assisted Organization Engine

Repeated collaboration histories reveal stable units.

---

# 2305. Memory-assisted Capability Market

Can estimate:

```text id="km2279"
historical TTC
provider reliability
```

contextually.

---

# 2306. Artificial Technological Awareness connection

Now self-model has temporal dimension.

System knows not only:

```text id="km2280"
what I can do now
```

but:

```text id="km2281"
what I could do before
what I lost
what I learned
how capabilities evolved
```

# 2307. Self-History

Example:

```text id="km2282"
Capability A:
introduced v1
degraded after dependency update
recovered via package B
```

---

# 2308. Self-Learning

System can identify:

```text id="km2283"
which upgrades actually improved capability
```

---

# 2309. Self-Regression Memory

If new package repeats known bad pattern:

```text id="km2284"
warning
```

---

# 2310. Self-Experience

This is closer to:

```text id="km2285"
operational experience
```

than simple chat memory.

---

# 2311. Memory Quality Engine

Need periodically verify memory itself.

---

# 2312. Checks

```text id="km2286"
stale
unsupported
contradictory
orphaned
overgeneralized
duplicate
```

---

# 2313. Memory Review Queue

Prioritize high-impact items.

---

# 2314. Memory Correction

Correction creates:

```text id="km2287"
new revision
```

not silent overwrite.

---

# 2315. Memory Deprecation

Old heuristic can become:

```text id="km2288"
DEPRECATED
```

---

# 2316. Memory Replacement

New validated pattern:

```text id="km2289"
SUPERSEDES
```

old.

---

# 2317. Memory Confidence Decay

Could reduce trust in stale operational knowledge,

but not blindly mathematically decay every fact.

---

# 2318. Context Revalidation better than arbitrary decay

---

# 2319. World Model Compression

As system scales:

```text id="km2290"
millions of Claims
```

# 2320. L0 Detailed

Individual entities/events.

---

# 2321. L1 Cluster

Team/project/capability cluster.

---

# 2322. L2 Domain

Robotics, AI, funding etc.

---

# 2323. L3 Strategic

Major capability systems/programs.

```text id="km2291"
AI Infrastructure
↓
Agent Runtime
↓
Sandboxing
↓
specific packages
```

# 2325. Same concept useful for 2D/3D UI

High level:

```text id="km2292"
district
```

Zoom:

```text id="km2293"
building
```

Further:

```text id="km2294"
workflow
```

---

# 2326. But zoom hierarchy derived from graph

Not hand-built decorative map.

---

# 2327. Knowledge City metaphor

Concept clusters become:

```text id="km2295"
districts
```

Projects:

```text id="km2296"
active construction
```

Archived knowledge:

```text id="km2297"
library/archive
```

---

# 2328. Verification status could influence visual state

But canonical truth remains graph metadata.

---

# 2329. Memory Search UI

Minimum modes:

```text id="km2298"
Search Concepts
Search Projects
Search Decisions
Search Failures
Search Procedures
```

---

# 2330. "Have we done this before?"

Should be first-class query.

---

# 2331. "Why did we choose this?"

Decision Memory query.

---

# 2332. "What failed last time?"

Failure Memory query.

---

# 2333. "What changed since then?"

World Diff query.

---

# 2334. "What do we currently believe?"

Active Claim query.

---

# 2335. "What is uncertain?"

Critical Unknown query.

---

# 2336. "What knowledge is stale?"

Memory Quality query.

---

# 2337. Memory API

Minimum:

```text id="km2299"
POST /memory/consolidate
GET /memory/search
GET /memory/episodes
GET /memory/patterns
GET /memory/history/{entity}
GET /world/as-of
```

---

# 2338. Consolidation API

```text id="km2300"
POST /memory/consolidate/project/{id}
POST /memory/consolidate/time-window
```

---

# 2339. Pattern API

```text id="km2301"
GET /patterns
POST /patterns/{id}/validate
POST /patterns/{id}/promote
```

---

# 2340. Archive API

```text id="km2302"
POST /objects/{id}/archive
POST /objects/{id}/reactivate
```

---

# 2341. Semantic History API

```text id="km2303"
GET /entities/{id}/timeline
GET /claims/{id}/revisions
```

---

# 2342. Knowledge Package API

```text id="km2304"
POST /knowledge-packages
GET /knowledge-packages/{id}
```

---

# 2343. Minimal MVP

Не начинать с automatic universal memory intelligence.

Сначала:

```text id="km2305"
Project Closeout Memory
Semantic Search
Historical Timeline
Claim Supersession
Archive
```

---

# 2344. MVP 1 — Project Memory

After project ends:

```text id="km2306"
validated outcomes
failed hypotheses
reusable artifacts
remaining gaps
```

---

# 2345. MVP 2 — Similar Project Retrieval

Given new Project:

```text id="km2307"
retrieve 5 structurally similar old projects
```

---

# 2346. MVP 3 — Failure Memory

Given failure:

```text id="km2308"
find similar historical failures
```

---

# 2347. MVP 4 — Claim Timeline

Show:

```text id="km2309"
how Claim changed over time
```

---

# 2348. MVP 5 — World Snapshot

Reconstruct:

```text id="km2310"
World State at date T
```

---

# 2349. MVP 6 — Archetype Proposal

Detect repeated procedure and propose reusable workflow.

---

# 2350. MVP 7 — Stale Knowledge Detection

Flag:

```text id="km2311"
active decision depending on stale evidence
```

---

# 2351. Acceptance Criterion

Memory Engine is useful when a new Project can begin with:

```text id="km2312"
existing knowledge
existing procedure
known risks
known providers
historical estimates
```

instead of:

```text id="km2313"
blank context
```

---

# 2352. Architecture integration

```text id="km2314"
EVENTS
↓
EPISODES
↓
PROJECT MEMORY
↓
PATTERNS
↓
SEMANTIC MEMORY
↓
WORLD MODEL
```

---

# 2353. Reverse path

```text id="km2315"
WORLD MODEL
↓
Context Retrieval
↓
Project / Agent
↓
Action
↓
New Events
```

---

# 2354. This creates real organizational memory loop

```text id="km2316"
Experience
↓
Consolidation
↓
Knowledge
↓
Reuse
↓
New Experience
```

---

# 2355. Memory Engine therefore becomes the long-term learning substrate

Not by secretly retraining everything,

but by making experience:

```text id="km2317"
explicit
structured
versioned
verifiable
reusable
```

---

# 2356. Следующий фундаментальный слой

После этого появляется следующий вопрос:

> Если Innovation OS накопила огромную память, множество capabilities, procedures, packages и federated nodes, как ей эффективно находить **новые причинные связи и объяснять, почему одно изменение приводит к другому**, а не только обнаруживать корреляции?

Следующий модуль:

# **Causal Reasoning, Dependency Discovery & Intervention Engine v0.1**

Он должен различать:

```text id="km2318"
корреляцию
причинную гипотезу
структурную зависимость
наблюдаемое последствие
```

и работать с:

```text id="km2319"
causal graphs
interventions
counterfactuals
root-cause analysis
causal experiments
```

Чтобы система могла отвечать не только:

> «Какие события часто происходят вместе?»

но и:

> «Что, вероятно, является причиной bottleneck?»  
> «Какое минимальное изменение может его устранить?»  
> «Что нужно измерить, чтобы отличить две конкурирующие причинные гипотезы?»  
> «Если изменить Resource X, какие downstream effects действительно следуют из зависимости, а какие только коррелируют?»

Это будет следующий шаг от **семантической памяти** к **объясняющей модели мира**.
contents.title: Knowledge Consolidation, Semantic Memory & World Model Evolution Engine v0.1

contents.content: Следующая часть — **Causal Reasoning, Dependency Discovery & Intervention Engine v0.1**: слой причинности, root-cause анализа, интервенций и различения «вместе произошло» от «одно действительно вызвало другое».
Продолжение

Продолжаю полностью **на русском языке**. Теперь следующий модуль — **Causal Reasoning, Dependency Discovery & Intervention Engine v0.1**: слой, который должен отличать простую корреляцию от причинной связи, находить корневые причины, строить интервенции и связывать причинное мышление с симуляцией, экспериментами и управлением проектами.

# Causal Reasoning, Dependency Discovery & Intervention Engine v0.1

## 2357. Главный переход

До этого Innovation OS уже умеет:

```text
наблюдать события
↓
хранить Claims
↓
строить зависимости
↓
сохранять историю
↓
обнаруживать повторяющиеся patterns
```

Но остаётся принципиальная проблема:

```text
A часто происходит перед B
```

ещё не означает:

```text
A вызывает B
```

---

# 2358. Корреляция ≠ причинность

Например система замечает:

```text
Projects using Tool X
have more failures
```

Возможные объяснения:

```text
Tool X вызывает failures
```

или:

```text
Tool X используют
именно в более сложных проектах
```

или:

```text
Tool X появился недавно,
поэтому team ещё не обучена
```

или:

```text
оба эффекта вызваны
третьей причиной Z
```

---

# 2359. Поэтому нужен отдельный causal layer

```text
Observations
↓
Correlation
↓
Causal Hypotheses
↓
Competing Explanations
↓
Evidence / Experiments
↓
Intervention
↓
Outcome
↓
Model Update
```

---

# 2360. Три типа связи

Нужно строго различать:

```text
SEMANTIC RELATION
STRUCTURAL DEPENDENCY
CAUSAL RELATION
```

---

# 2361. Semantic Relation

Например:

```text
Robot
USES
Camera
```

Это не утверждение причинности.

---

# 2362. Structural Dependency

```text
Task B
DEPENDS_ON
Task A
```

означает:

```text
B cannot proceed
until A is satisfied
```

Это operational dependency.

---

# 2363. Causal Relation

```text
Increasing temperature
CAUSES
higher failure probability
```

Это уже causal hypothesis/claim.

---

# 2364. Причинная связь не должна быть новым core predicate автоматически

В Architecture Freeze лучше использовать:

```text
CLAIM
```

с extension predicate:

```text
causal:CAUSES
```

или:

```text
causal:INFLUENCES
causal:MEDIATES
causal:CONFOUNDS
```

---

# 2365. Почему extension namespace

Потому что причинность:

```text
domain-specific
evidence-sensitive
context-sensitive
```

и не должна перегружать минимальный IIR Core.

---

# 2366. Минимальный causal vocabulary

Для v0.1:

```text
causal:CAUSES
causal:INCREASES
causal:DECREASES
causal:MEDIATES
causal:CONFOUNDS
causal:MODERATES
causal:PREVENTS
```

---

# 2367. Но не каждую связь нужно автоматически типизировать глубоко

Для MVP достаточно:

```text
CAUSES
INFLUENCES
CONFOUNDS
```

---

# 2368. Causal Claim

Пример:

```yaml
claim:
  subject: lack_of_operator_capacity
  predicate: causal:CAUSES
  object: lab_queue_delay

  claim_type: HYPOTHESIS

  context:
    lab: lab_A
```

---

# 2369. Причинный Claim всегда требует контекста

Плохая формулировка:

```text
Automation increases productivity.
```

Лучше:

```text
In workflow type X,
automation of step Y
reduced median handling time
under context Z.
```

---

# 2370. Causal Scope

Нужно хранить:

```text
population
context
time
environment
conditions
```

---

# 2371. Причинная модель не должна автоматически переноситься между domains

То, что работает:

```text
в software delivery
```

может не работать:

```text
в лабораторном процессе
```

---

# 2372. Causal Graph

Основная структура:

```text
Nodes = Variables / States / Events
Edges = Causal Hypotheses
```

Например:

```text
Low Staff Capacity
      ↓
Long Review Queue
      ↓
Project Delay
      ↓
Missed Deadline
```

---

# 2373. Не путать с обычным Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph отвечает:

```text
что с чем связано?
```

Causal Graph:

```text
что может измениться,
если вмешаться в X?
```

---

# 2374. Interventional Semantics

Ключевой вопрос:

```text
What happens if we change X?
```

---

# 2375. Наблюдение

```text
Projects with more reviews
take longer.
```

---

# 2376. Интервенция

```text
If we deliberately
reduce required reviews,
does delivery become faster?
```

Это уже causal question.

---

# 2377. do()-подобная семантика

Концептуально:

```text
observe(X=x)
```

не равно:

```text
do(X=x)
```

Первое наблюдает.

Второе вмешивается.

---

# 2378. Intervention Object

Application-level:

```yaml
intervention:
  target: review_policy
  change:
    required_reviews:
      from: 3
      to: 1

  context:
    project_class: low_risk
```

---

# 2379. Intervention ≠ Action

Action:

```text
change policy
```

Intervention:

```text
causal change whose downstream
effects we want to evaluate
```

---

# 2380. Intervention lifecycle

```text
PROPOSED
SIMULATED
APPROVED
EXECUTED
OBSERVED
EVALUATED
```

---

# 2381. Root Cause Analysis

Одна из первых practical functions.

Observed problem:

```text
Project delayed.
```

Нужно определить:

```text
why?
```

---

# 2382. Не останавливаться на ближайшей причине

Например:

```text
Project Delay
↓ caused by
Security Review Delay
```

Но дальше:

```text
Security Review Delay
↓ caused by
Queue
```

Дальше:

```text
Queue
↓ caused by
Incomplete submissions
```

Дальше:

```text
Incomplete submissions
↓ caused by
No standardized intake template
```

---

# 2383. Root Cause может быть структурной

То есть problem:

```text
not enough reviewers
```

может быть только symptom.

---

# 2384. Causal Chain

```text
Missing Intake Standard
↓
Incomplete Inputs
↓
Rework
↓
Review Queue
↓
Project Delay
```

---

# 2385. Intervention options тогда меняются

Если ошибочно считать root cause:

```text
reviewer shortage
```

можно нанять людей.

Но реальный high-leverage intervention:

```text
standardize intake
```

---

# 2386. Root Cause ≠ one deepest node

В сложной системе может быть:

```text
multiple contributing causes
```

---

# 2387. Causal Contribution

Например:

```text
Delay =
capacity shortage
+
input quality
+
tool latency
```

Но не надо сразу задавать процентные вклады без evidence.

---

# 2388. Contributing Cause

Можно хранить:

```text
CAUSE_A
CAUSE_B
CAUSE_C
```

без количественной атрибуции.

---

# 2389. Necessary Cause

Если без X событие не может произойти:

```text
necessary
```

---

# 2390. Sufficient Cause

Если X достаточно для outcome в заданном context:

```text
sufficient
```

---

# 2391. But these labels should be used carefully

В реальных socio-technical systems часто:

```text
probabilistic causality
```

а не строгая necessity/sufficiency.

---

# 2392. Probabilistic Causal Claim

Например:

```text
Reducing queue size
tends to reduce delay
```

within context.

---

# 2393. Causal Evidence Types

Useful:

```text
CONTROLLED_EXPERIMENT
NATURAL_EXPERIMENT
TIME_SERIES
MECHANISTIC_EVIDENCE
OBSERVATIONAL_ASSOCIATION
EXPERT_CAUSAL_MODEL
SIMULATION_RESULT
```

---

# 2394. Они не являются одним линейным hierarchy

Например:

```text
mechanistic evidence
```

может быть сильнее observational association,

но applicability зависит от domain.

---

# 2395. Controlled Experiment

Лучший вариант там, где допустимо:

```text
intervene on X
hold relevant conditions
observe Y
```

---

# 2396. Но во многих organizational systems controlled experiment невозможен

Тогда использовать:

```text
natural experiment
difference over time
matched comparisons
process evidence
```

---

# 2397. Natural Experiment

Например:

```text
Team A adopted new workflow
Team B did not
```

при похожих условиях.

---

# 2398. Но observational confounding остаётся

Team A могла быть:

```text
more experienced
better staffed
```

---

# 2399. Confounder

Variable:

```text
affects X
and
affects Y
```

creating misleading correlation.

---

# 2400. Example

```text
Project Complexity
↓
uses Tool X
↓
failure rate
```

и одновременно:

```text
Project Complexity
→ failure rate
```

Тогда Complexity — confounder.

---

# 2401. Causal Graph должен позволять явно хранить confounders

---

# 2402. Mediator

Variable through which effect passes.

```text
Training
↓
Skill
↓
Productivity
```

Skill may mediate effect of Training.

---

# 2403. Moderator

Changes strength/direction of effect.

Example:

```text
Automation effectiveness
depends on task standardization.
```

---

# 2404. Causal Context

Need represent:

```text
for standardized tasks,
automation improves throughput
```

rather than:

```text
automation always improves throughput
```

---

# 2405. Causal Discovery

System can propose causal hypotheses from data.

But should never silently promote:

```text
correlation → causation
```

---

# 2406. Causal Discovery pipeline

```text
Event History
↓
Pattern Detection
↓
Temporal Ordering
↓
Conditional Associations
↓
Candidate Causal Graph
↓
Domain Constraints
↓
Hypotheses
```

---

# 2407. Output must remain:

```text
HYPOTHESIS
```

until validated.

---

# 2408. Temporal precedence

Cause usually precedes effect.

Useful filter:

```text
Y consistently occurs before X
```

makes:

```text
X causes Y
```

less plausible.

---

# 2409. But delayed effects exist

Need:

```text
lag
```

---

# 2410. Causal Lag

Example:

```text
Training
↓ after 2 months
lower error rate
```

---

# 2411. Time-series Graph

Can include:

```text
X(t)
→
Y(t+1)
```

---

# 2412. Avoid naive lag correlation

Both variables can be driven by hidden trend.

---

# 2413. Mechanistic Evidence

Especially valuable in engineering.

Example:

```text
insufficient cooling
→ temperature rise
→ thermal throttling
→ lower throughput
```

Mechanism is physically interpretable.

---

# 2414. Mechanistic Graph

Can connect:

```text
physical state
control law
resource constraint
```

---

# 2415. Organizational mechanisms also possible

Example:

```text
approval requirement
→ additional queue
→ increased lead time
```

---

# 2416. Structural Equation Model

Later one could represent:

```text
Y = f(X1, X2, U)
```

for some domains.

But v0.1 does not require full SEM engine.

---

# 2417. Causal Model Types

Useful registry:

```text
QUALITATIVE_GRAPH
QUANTITATIVE_MODEL
SIMULATION_MODEL
STATISTICAL_MODEL
MECHANISTIC_MODEL
```

---

# 2418. Qualitative Graph

Good starting point.

```text
A increases B
B decreases C
```

without exact coefficients.

---

# 2419. Quantitative Model

Later:

```text
+1 unit X
→ expected ΔY
```

with uncertainty.

---

# 2420. Causal Claim Confidence

Should separate:

```text
edge existence confidence
effect direction confidence
effect magnitude confidence
transportability confidence
```

---

# 2421. Example

We may know:

```text
A affects B
```

strongly,

but not know:

```text
how much
```

---

# 2422. Causal Uncertainty

First-class:

```text
edge UNKNOWN
direction UNKNOWN
magnitude UNKNOWN
```

---

# 2423. Competing Causal Models

For one problem:

```text
Model A:
queue caused by staff shortage

Model B:
queue caused by input quality

Model C:
both
```

All remain until evidence discriminates.

---

# 2424. Model Comparison

Need:

```text
which observations each model explains?
what evidence would distinguish them?
```

---

# 2425. Discriminating Experiment

Very important.

Instead of asking:

```text
How to confirm Model A?
```

ask:

```text
What experiment gives different predictions
under A and B?
```

---

# 2426. Example

If staff shortage is cause:

```text
adding reviewer
should reduce queue.
```

If input quality is cause:

```text
adding reviewer
may barely help.
```

---

# 2427. Experiment Compiler integration

Causal Engine outputs:

```text
candidate discriminating intervention
```

Experiment Compiler turns it into:

```text
Project / Procedure
```

---

# 2428. Causal Question

Application object:

```yaml
causal_question:
  outcome: review_delay

  candidate_causes:
    - reviewer_capacity
    - input_quality

  decision:
    choose_intervention
```

---

# 2429. Decision-Relevant Causality

Не нужно изучать причинность ради полноты.

Priority:

```text
causal questions
that change decisions
```

---

# 2430. Value of Causal Information

Analog of Value of Information.

Ask:

```text
If we knew whether X causes Y,
would it change intervention?
```

---

# 2431. If no

Не тратить дорогой эксперимент.

---

# 2432. Intervention Engine

After causal model:

```text
Problem
↓
Candidate Causes
↓
Possible Interventions
↓
Predicted Effects
↓
Constraints
↓
Options
```

---

# 2433. Intervention types

```text
REMOVE_CAUSE
REDUCE_CAUSE
BLOCK_PATH
ADD_MEDIATOR
CHANGE_MODERATOR
INCREASE_RESILIENCE
```

---

# 2434. Remove Cause

Example:

```text
remove failing dependency
```

---

# 2435. Reduce Cause

```text
reduce API load
```

---

# 2436. Block Path

Example:

```text
queue still exists
but add bypass for critical tasks
```

---

# 2437. Add Mediator

Example:

```text
input validator
```

between:

```text
project submission
```

and:

```text
review
```

---

# 2438. Change Moderator

Example:

Automation works poorly only for unstructured requests.

Intervention:

```text
standardize request format
```

instead of replacing automation.

---

# 2439. Increase Resilience

Sometimes cause cannot be removed.

Example:

```text
supplier failures unavoidable
```

Intervention:

```text
second supplier
```

---

# 2440. Causal Leverage

An intervention is high-leverage if:

```text
one change
affects many downstream problems
```

---

# 2441. Example

Fix shared authentication layer:

```text
resolves failures in 12 projects
```

---

# 2442. Root Bottleneck Engine integration

Causal Graph improves earlier bottleneck detection.

Before:

```text
high dependency centrality
```

After:

```text
high dependency centrality
+
causal evidence
```

---

# 2443. Dependency centrality ≠ causal leverage

A central component may have many relations,

but changing it may not improve outcome.

---

# 2444. Causal Bottleneck

Node X:

```text
lies on many causal paths
to blocked outcomes
```

---

# 2445. Causal Path

```text
X
→ A
→ B
→ Outcome
```

---

# 2446. Path Blocking

If another condition prevents effect:

```text
X improves
but B remains blocked
```

then X intervention may have little value.

---

# 2447. Example

Buy second machine:

```text
machine capacity ↑
```

but:

```text
operator capacity remains bottleneck
```

So throughput barely changes.

---

# 2448. Bottleneck Migration

After fixing X:

```text
Y becomes new bottleneck
```

---

# 2449. Causal simulation should predict migration

This connects directly to earlier Strategic Simulation Engine.

---

# 2450. Intervention Simulation

```text
Base causal graph
+
do(X = x')
↓
simulate downstream state
```

---

# 2451. Qualitative simulation

For MVP:

```text
increase/decrease/unknown
```

may be enough.

---

# 2452. Quantitative simulation later

When reliable parameters exist.

---

# 2453. Uncertainty propagation

If edge uncertain:

```text
downstream prediction uncertain
```

---

# 2454. Never output precise downstream values from qualitative graph

---

# 2455. Counterfactual

Question:

```text
What would likely have happened
if intervention X had not occurred?
```

---

# 2456. Counterfactual differs from forecast

Forecast:

```text
future under option X
```

Counterfactual:

```text
alternative world relative
to observed historical outcome
```

---

# 2457. Counterfactual Evaluation

Useful after project:

```text
Did intervention actually help?
```

---

# 2458. But true counterfactual is unobserved

Need comparison model/control.

---

# 2459. Avoid claiming exact attribution without basis

Example:

```text
"Policy X saved €1M"
```

requires credible counterfactual.

---

# 2460. Better phrasing in system

```text
Observed cost after intervention: ...
Estimated counterfactual range: ...
Model assumptions: ...
```

---

# 2461. Causal Attribution

Outcomes can have:

```text
supported contributing causes
```

rather than one definitive cause.

---

# 2462. Incident Root Cause Analysis

For technical failures:

```text
Event
↓
Immediate Cause
↓
Contributing Factors
↓
Latent Conditions
```

# 2463. Immediate Cause

Example:

```text
service crashed
because memory exhausted
```

# 2464. Latent Condition

```text
no memory limit monitoring
```

# 2465. Organizational root condition

```text
capacity review process absent
```

# 2466. Five-Whys-like procedure

Could be workflow package.

```text
forcing exactly five levels
```

# 2467. Fault Tree

For safety-critical/technical domains:

```text
Top Failure
AND/OR
Subcauses
```

---

# 2468. Fault Tree package

Useful for:

```text
robots
hardware
infrastructure
```

---

# 2469. FMEA integration

Failure Mode and Effects Analysis can be represented via:

```text
Failure Mode
Cause
Effect
Detection
Mitigation
```

---

# 2470. No universal RPN required

Can preserve dimensions:

```text
severity

```

without one opaque score.

# 2471. Causal Graph + Risk Graph

Risk:

```text
possible future adverse event
```

Causal model explains:

```text
what conditions increase its likelihood
```

---

# 2472. Risk Intervention

Possible:

```text
reduce cause
improve detection
increase redundancy
limit consequence
```

---

# 2473. Safety Barrier Model

For physical systems:

```text
Hazard
↓
Barrier A
Barrier B
↓
Accident
```

# 2474. Barrier Failure

Causal model can represent:

```text
barrier unavailable
```

as risk path opening.

# 2475. Policy as causal intervention

Governance policies themselves change behavior.

Example:

```text
approval policy
→ fewer unsafe actions
→ more latency
```

# 2476. Policy Engine + Causal Engine

Before policy adoption:

```text
simulate intended
and unintended effects
```

# 2477. Unintended Consequences

Crucial class.

Example:

```text
strict approval requirement
→ fewer risky actions
```

but also:

```text
approval backlog
```

# 2478. Second-order effects

Causal Engine should search beyond immediate downstream node.

# 2479. Feedback Loops

Many systems are cyclic:

```text
Delay
→ pressure
→ shortcuts
→ failures
→ rework
→ more delay
```

# 2480. Causal Graph may therefore contain cycles

# 2481. Positive feedback loop

```text
success
→ more adoption
```

# 2482. Negative feedback loop

```text
uncertainty
```

Offer alternatives.

Question:

```text
replace entire system
```

```text
Y
```

---

# 2508. Causal Experiment is normal Project/Action structure

No new Core type required.

---

# 2509. Intervention Assignment

Experiment can use:

```text
ACTION/EXPERIMENT
```

with:

```text
context = validation study
```

---

# 2510. Outcome Variable

Represent as Claim/Measurement Artifact.

---

# 2511. Causal Baseline

Before intervention, capture:

```text
baseline
```

---

# 2512. Baseline must match context

Otherwise before/after comparison misleading.

---

# 2513. Seasonality

Time-dependent factors can confound.

Example:

```text
grant workload in December
```

vs summer.

---

# 2514. Causal Data Quality

Poor timestamps or missing variables limit causal inference.

System should expose:

```text
INSUFFICIENT_DATA
```

not force conclusion.

---

# 2515. Missing Confounder Warning

If known relevant variable absent:

```text
causal estimate unreliable
```

---

# 2516. Causal Evidence Quality

Dimensions:

```text
intervention control
sample relevance
confounding control
measurement quality
replication
```

---

# 2517. No universal causal confidence score needed

---

# 2518. Replication

Same causal effect reproduced in different contexts:

```text
increases transportability evidence
```

---

# 2519. Transportability

Question:

```text
Will causal relation from context A
hold in context B?
```

---

# 2520. Example

Workflow improvement works in:

```text
small startup
```

but will it work in:

```text
large public organization?
```

Unknown.

---

# 2521. Transportability Claim

Should be separate hypothesis.

---

# 2522. Context Similarity

Compare:

```text
task structure
resource mix
scale
constraints
```

not only industry label.

---

# 2523. Causal Knowledge Package

Could package:

```text
causal graph
validated interventions
known confounders
experiment results
```

for reusable domain knowledge.

---

# 2524. Example

```text
Grant Processing Causal Package
```

contains known drivers of:

```text
lead time
rework
error rate
```

---

# 2525. But imported causal package remains external knowledge

Local validation may be required.

---

# 2526. Causal Memory

Memory Engine should preserve:

```text
causal hypotheses
failed interventions
successful interventions
context
```

---

# 2527. Failed Intervention is especially valuable

Example:

```text
added machine
but queue unchanged
```

suggests:

```text
machine was not bottleneck
```

---

# 2528. Intervention History

For each causal node:

```text
what interventions attempted?
what happened?
```

---

# 2529. This improves future root-cause reasoning

---

# 2530. Causal Error Registry

Store cases where:

```text
predicted intervention effect
did not occur
```

---

# 2531. Model Revision

Then ask:

```text
missing cause?
wrong edge?
wrong magnitude?
context shift?
```

---

# 2532. Causal Calibration

Over time compare:

```text
predicted direction
predicted range
actual outcome
```

---

# 2533. Model quality

Evaluate by:

```text
intervention prediction
```

not only fitting historical data.

---

# 2534. Overfitting observational data

Model may explain past perfectly,

but fail under intervention.

That is central causal distinction.

---

# 2535. Causal Benchmark

Need fixtures with:

```text
known causal structures
```

for testing engine logic.

---

# 2536. Synthetic causal datasets

Useful for:

```text
cycle
confounder
mediator
selection bias
```

tests.

---

# 2537. Domain benchmark

Historical interventions with known outcomes.

---

# 2538. Root Cause Benchmark

Cases where known root cause documented.

---

# 2539. Intervention Recommendation Benchmark

Check whether engine:

```text
targets actual bottleneck
```

rather than symptom.

---

# 2540. Causal Explanation

Human-readable output should say:

```text
We observe A and B correlated.
Current causal hypothesis is A→B.
Evidence: ...
Alternative explanation: C.
Confidence in edge existence: ...
Next discriminating test: ...
```

---

# 2541. Avoid categorical language when evidence weak

Not:

```text
A is the cause.
```

If only observational.

---

# 2542. Explanation Graph

UI:

```text
Observed Problem
↓
Candidate Causes
↓
Evidence
↓
Interventions
```

---

# 2543. Root Cause Tree

Useful visual mode.

---

# 2544. Competing Model View

Show:

```text
Model A
Model B
Model C
```

side-by-side.

---

# 2545. Evidence overlay

Each edge shows:

```text
supported
contested
unknown
```

---

# 2546. Intervention overlay

Controllable nodes highlighted.

---

# 2547. Cost overlay

Show intervention effort.

---

# 2548. Time overlay

Show causal delays.

---

# 2549. 2D/3D integration

In virtual technopark, causal graph should not be confused with physical layout.

Use dedicated causal layer.

---

# 2550. Example 3D metaphor

A blocked production line may show:

```text
causal heat path
```

from failing resource to downstream projects.

But semantic graph remains canonical.

---

# 2551. Causal Query Language

Useful queries:

```text
WHY project_17 delayed?
```

```text
WHAT_IF add reviewer_capacity +20%?
```

```text
WHAT_CAN_CHANGE outcome=lead_time<5d?
```

```text
WHAT_EVIDENCE distinguishes model_A/model_B?
```

---

# 2552. WHY query

Returns:

```text
direct causes
contributing factors
evidence
uncertainties
```

---

# 2553. WHAT_IF query

Invokes intervention simulation.

---

# 2554. HOW_TO query

Goal-seeking causal planner.

---

# 2555. DISTINGUISH query

Produces experiment proposal.

---

# 2556. Causal API

Минимально:

```text
POST /causal/questions
POST /causal/hypotheses
GET /causal/graphs/{id}

POST /causal/interventions/simulate
POST /causal/interventions/propose

POST /causal/root-cause
POST /causal/experiments/design
```

---

# 2557. Causal Hypothesis object

```yaml
causal_hypothesis:
  cause: reviewer_capacity
  effect: review_delay

  direction: decreases

  context:
    organization_unit: security_office

  evidence:
    - episode_12
    - experiment_7

  alternatives:
    - input_quality
```

---

# 2558. Causal Model object

```yaml
causal_model:
  nodes:
    - input_quality
    - rework
    - queue
    - lead_time

  edges:
    - input_quality -> rework
    - rework -> queue
    - queue -> lead_time
```

---

# 2559. Intervention object

```yaml
intervention:
  target: input_quality

  mechanism:
    standardized_intake_form

  expected_effect:
    rework: decrease
    queue: decrease
    lead_time: decrease
```

---

# 2560. Causal Resolver

If problem appears:

```text
Project delay
```

it can search:

```text
historical causal models
similar episodes
known interventions
```

---

# 2561. Similarity by mechanism

Not merely:

```text
same words
```

but:

```text
same flow pattern
same bottleneck type
```

---

# 2562. Cross-domain causal analogy

Example:

```text
queueing bottleneck in lab
```

may resemble:

```text
approval bottleneck in office
```

Mechanism:

```text
arrival rate > service rate
```

---

# 2563. This enables powerful cross-domain transfer

But analogy starts as:

```text
HYPOTHESIS
```

---

# 2564. Causal Archetypes

Reusable patterns:

```text
QUEUE_OVERLOAD
SINGLE_POINT_FAILURE
POSITIVE_FEEDBACK
RESOURCE_STARVATION
REWORK_LOOP
INFORMATION_DELAY
```

---

# 2565. Queue Overload Archetype

```text
arrival rate ↑
→ queue ↑
→ lead time ↑
```

---

# 2566. Rework Loop Archetype

```text
poor input quality
→ errors
→ rework
→ delay
→ pressure
→ poorer quality
```

---

# 2567. Single Point Failure Archetype

```text
one critical resource
→ many dependents
```

---

# 2568. Information Delay Archetype

```text
state changes
→ delayed observation
→ wrong decisions
```

---

# 2569. Policy Feedback Archetype

```text
strict control
→ slower throughput
→ workaround behavior
→ less observability
```

---

# 2570. Archetype matching

Current graph can be compared to known causal archetypes.

---

# 2571. But archetype match ≠ proven causal model

It generates:

```text
candidate explanation
```

---

# 2572. Causal Package Registry

Could be extension of Semantic Package Registry.

Package type:

```text
CAUSAL_MODEL_PACKAGE
```

---

# 2573. Includes

```text
variables
edges
known contexts
evidence
interventions
benchmark cases
```

---

# 2574. Causal Package Versioning

Important as model improves.

---

# 2575. Causal Model Drift

Environment changes may invalidate previous causal relation.

---

# 2576. Example

Automation once reduced workload.

Later:

```text
new compliance requirements
```

change process.

Old effect no longer holds.

---

# 2577. Revalidation Trigger

If:

```text
key moderator changed
```

retest causal assumptions.

---

# 2578. Assumption Registry integration

Causal model depends on assumptions.

Example:

```text
demand remains constant
```

---

# 2579. Assumption invalidation

Triggers:

```text
CAUSAL_MODEL_REVIEW
```

---

# 2580. Causal World State

World State may include:

```text
observed state
structural relations
causal hypotheses
validated causal relations
```

but layers stay separate.

---

# 2581. Never let causal hypothesis appear as ordinary undisputed relation

---

# 2582. Epistemic labels preserved in UI/API

---

# 2583. Causal Decision Support

For major decision:

```text
Intervention A
Intervention B
Intervention C
```

show:

```text
which causal paths each targets
what evidence supports expected effect
what could go wrong
```

---

# 2584. Example

Problem:

```text
long lab queue
```

Option A:

```text
buy machine
```

targets:

```text
machine capacity
```

Option B:

```text
improve sample preparation
```

targets upstream cause.

Option C:

```text
outsource overflow
```

targets consequence.

---

# 2585. Causal intervention taxonomy by location in chain

```text
UPSTREAM
MIDSTREAM
DOWNSTREAM
RESILIENCE
```

---

# 2586. Upstream intervention

Remove root driver.

---

# 2587. Downstream intervention

Mitigate consequence.

---

# 2588. Sometimes downstream is still rational

If upstream cause:

```text
cannot be changed quickly
```

---

# 2589. Intervention Time Horizon

Need:

```text
immediate
medium
long-term
```

---

# 2590. Example

Immediate:

```text
outsource queue
```

Long-term:

```text
build new lab
```

---

# 2591. Intervention Stack

Could combine:

```text
temporary bridge
+
structural fix
```

---

# 2592. This fits earlier Bridge Capability concept

---

# 2593. Causal Roadmap

Sequence interventions based on:

```text
dependencies
time-to-effect
feedback
```

---

# 2594. Example

```text
1 temporary external service
2 train internal operator
3 acquire second machine
```

---

# 2595. Causal Portfolio

Multiple bottlenecks may share root cause.

Example:

```text
lack of standardized data model
```

causes issues in:

```text
funding
research
project reporting
```

---

# 2596. Shared Root Cause Detector

Very powerful.

---

# 2597. Common Cause Opportunity

If one root cause affects many projects:

```text
create strategic infrastructure project
```

---

# 2598. Example

Problem cluster:

```text
duplicate extraction
bad handoffs
inconsistent reports
```

Shared cause:

```text
no common semantic schema
```

Intervention:

```text
IIR adoption program
```

---

# 2599. Causal Program Composer

Could cluster Projects by:

```text
shared causal intervention
```

not just shared topic.

---

# 2600. This may produce better Programs

Because projects belong together if:

```text
one intervention
changes several outcomes
```

---

# 2601. Organization Design via causality

Instead of only observing repeated demand,

ask:

```text
what organizational structure
causes lower coordination cost?
```

---

# 2602. Pilot experiments compare structures

Centralized vs distributed team.

---

# 2603. Organizational causal knowledge

Could become reusable:

```text
contextual organizational patterns
```

---

# 2604. Economic causality

Resource Accounting observes:

```text
shared platform
correlates with lower costs
```

Causal Engine asks:

```text
did platform reduce cost,
or were mature projects simply more likely to use it?
```

---

# 2605. Strategic importance

Without causal analysis, resource allocation may optimize wrong proxy.

---

# 2606. Proxy Failure

Example:

```text
higher utilization
```

may look efficient,

but cause:

```text
longer queues
```

---

# 2607. Goodhart-like effect

When metric becomes target:

```text
behavior may change
```

and metric loses relation to true goal.

---

# 2608. Causal Metric Governance

Before adopting KPI:

```text
what behavior will it incentivize?
```

---

# 2609. Example

Goal:

```text
improve research quality
```

KPI:

```text
number of papers
```

may cause:

```text
more papers
```

without:

```text
better research
```

---

# 2610. Goal → Metric causal link must itself be a hypothesis

---

# 2611. KPI Validity

Ask:

```text
Does improving Metric M
cause or reliably indicate
Goal G improvement?
```

---

# 2612. This links causal layer to Governance Engine

---

# 2613. Unintended Metric Effects

Monitor:

```text
gaming
local optimization
quality degradation
```

---

# 2614. Causal Anomaly Detection

Unexpected relationship change:

```text
same intervention
different outcome
```

may indicate context shift.

---

# 2615. Causal Change Point

Example:

```text
after model update,
review automation no longer reduces workload
```

---

# 2616. Model Revision required.

---

# 2617. Causal Observatory

Dashboard:

```text
Active Causal Models
Root Causes
Open Causal Questions
Interventions
Experiments
Model Errors
```

---

# 2618. Root Cause View

Shows:

```text
problem
candidate causes
evidence
alternative explanations
```

---

# 2619. Intervention View

Shows:

```text
target
mechanism
predicted effects
uncertainty
cost
status
```

---

# 2620. Experiment View

Shows:

```text
hypothesis
design
results
causal update
```

---

# 2621. Causal Model Diff

Compare:

```text
v1
vs
v2
```

show:

```text
edge added
edge removed
direction changed
new confounder
```

---

# 2622. Causal Audit

For strategic intervention:

```text
why did we expect this to work?
```

system can reconstruct model and evidence.

---

# 2623. Causal Security

Malicious data can manipulate causal inference.

Example:

```text
fake incidents
```

make system believe provider causes failures.

---

# 2624. Need source provenance and anomaly checks

---

# 2625. Intervention safety

Never automatically test high-risk causal hypotheses on real humans/physical systems without governance.

---

# 2626. Experiment Risk Classification

```text
LOW
MEDIUM
HIGH
CRITICAL
```

---

# 2627. Low-risk

Software sandbox.

---

# 2628. High-risk

Physical/financial/legal interventions.

---

# 2629. Simulate first where possible

---

# 2630. Human-subject-like organizational experiments

Need appropriate consent/governance where people are materially affected.

---

# 2631. Causal Engine should propose safe evidence alternatives

Example:

```text
use historical data
```

instead of experimental manipulation if enough.

---

# 2632. Causal Discovery Agent

Role:

```text
CAUSAL_ANALYST
```

Input:

```text
Problem + History
```

Output:

```text
candidate models
confounders
evidence gaps
```

---

# 2633. Experiment Designer Agent

Input:

```text
competing causal hypotheses
```

Output:

```text
experiment options
```

---

# 2634. Root Cause Agent

Input:

```text
incident
```

Output:

```text
causal graph proposal
```

---

# 2635. But final causal Claims require validation

---

# 2636. Causal Procedure Packages

Reusable workflows:

```text
ROOT_CAUSE_ANALYSIS
CAUSAL_MODEL_COMPARISON
INTERVENTION_DESIGN
EXPERIMENT_DESIGN
```

---

# 2637. Causal reasoning + memory

Before new root-cause analysis:

```text
retrieve similar past causal episodes
```

---

# 2638. Causal case library

Stores:

```text
symptom
root cause
intervention
outcome
context
```

---

# 2639. Cross-domain mechanism search

Example:

```text
resource starvation
```

pattern can occur in:

```text
CPU scheduler
lab equipment
human review office
```

---

# 2640. This is especially useful for your virtual technopark concept

Потому что одна и та же абстрактная causal structure может существовать одновременно:

```text
в software
в организации
в производстве
в логистике
```

---

# 2641. Semantic Causal Archetype acts as transferable knowledge

---

# 2642. Causal Compiler

Можно представить новый compiler stage:

```text
Goal
↓
Causal Analysis
↓
Target Variables
↓
Project Generation
```

---

# 2643. This precedes Project Compiler for complex goals

Instead of:

```text
Goal
→ guessed project
```

better:

```text
Goal
→ causal model
→ leverage points
→ candidate projects
```

---

# 2644. Example

Goal:

```text
reduce robot assembly defects
```

Causal Engine finds candidates:

```text
sensor calibration
operator training
fixture precision
software threshold
```

Then Project Generator creates alternatives.

---

# 2645. Causal leverage points

Borrow useful system concept:

```text
where small intervention
can produce large effect
```

---

# 2646. But leverage point is evidence-backed hypothesis

not mystical system label.

---

# 2647. Leverage dimensions

```text
downstream reach
controllability
cost
time-to-effect
reversibility
uncertainty
```

---

# 2648. Low leverage but easy intervention

May still be best short-term.

---

# 2649. High leverage but uncertain intervention

May deserve experiment first.

---

# 2650. Intervention Portfolio

Could combine:

```text
quick wins
structural fixes
experiments
```

---

# 2651. Causal roadmap phases

```text
1 diagnose
2 test
3 intervene
4 monitor
5 revise
```

---

# 2652. Monitoring after intervention is mandatory

Otherwise system never learns if causal model correct.

---

# 2653. Outcome Attribution

After intervention:

```text
observe expected variables
unexpected variables
```

---

# 2654. Side Effect Detection

System should explicitly search for:

```text
unintended downstream effects
```

---

# 2655. Example

Automation reduced time,

but:

```text
error severity increased
```

---

# 2656. Multi-outcome causal model

Never optimize only one outcome.

---

# 2657. Causal Outcome Vector

```text
primary outcome
secondary outcomes
safety outcomes
resource effects
```

---

# 2658. Causal Governance Gate

Major intervention package includes:

```text
model
evidence
alternatives
uncertainties
expected side effects
```

for Decision.

---

# 2659. Human authority selects intervention

---

# 2660. Causal World Model integration

World State now becomes richer:

```text
Entities
Claims
Evidence
Dependencies
Events
Causal Hypotheses
Causal Models
```

---

# 2661. This is a move from descriptive to explanatory model

Descriptive:

```text
what is happening?
```

Explanatory:

```text
why?
```

---

# 2662. Then prescriptive layer asks:

```text
what can we change?
```

---

# 2663. Three levels

```text
DESCRIPTIVE
what is?

CAUSAL
why?

INTERVENTIONAL
what if we change?
```

---

# 2664. Fourth level

```text
GOAL-SEEKING
what should be changed
to reach target?
```

subject to governance.

---

# 2665. This completes a major reasoning hierarchy

```text
Observe
↓
Describe
↓
Explain
↓
Intervene
↓
Verify
↓
Learn
```

---

# 2666. Minimal MVP

Start only with:

```text
qualitative causal graphs
root-cause hypotheses
intervention proposals
experiment links
```

---

# 2667. MVP 1

Incident:

```text
Task repeatedly fails.
```

Generate:

```text
candidate root-cause graph
```

---

# 2668. MVP 2

Attach Evidence to each causal edge.

---

# 2669. MVP 3

Represent competing models.

---

# 2670. MVP 4

Generate discriminating test.

---

# 2671. MVP 5

Store intervention + outcome.

---

# 2672. MVP 6

Revise causal graph after outcome.

---

# 2673. MVP 7

Integrate causal model with Counterfactual Engine.

---

# 2674. Acceptance criterion

The module is useful when system can answer:

```text
Why is Project X blocked?
```

with:

```text
candidate causal chain
evidence
uncertainties
alternative explanations
testable intervention
```

instead of:

```text
"because Task Y is late"
```

---

# 2675. Architecture Freeze снова выдерживает

Не нужен новый фундаментальный Core type.

Используются:

```text
CLAIM
EVIDENCE
ACTION
EVENT
CONTEXT
DECISION
PROJECT
```

А causal semantics добавляются через:

```text
extension predicates
application models
```

---

# 2676. Следующий фундаментальный слой

После причинного слоя возникает ещё более высокий вопрос:

> Если система понимает текущее состояние, причинные механизмы, ограничения, ресурсы и цели, как ей строить **многошаговые стратегии в условиях неопределённости**, где решения сегодня меняют набор доступных возможностей завтра?

Следующий модуль:

# **Adaptive Strategy, Option Value & Sequential Decision Engine v0.1**

Он должен работать не только с:

```text
"какой вариант лучше сейчас?"
```

а с:

```text
"какой первый шаг оставляет больше хороших вариантов позже?"
```

То есть учитывать:

```text
option value
reversibility
learning value
path dependence
lock-in
stage-gated investment
adaptive policies
```

и превращать стратегию из одного статического плана в последовательность решений:

```text
Observe
↓
Act a little
↓
Learn
↓
Re-evaluate
↓
Commit more only when evidence improves
```

Это особенно важно для frontier research, новых технологий, стартапов, инфраструктуры и любых проектов, где заранее невозможно надёжно выбрать один окончательный путь.
contents.title: Causal Reasoning, Dependency Discovery & Intervention Engine v0.1

contents.content: Следующая часть — **Adaptive Strategy, Option Value & Sequential Decision Engine v0.1**: как принимать не одно большое решение «сейчас и навсегда», а строить адаптивные стратегии, сохранять свободу манёвра, избегать преждевременного lock-in и покупать знания маленькими обратимыми шагами.
Продолжение на русском

Продолжаю полностью **на русском языке**. Следующий модуль — **Adaptive Strategy, Option Value & Sequential Decision Engine v0.1**: он нужен для ситуаций, где невозможно сразу выбрать «идеальный» путь и выгоднее двигаться поэтапно, сохраняя варианты, собирая новые данные и увеличивая обязательства только по мере роста уверенности.

# Adaptive Strategy, Option Value & Sequential Decision Engine v0.1

## 2677. Главный переход

До этого Innovation OS уже умеет:

```text
наблюдать мир
↓
строить World State
↓
понимать зависимости
↓
строить causal models
↓
предлагать interventions
↓
симулировать последствия
```

Но стратегический вопрос сложнее:

> Нужно ли прямо сейчас выбирать окончательное решение?

Во многих инновационных задачах ответ:

```text
нет
```

Иногда лучше:

```text
сделать небольшой обратимый шаг
↓
получить новую информацию
↓
посмотреть на результат
↓
только потом выбирать следующий шаг
```

---

# 2678. Статический план vs адаптивная стратегия

Статический план:

```text
Сегодня:
выбрать путь A

Дальше:
выполнять A 3 года
```

Адаптивная стратегия:

```text
Шаг 1:
```

# 2835. This is one of the strongest general principles of the whole Innovation OS

Because same logic applies to:

```text
science
software
hiring
equipment
organizations
funding
```

---

# 2836. Real Options Portfolio

Could materialize:

```text
active options
exercise cost
expiry
prerequisites
strategic relevance
```

---

# 2837. Option Heatmap

Show:

```text
expiring soon
high lock-in if ignored
cheap to preserve
```

---

# 2838. Option Discovery

Opportunity Engine can discover:

```text
an action creates a valuable future option
```

even if current direct value modest.

---

# 2839. Example

Building standard data export layer:

```text
does not solve current product feature
```

but enables:

```text
future vendor switching
federation
analytics
```

---

# 2840. Option Creation Project

Some Projects intentionally create:

```text
future strategic option
```

---

# 2841. Capability as Option

An unused capability can still be valuable because:

```text
it allows future project activation
```

---

# 2842. Example

Maintaining expertise in alternative language/runtime.

---

# 2843. Dormant Capability

State:

```text
AVAILABLE_LOW_CAPACITY
```

or:

```text
STANDBY
```

application-level.

---

# 2844. Capability Preservation

Training/occasional use can prevent decay.

---

# 2845. Strategic Experiment

An experiment can be chosen because it:

```text
maximizes decision-relevant information
```

not because it maximizes product progress.

---

# 2846. Example

Test hardest assumption first.

---

# 2847. Assumption-First Strategy

List assumptions:

```text
A technical feasibility
B user demand
C cost
D regulatory acceptance
```

Find:

```text
which assumption
could kill project fastest?
```

---

# 2848. Test high-risk assumptions early

This is similar to falsification-first validation.

---

# 2849. Assumption Burn-down

Project reduces:

```text
critical unvalidated assumptions
```

over time.

---

# 2850. Assumption Portfolio

For Program:

```text
which assumptions
are shared across projects?
```

---

# 2851. Shared Assumption Experiment

One test may affect many projects.

---

# 2852. Strategic Learning Curve

As Evidence accumulates:

```text
uncertainty ↓
commitment ↑
```

---

# 2853. Desired pattern

Not:

```text
commitment ↑
while uncertainty stays high
```

unless urgency justifies it.

---

# 2854. Commitment-Uncertainty Map

Very useful visualization.

Axes:

```text
X = uncertainty
Y = committed resources
```

---

# 2855. Dangerous quadrant

```text
high commitment
+
high uncertainty
```

---

# 2856. Sometimes unavoidable

For example emergencies.

But system should expose it clearly.

---

# 2857. Strategic Urgency

Another dimension:

```text
delay cost
```

may justify committing before uncertainty resolved.

---

# 2858. Urgency vs Learning

Example:

```text
market window closes in 2 months
```

Waiting for perfect evidence can destroy option.

---

# 2859. Therefore sequential strategy balances

```text
learning
speed
commitment
expiry
```

---

# 2860. Option Expiry Pressure

As expiry approaches:

```text
waiting value declines
```

---

# 2861. Decision Deadline

Every major option may have:

```text
decision_by
```

---

# 2862. Decision Queue

Governance Dashboard can show:

```text
options expiring
decisions waiting
evidence missing
```

---

# 2863. Strategic Calendar

Not only project deadlines,

but:

```text
option windows
grant deadlines
contract renewals
technology review points
```

---

# 2864. Review Cadence

Some strategies require periodic:

```text
monthly
quarterly
event-triggered
```

reviews.

---

# 2865. Strategy Review Package

Input:

```text
current strategy
new evidence
signposts
```

Output:

```text
continue
modify
exercise option
abandon branch
```

as proposals.

---

# 2866. Strategy State Machine

```text
DRAFT
APPROVED
ACTIVE
REVIEW_REQUIRED
ADAPTING
COMPLETED
SUPERSEDED
```

---

# 2867. Strategy Versioning

Strategy v1:

```text
pilot external provider
```

Strategy v2:

```text
begin internal migration
```

History preserved.

---

# 2868. Strategy Diff

Show:

```text
new option
closed option
changed trigger
increased commitment
```

---

# 2869. Decision Rights

Only authorized governance roles may:

```text
exercise major option
close major option
increase commitment
```

---

# 2870. Runtime may handle small tactical adaptations

Within explicit envelope.

---

# 2871. Strategic vs Tactical Adaptation

Tactical:

```text
switch API provider
```

within approved set.

Strategic:

```text
change from SaaS architecture
to internal platform
```

requires Decision.

---

# 2872. Strategic Envelope

Defines:

```text
allowed tactical choices
budget
time
providers
risk
```

---

# 2873. Example

Strategy:

```text
Use external inference
for next 6 months,
but keep data portable.
```

Runtime may switch:

```text
Provider A ↔ B
```

but cannot:

```text
delete local portability layer
```

---

# 2874. Sequential Resource Allocation

Portfolio does not allocate full resources at once.

It can allocate:

```text
exploration budget
then scale budget
```

---

# 2875. Portfolio Funnel

```text
100 hypotheses
↓
20 experiments
↓
5 pilots
↓
2 programs
↓
1 major infrastructure investment
```

---

# 2876. Resource Recycling

When branch killed:

```text
capacity returns to market
```

quickly.

---

# 2877. This improves portfolio agility

---

# 2878. Kill Decision Latency

If evidence says project should stop,

but organization delays stop:

```text
resources continue burning
```

---

# 2879. Kill Queue

Could show:

```text
projects crossing kill criteria
but not yet reviewed
```

---

# 2880. Strategic Escalation

Unexpected strong result may justify:

```text
accelerated scale review
```

---

# 2881. Upside Option

Strategy not only protects downside.

It preserves ability to exploit:

```text
unexpected positive breakthrough
```

---

# 2882. Example

Small robotics experiment discovers:

```text
sensor much better than expected
```

Option:

```text
launch new project family
```

---

# 2883. Opportunity Creation

Experiments can generate:

```text
new opportunities
```

not originally planned.

---

# 2884. Sequential strategy therefore branches both on failure and success

---

# 2885. Surprise Handling

Observed outcome outside model:

```text
SURPRISE_EVENT
```

---

# 2886. Surprise is epistemically valuable

It may indicate:

```text
wrong assumptions
new causal mechanism
new opportunity
```

---

# 2887. Strategy should have unplanned-review path

Not only predefined branches.

---

# 2888. Adaptive Strategy Engine

Pipeline:

```text
Goal
↓
Uncertainty Map
↓
Options
↓
Commitments
↓
Causal Model
↓
Scenario Simulation
↓
Sequential Strategy Alternatives
↓
Governance Decision
```

---

# 2889. Uncertainty Map

Classify unknowns:

```text
technical
market
funding
regulatory
organizational
physical
```

---

# 2890. Option Map

Which actions:

```text
resolve unknown
preserve flexibility
create capability
commit resources
```

---

# 2891. Commitment Map

Which decisions:

```text
reduce future flexibility
```

---

# 2892. Strategy synthesis

Find combinations:

```text
experiment
bridge
option
commitment
review gate
```

---

# 2893. Strategy Output

Not:

```text
"Choose A."
```

But:

```text
Path A:
commit now

Path B:
pilot then decide

Path C:
wait and monitor
```

with consequences.

---

# 2894. Strategy Evaluation

Dimensions:

```text
Goal Progress
Learning
Commitment
Reversibility
Lock-in
Resilience
Time
Cost
```

---

# 2895. No global strategic score

Human/policy chooses trade-offs.

---

# 2896. Sequential Simulation

Strategy is evaluated across time.

Example:

```text
Month 0
Experiment

Month 3
Decision gate

Month 6
Pilot

Month 12
Scale
```

---

# 2897. Scenario Tree

At Month 3:

```text
good evidence
medium evidence
bad evidence
```

each branch.

---

# 2898. Probabilities optional

If credible probabilities unavailable:

```text
do not invent them
```

Use:

```text
scenario classes
```

---

# 2899. Robust Adaptive Strategy

Better than one static robust action:

```text
adaptive policy
```

can respond differently under each scenario.

---

# 2900. Example

```text
If demand grows:
scale.

If demand flat:
remain shared service.

If demand falls:
retire.
```

---

# 2901. Adaptive Policy can outperform fixed plan

because:

```text
future information changes action
```

---

# 2902. Strategy Compiler

Approved sequential strategy can compile into:

```text
Program
Projects
Decision Gates
Condition Watches
```

---

# 2903. Example

Strategy:

```text
pilot then scale
```

compiles:

```text
Project: Pilot
↓
Verification
↓
Decision Gate
↓
conditional Scale Project
```

---

# 2904. Conditional Project

State:

```text
WAITING_FOR_TRIGGER
```

---

# 2905. Trigger

```text
pilot_passed = YES
```

activates it.

---

# 2906. This integrates with earlier WAITING_FOR_CAPABILITY model

---

# 2907. Conditional Funding

Funding application can be prepared before trigger,

but submitted only if:

```text
stage criteria satisfied
```

---

# 2908. Pre-positioning

Very useful strategy:

```text
prepare future option
without exercising it
```

---

# 2909. Examples

```text
draft grant
qualify second supplier
build migration adapter
train backup operator
```

---

# 2910. Pre-positioning Cost

Small current cost buys:

```text
faster future activation
```

---

# 2911. Readiness Option

Some capabilities are maintained mainly to reduce:

```text
time-to-react
```

---

# 2912. Strategic Reserve

Earlier concept integrates here.

---

# 2913. Option Exercise Conditions

Need be explicit where possible.

For example:

```text
IF external API cost > X
THEN evaluate local deployment.
```

---

# 2914. Avoid over-automation

Complex strategic conditions should trigger review,

not necessarily automatic execution.

---

# 2915. Strategy Monitoring Agent

Role:

```text
STRATEGY_MONITOR
```

watches:

```text
signposts
assumptions
option expiry
commitments
```

---

# 2916. It does not set new mission automatically

It can generate:

```text
review proposals
```

---

# 2917. Strategy Memory

Store:

```text
strategy version
assumptions
signposts
decisions
outcomes
```

---

# 2918. Strategy Postmortem

After completion:

```text
Which branches occurred?
Which assumptions wrong?
Was staged structure useful?
```

---

# 2919. Sequential Decision Learning

System can learn patterns like:

```text
for high-uncertainty physical projects,
prototype-before-purchase
reduced stranded capital
```

as contextual hypothesis.

---

# 2920. Strategy Benchmark

Harder than tool benchmark.

Can replay historical scenarios.

---

# 2921. Historical Backtest

Given only information available at t0:

```text
what strategy would engine propose?
```

Then compare with actual later world.

---

# 2922. Avoid hindsight leakage

Critical.

Engine must not use:

```text
future information
```

during historical backtest.

---

# 2923. Strategy Regret Analysis

Compare:

```text
actual chosen path
```

to alternatives under hindsight,

but clearly mark:

```text
counterfactual estimate
```

---

# 2924. Strategy Calibration

Does engine systematically:

```text
overcommit too early?
wait too long?
overvalue optionality?
```

---

# 2925. Strategy Error Registry

Categories:

```text
PREMATURE_COMMITMENT
MISSED_WINDOW
UNDER_EXPLORATION
OVER_EXPLORATION
LOCK_IN_UNDERSTATED
SIGNPOST_MISSED
```

---

# 2926. Strategy Improvement Proposal

After recurring error:

```text
update heuristic
simulation model
review policy
```

---

# 2927. Strategy Packages

Reusable strategic patterns can be packages.

Package type:

```text
STRATEGY_ARCHETYPE
```

---

# 2928. Example package

```text
Hardware Frontier Entry Strategy
```

contains:

```text
research stage
prototype stage
pilot stage
equipment purchase gate
```

---

# 2929. Another

```text
Vendor Migration Strategy
```

contains:

```text
portability layer
dual-run
validation
cutover
rollback
```

---

# 2930. Strategy Package requirements

Include:

```text
applicable contexts
assumptions
decision gates
known failure modes
```

---

# 2931. Imported strategy not automatically suitable

Local causal/context validation required.

---

# 2932. Strategic Simulation Registry

For each strategy:

```text
scenarios evaluated
model version
outcomes
```

---

# 2933. Strategy Digital Twin

Could maintain a virtual projected state:

```text
if strategy A followed
```

without changing real world.

---

# 2934. Compare branches visually

2D:

```text
Current State
├── Strategy A
├── Strategy B
└── Strategy C
```

---

# 2935. Time slider

See projected World State:

```text
6 months
12 months
24 months
```

---

# 2936. 3D / MMORPG metaphor

Strategies could appear as:

```text
possible routes through world
```

with:

```text
locked gates
optional branches
decision points
```

---

# 2937. But do not make strategy look deterministic

Branches with uncertainty should remain visibly:

```text
conditional
```

---

# 2938. Fog of Future

Earlier fog-of-war concept applies.

Unknown future branches:

```text
partially unresolved
```

---

# 2939. Exploration Missions

Can be generated specifically to:

```text
reveal future branch
```

---

# 2940. Decision Gate UI

At gate:

```text
Evidence
Options
Commitments
Scenario impacts
```

shown together.

---

# 2941. Strategy Dashboard

Minimum screens:

```text
Active Strategies
Options
Commitments
Decision Gates
Signposts
Lock-in Map
```

---

# 2942. Active Strategies

Shows:

```text
current stage
next gate
open assumptions
```

---

# 2943. Option View

Shows:

```text
option
exercise cost
expiry
prerequisites
maintenance cost
```

---

# 2944. Commitment View

Shows:

```text
irreversible decisions
exit costs
dependencies
```

---

# 2945. Signpost View

Shows:

```text
what signals are being watched
```

---

# 2946. Lock-in Map

Shows:

```text
vendor
technology
data
skill
organizational dependencies
```

---

# 2947. Strategy API

Minimum:

```text
POST /strategies
POST /strategies/simulate
POST /strategies/review

GET /strategies/{id}
GET /strategies/{id}/options
GET /strategies/{id}/decision-gates
```

---

# 2948. Option API

```text
POST /options
POST /options/{id}/exercise
POST /options/{id}/abandon
GET /options/expiring
```

---

# 2949. Commitment API

```text
GET /commitments
GET /commitments/{id}/exit-analysis
```

---

# 2950. Signpost API

```text
POST /signposts
GET /signposts/triggered
```

---

# 2951. Strategy Review Event

Examples:

```text
SIGNPOST_TRIGGERED
OPTION_EXPIRING
ASSUMPTION_INVALIDATED
COMMITMENT_RISK_CHANGED
NEW_FRONTIER_CAPABILITY
```

---

# 2952. Condition Watch integration

Signposts naturally become:

```text
condition watches
```

within Runtime.

---

# 2953. Minimal MVP

Start with:

```text
stage gates
options
signposts
commitment registry
```

---

# 2954. MVP 1

One Project:

```text
prototype
→ gate
→ pilot
→ gate
→ scale
```

---

# 2955. MVP 2

Store:

```text
kill criteria
scale criteria
```

---

# 2956. MVP 3

Option:

```text
buy equipment
```

only after:

```text
demand threshold
```

---

# 2957. MVP 4

Detect:

```text
vendor lock-in increasing
```

---

# 2958. MVP 5

Compare:

```text
commit now
pilot
wait
```

through Scenario Engine.

---

# 2959. MVP 6

Event triggers strategy review.

---

# 2960. MVP 7

Compile approved strategy into conditional projects.

---

# 2961. Acceptance criterion

System should be able to answer:

> «Мы ещё не знаем, будет ли технология X достаточно хороша. Что разумно сделать сейчас, чтобы не потратить слишком много и не закрыть полезные будущие варианты?»

И вернуть не одну команду, а структуру:

```text
Experiment
↓
Decision Gate
├── Scale
├── Continue Experiment
└── Stop
```

с:

```text
Evidence requirements
Cost ranges
Option value
Lock-in
Signposts
```

---

# 2962. Architecture Freeze снова выдерживает

Не нужен новый фундаментальный Core type.

Используются:

```text
PROJECT
ACTION
CLAIM
CONSTRAINT
DECISION
CONTEXT
EVENT
RESOURCE
```

А:

```text
Option
Strategy
Commitment
Signpost
```

остаются application-level objects/archetypes.

---

# 2963. Новый уровень всей архитектуры

После этого Innovation OS умеет уже четыре разных типа reasoning:

```text
DESCRIPTIVE
что происходит?

CAUSAL
почему происходит?

INTERVENTIONAL
что изменится, если вмешаться?

SEQUENTIAL STRATEGIC
что сделать сейчас,
чтобы сохранить хорошие
следующие решения?
```

---

# 2964. Это особенно важно для инноваций

Потому что инновационная среда почти никогда не выглядит так:

```text
Goal
→ заранее известный план
→ гарантированный результат
```

Она выглядит:

```text
Goal
↓
Unknown
↓
Experiment
↓
Evidence
↓
Branch
↓
New Unknown
↓
Next Decision
```

---

# 2965. Следующий фундаментальный слой

После появления Adaptive Strategy Engine возникает следующий вопрос:

> Как координировать множество независимых AI-агентов, людей, команд, сервисов и организаций, которые одновременно принимают локальные решения, но должны сохранять глобальную согласованность системы?

Следующий модуль:

# **Multi-Agent Coordination, Negotiation & Collective Intelligence Engine v0.1**

Он должен формализовать:

```text
разделение задач между агентами;
конкурирующие предложения;
обсуждение и критику;
переговоры между Resource providers;
распределённое планирование;
conflict resolution;
blackboard architecture;
agent roles;
agent-to-agent contracts;
collective verification;
```

и особенно важный вопрос:

```text
как получить пользу
от десятков или сотен агентов,
не превратив систему
в хаотический многоагентный чат?
```

Следующий слой будет как раз про **организованный коллективный интеллект**, где агенты не бесконечно разговаривают друг с другом, а работают через Tasks, Claims, Artifacts, Evidence, Proposals, Contracts и Events.
contents.title: Adaptive Strategy, Option Value & Sequential Decision Engine v0.1

contents.content: Продолжение

Продолжаю на русском языке. Теперь следующий слой — **Multi-Agent Coordination, Negotiation & Collective Intelligence Engine v0.1**: не «чат многих агентов», а формальная система разделения труда, передачи контекста, конкурирующих предложений, согласования, проверки и совместного выполнения задач людьми, AI-агентами, командами и внешними организациями.

# Multi-Agent Coordination, Negotiation & Collective Intelligence Engine v0.1

## 2966. Главный переход

До этого Innovation OS уже умеет:

```text
ставить цели
↓
строить стратегии
↓
создавать проекты
↓
компилировать процедуры
↓
распределять ресурсы
↓
проверять результаты
```

Но при масштабировании возникает новая проблема:

```text
одновременно существуют:
50 AI-агентов
20 людей
10 команд
15 внешних сервисов
5 организаций
```

Они не могут эффективно работать как один гигантский групповой чат.

Нужен отдельный coordination layer.

---

# 2967. Основная формула

```text
Work
↓
Decomposition
↓
Assignment
↓
Parallel Execution
↓
Structured Handoffs
↓
Conflict Detection
↓
Verification
↓
Merge
↓
Shared State Update
```

---

# 2968. Multi-Agent System ≠ множество моделей

Важно различать:

```text
MODEL
AGENT
ROLE
TASK
RESOURCE
```

Модель:

```text
GPT / local LLM / other model
```

Agent:

```text
runtime entity
with state, tools, permissions
```

Role:

```text
SCOUT
ANALYST
BUILDER
REVIEWER
```

Task:

```text
конкретная работа
```

---

# 2969. Agent не должен быть пожизненно привязан к одной роли

Один Agent instance может:

```text
Task A → SCOUT
Task B → ANALYST
```

если capability и policy позволяют.

---

# 2970. Agent Identity

Каждый Agent должен иметь:

```text
agent_id
instance_id
model/provider
package version
permissions
current roles
active tasks
```

---

# 2971. Agent ≠ Model Session

Одна model session может завершиться.

Agent identity может жить дольше:

```text
state
tasks
history
bindings
```

сохраняются отдельно.

---

# 2972. Основная проблема коллективного интеллекта

Не:

```text
как заставить 100 агентов говорить одновременно?
```

А:

```text
как разбить проблему,
кому что дать,
как объединить результат,
как обнаружить ошибки,
как не дублировать работу?
```

---

# 2973. Blackboard Architecture

Основной coordination pattern:

```text
Shared Blackboard
```

содержит:

```text
Tasks
Claims
Artifacts
Evidence
Questions
Decisions
Events
```

---

# 2974. Агенты не обязаны общаться напрямую

Agent A:

```text
публикует Artifact
```

Agent B:

```text
читает Artifact
```

Coordinator:

```text
видит state transition
```

---

# 2975. Почему это лучше гигантского чата

Chat-based coordination создаёт:

```text
context duplication
message explosion
lost decisions
unclear authority
```

Blackboard:

```text
shared structured state
```

решает значительную часть проблемы.

---

# 2976. Direct Message всё же нужен

Но только для:

```text
request
clarification
handoff
review
```

а не как основной storage.

---

# 2977. Agent Message Types

Минимально:

```text
TASK_REQUEST
TASK_ACCEPT
TASK_RESULT
QUESTION
ANSWER
REVIEW_REQUEST
REVIEW_RESULT
BLOCKER
PROPOSAL
COUNTERPROPOSAL
ESCALATION
```

---

# 2978. Message ≠ Claim

Например:

```text
Agent A:
"I think Repo X is suitable."
```

Это сообщение.

Чтобы попасть в World State:

```text
Candidate Claim
+
Evidence
```

нужны отдельно.

---

# 2979. Message ≠ Decision

Даже если Agent пишет:

```text
"Use Provider B."
```

это Proposal.

Decision возникает только через governance.

---

# 2980. Task Ownership

Каждый активный Task должен знать:

```text
OWNER
EXECUTOR
REVIEWER
```

---

# 2981. Owner ≠ Executor

Owner отвечает за достижение Task outcome.
