```text
изменения,
которое действительно способно
изменить Mission Portfolio
```

---

# 12631. После этого появится полноценный цикл:

```text
PAST
→ Ecosystem Learning

PRESENT
→ World State

FUTURE
→ Strategic Foresight
```

---

# 12632. И Innovation OS сможет работать одновременно с:

```text
историей
текущим состоянием
вариантами будущего
```

не смешивая их между собой.
contents.title: Innovation Portfolio, Program Synthesis & Mission-Oriented Planning Engine v0.1

contents.content: Да

Продолжаю. Теперь добавляем **Strategic Foresight, Horizon Scanning & Weak-Signal Intelligence Engine v0.1** — слой, который отделяет внешний шум от действительно значимых изменений и связывает слабые сигналы с Mission, сценариями, signposts и пересмотром портфеля.

# Strategic Foresight, Horizon Scanning & Weak-Signal Intelligence Engine v0.1

## 12633. Главный переход

До этого Innovation OS уже работает с:

```text id="p8mdqs"
PAST
→ Ecosystem Learning

PRESENT
→ World State

PLANNED FUTURE
→ Strategy / Portfolio
```

Теперь добавляется ещё один слой:

```text id="rz91pj"
POSSIBLE FUTURES
```

---

# 12634. Это не прогнозирование одного будущего

Ключевой принцип:

```text id="uag60v"
Forecast
≠
Future
```

---

# 12635. Система не должна строить одну линию:

```text id="9qphuf"
2026
→ 2027
→ 2028
→ 2029
```

как будто она известна.

---

# 12636. Вместо этого:

```text id="apgsmh"
Current World
↓
Signals
↓
Uncertainties
↓
Alternative Scenarios
↓
Signposts
↓
Adaptive Responses
```

---

# 12637. Strategic Foresight нужен потому, что

Mission Portfolio зависит не только от внутреннего исполнения.

---

# 12638. На него влияют:

```text id="4sfj66"
science
technology
regulation
markets
funding
supply chains
standards
talent
geopolitics
infrastructure
```

---

# 12639. Но отслеживать всё одинаково невозможно

---

# 12640. Поэтому главный вопрос:

```text id="cru3gs"
Какое внешнее изменение
имеет значение именно для нашей Mission?
```

---

# 12641. Это Mission-Relevant Foresight

---

# 12642. Общая архитектура

```text id="f5am6a"
External Sources
↓
Observation
↓
Signal Extraction
↓
Signal Validation
↓
Relevance Mapping
↓
Trend / Change Hypotheses
↓
Scenario Impact
↓
Strategic Signposts
↓
Portfolio Review
```

---

# 12643. External Observation ≠ Strategic Signal

---

# 12644. Например

```text id="h6icvd"
new GitHub repository published
```

это:

```text id="5lxfku"
Observation
```

---

# 12645. Оно становится Strategic Signal только если связано с:

```text id="em60oa"
Capability Gap
Strategic Goal
Dependency
Option
Threat
```

---

# 12646. То есть:

```text id="a78jxl"
Signal = Observation + Relevance Context
```

---

# 12647. Weak Signal

Weak Signal — ранний, ещё неустойчивый признак возможного изменения.

---

# 12648. Например:

```text id="1f1ho1"
несколько независимых research papers
+
новые repositories
+
первые hiring signals
```

могут указывать на:

```text id="jgl6op"
формирование новой technological capability
```

---

# 12649. Но это ещё не Trend Fact

---

# 12650. Поэтому weak signal хранится как:

```text id="bhxz5n"
HYPOTHESIS-supported observation cluster
```

---

# 12651. Нельзя превращать weak signal в:

```text id="nzi4ir"
"рынок уже изменился"
```

без evidence.

---

# 12652. Signal Types

Полезно различать:

```text id="4yiac5"
TECHNOLOGY
RESEARCH
MARKET
FUNDING
TALENT
REGULATION
STANDARD
SUPPLY
INFRASTRUCTURE
SECURITY
```

---

# 12653. Но это classification,

не новые Core roots.

---

# 12654. Signal object

Application model:

```python id="potkl2"
class StrategicSignal(BaseModel):
    id: UUID

    signal_type: str
    subject_ids: list[UUID]

    observation_ids: list[UUID]
    relevant_mission_ids: list[UUID]

    status: str
    confidence: float | None

    first_seen_at: datetime
    last_seen_at: datetime
```

---

# 12655. Confidence относится к Signal Claim,

не к underlying Entity.

---

# 12656. Signal Lifecycle

```text id="8x0xv7"
OBSERVED
CLUSTERING
CANDIDATE
VALIDATED
MONITORING
ESCALATED
DISMISSED
STALE
```

---

# 12657. OBSERVED

Одиночное событие.

---

# 12658. CLUSTERING

Система ищет related observations.

---

# 12659. CANDIDATE

Есть meaningful pattern.

---

# 12660. VALIDATED

Есть достаточное evidence,

что изменение реально происходит.

---

# 12661. MONITORING

Не требует action,

но signposts отслеживаются.

---

# 12662. ESCALATED

Влияние достаточно значимо для:

```text id="99dn7z"
Portfolio Review
```

---

# 12663. DISMISSED

Signal оказался:

```text id="u837kh"
noise
duplicate
irrelevant
```

---

# 12664. STALE

Signal больше не подтверждается свежими observations.

---

# 12665. Signal Provenance

Каждый signal должен отвечать:

```text id="5d64n8"
Что мы увидели?
Где?
Когда?
Какие независимые источники?
```

---

# 12666. Weak Signal без provenance

почти бесполезен.

---

# 12667. Cross-source validation

Особенно важна.

---

# 12668. Example

Research-only signal:

```text id="7zzdtf"
many papers
```

может означать:

```text id="gu89am"
academic interest
```

но не industrial adoption.

---

# 12669. GitHub-only signal:

```text id="fp965p"
many repos
```

может означать experimentation.

---

# 12670. Hiring-only signal:

```text id="cwce2j"
growing demand
```

может означать emerging operational need.

---

# 12671. Funding-only signal:

```text id="q2oh4u"
many grants
```

может reflect policy priorities.

---

# 12672. Поэтому multi-source signal сильнее.

---

# 12673. Example

```text id="mf4b40"
Research activity ↑
GitHub implementations ↑
Hiring ↑
Funding ↑
```

---

# 12674. Это может поддержать hypothesis:

```text id="ulw3me"
technology is moving
from research toward operational adoption
```

---

# 12675. Но scope/time/geography обязателен.

---

# 12676. Global trend ≠ local availability

---

# 12677. Example

Technology globally mature

но locally:

```text id="1dqagx"
no suppliers
no skills
no funding
```

---

# 12678. Поэтому Foresight Engine должен различать:

```text id="4tird0"
GLOBAL SIGNAL
REGIONAL SIGNAL
NODE-RELEVANT SIGNAL
```

---

# 12679. Geographic scope is Context.

---

# 12680. Temporal scope тоже.

---

# 12681. Signal half-life

Некоторые сигналы быстро устаревают.

---

# 12682. Example:

```text id="xv7e1a"
temporary funding call
```

имеет короткий horizon.

---

# 12683. Scientific paradigm shift:

```text id="d7sbmp"
longer horizon
```

---

# 12684. Поэтому signal freshness policy должна быть domain-specific.

---

# 12685. Horizon Classes

Можно использовать:

```text id="e7cdod"
NEAR
MID
LONG
```

---

# 12686. Например:

```text id="nmv3k3"
NEAR = months
MID = 1–3 years
LONG = 3+ years
```

но конкретные границы configurable.

---

# 12687. Не все industries имеют одинаковые horizons.

---

# 12688. Horizon Scan

Это не "прочитать новости".

---

# 12689. Это систематический процесс:

```text id="erv1aj"
Mission
↓
Strategic Unknowns
↓
Search Domains
↓
Source Portfolio
↓
Signal Collection
↓
Relevance Analysis
```

---

# 12690. Mission определяет search space.

---

# 12691. Example Mission:

```text id="so4e1e"
Build distributed robotics ecosystem
```

---

# 12692. Scan domains:

```text id="up031n"
robotics hardware
simulation
AI perception
safety standards
industrial funding
robotics talent
```

---

# 12693. Не нужно мониторить:

```text id="d39q1j"
все технологии мира
```

одинаково.

---

# 12694. Search Portfolio

Для каждой Mission:

```text id="nk6250"
priority topics
watch topics
adjacent topics
blind-spot exploration
```

---

# 12695. Priority Topics

Прямо связаны с gaps.

---

# 12696. Watch Topics

Связаны с known options/dependencies.

---

# 12697. Adjacent Topics

Могут создать unexpected alternative.

---

# 12698. Blind-Spot Exploration

Небольшая доля scanning budget для:

```text id="vtu4cr"
непредвиденных возможностей
```

---

# 12699. Это важно,

иначе система будет видеть только то, что уже ожидает.

---

# 12700. Confirmation Bias Risk

Если scanning ищет только evidence текущей strategy,

foresight becomes:

```text id="3mo9ho"
strategy confirmation engine
```

---

# 12701. Поэтому должны быть:

```text id="fuxr38"
disconfirming search queries
```

---

# 12702. Example

Current plan assumes:

```text id="32ob1q"
Technology A will dominate
```

---

# 12703. Search should also ask:

```text id="pda394"
What alternatives to A are improving?
What evidence suggests A may fail?
```

---

# 12704. This is Strategic Red Teaming.

---

# 12705. Foresight Agent Roles

```text id="vhgsft"
Horizon Scout
Signal Analyst
Trend Skeptic
Scenario Builder
Mission Relevance Analyst
Signpost Monitor
```

---

# 12706. Horizon Scout

Находит observations.

---

# 12707. Signal Analyst

Группирует.

---

# 12708. Trend Skeptic

Ищет альтернативные объяснения.

---

# 12709. Scenario Builder

Формирует possible futures.

---

# 12710. Mission Relevance Analyst

Связывает signal с:

```text id="v1vkxr"
Mission
Programs
Capabilities
Dependencies
```

---

# 12711. Signpost Monitor

Следит за conditions,

которые требуют review.

---

# 12712. Collective Foresight

Лучше:

```text id="wtew23"
несколько независимых hypotheses
```

чем одна narrative.

---

# 12713. Example

Signal:

```text id="rh6ax3"
rapid growth of small local AI models
```

---

# 12714. Hypothesis A:

```text id="czqwiv"
local inference becomes cheaper
```

---

# 12715. Hypothesis B:

```text id="k1f9za"
models improve but remain insufficient
for high-complexity tasks
```

---

# 12716. Hypothesis C:

```text id="19uwbe"
hybrid local/cloud architecture dominates
```

---

# 12717. Preserve all plausible hypotheses.

---

# 12718. Foresight ≠ consensus production

---

# 12719. Trend Hypothesis

Application representation:

```python id="0ppg1e"
class TrendHypothesis(BaseModel):
    subject_id: UUID
    signal_ids: list[UUID]

    direction: str | None
    scope_context_id: UUID
    horizon: str

    supporting_evidence_ids: list[UUID]
    refuting_evidence_ids: list[UUID]
```

---

# 12720. Trend direction examples:

```text id="6vto5l"
INCREASING
DECREASING
SHIFTING
FRAGMENTING
CONSOLIDATING
```

---

# 12721. But only when semantics appropriate.

---

# 12722. Trend ≠ Forecast

---

# 12723. Trend says:

```text id="68jkn0"
current directional pattern
```

---

# 12724. Forecast says:

```text id="metzdk"
expected future state
```

---

# 12725. Must remain separate.

---

# 12726. Forecast object

Should be Claim with:

```text id="67da92"
target variable
time horizon
range
model/method
```

---

# 12727. Example

```text id="hrmxkk"
Demand may rise 20–40%
within 12 months
```

---

# 12728. Range + method important.

---

# 12729. But for highly uncertain strategic futures,

scenario often better than numerical forecast.

---

# 12730. Scenario

Scenario is:

```text id="iy7o3h"
internally coherent possible future
```

---

# 12731. Scenario ≠ prediction

---

# 12732. Scenario object can be Context:

```text id="4h3n5m"
context_type = FUTURE_SCENARIO
```

---

# 12733. Scenario contains assumptions

```text id="1aoczo"
technology
market
funding
regulation
resources
```

---

# 12734. Example

Scenario A:

```text id="zrmbct"
Open AI Ecosystem
```

Assumptions:

```text id="bcx61m"
open models improve
open tooling matures
interoperability rises
```

---

# 12735. Scenario B:

```text id="8pnb06"
Platform Concentration
```

---

# 12736. Assumptions:

```text id="8ekhj4"
few major providers dominate
switching costs rise
```

---

# 12737. Scenario C:

```text id="e0sqmy"
Regulated Fragmentation
```

---

# 12738. Assumptions:

```text id="ey142i"
regional rules diverge
data sovereignty increases
```

---

# 12739. Не нужно выбирать "правильный" scenario

---

# 12740. Portfolio stress-tested against all.

---

# 12741. Scenario Building Pipeline

```text id="36aa5c"
Critical Uncertainties
↓
Alternative States
↓
Scenario Combinations
↓
Internal Consistency Check
↓
Mission Impact
```

---

# 12742. Critical Uncertainty

Variable that:

```text id="hbv9ye"
high impact
+
high uncertainty
```

---

# 12743. Examples:

```text id="c1xgw9"
GPU cost
regulation
talent availability
open model quality
```

---

# 12744. High Impact + Low Uncertainty

Not scenario axis,

but planning assumption.

---

# 12745. Low Impact + High Uncertainty

Usually monitor,

not build portfolio around it.

---

# 12746. Again no one formula needed.

---

# 12747. Scenario Consistency

Example impossible/contradictory combination:

```text id="lamyi5"
strict data localization
+
all compute centralized overseas
```

может быть inconsistent in context.

---

# 12748. Consistency checker flags,

human/agent reviews.

---

# 12749. Scenario Dependency Graph

Assumptions can influence each other.

---

# 12750. Example

```text id="40wq2k"
energy cost ↑
→ local GPU cost ↑
→ cloud economics shift
```

---

# 12751. This connects to Causal Engine.

---

# 12752. Causal Scenario

More sophisticated scenario includes:

```text id="8ah5jp"
causal chains
```

---

# 12753. But keep hypothesis status.

---

# 12754. Wild Cards

Rare/high-impact possibilities.

---

# 12755. Examples:

```text id="bpca3h"
major API shutdown
unexpected scientific breakthrough
supply chain disruption
```

---

# 12756. Wild Card ≠ prediction

---

# 12757. Purpose:

```text id="zh96f9"
stress resilience
```

---

# 12758. Black Swan language should be used cautiously

because true unpredictability cannot be enumerated exhaustively.

---

# 12759. Better category:

```text id="cutvv1"
LOW-PROBABILITY / HIGH-IMPACT SCENARIO
```

if probabilities are actually estimated.

---

# 12760. If no probability:

```text id="ndxlbo"
STRESS SCENARIO
```

---

# 12761. Unknown Unknowns

System cannot enumerate all.

---

# 12762. Therefore resilience/optionality remain necessary

even with strong foresight.

---

# 12763. Foresight cannot eliminate uncertainty.

---

# 12764. It improves:

```text id="4j5fr6"
preparedness
```

---

# 12765. Strategic Signpost

A signpost is observable condition indicating:

```text id="hdjsoc"
scenario becoming more/less plausible
```

или:

```text id="owq9bd"
portfolio assumption needs review
```

---

# 12766. Example

Assumption:

```text id="s8iy88"
open model performance will reach threshold
```

---

# 12767. Signpost:

```text id="iyq7yc"
benchmark X reaches Y
```

---

# 12768. Another:

```text id="mpytms"
three independent production deployments appear
```

---

# 12769. Signpost should be observable

---

# 12770. Not vague:

```text id="6b31d5"
technology becomes mature
```

---

# 12771. Better:

```text id="87fl5y"
latency < threshold
benchmark ≥ threshold
3 verified providers available
```

---

# 12772. Signpost Definition

```python id="agrz9p"
class StrategicSignpost(BaseModel):
    mission_id: UUID
    description: str

    observation_rule: dict

    related_assumption_ids: list[UUID]
    review_action: str
```

---

# 12773. Signpost state:

```text id="abpjsg"
NOT_OBSERVED
PARTIAL
OBSERVED
INVALIDATED
```

---

# 12774. Signpost OBSERVED

does not automatically execute strategic change.

---

# 12775. It triggers:

```text id="tf0cfc"
REVIEW
```

unless policy explicitly preauthorizes limited transition.

---

# 12776. This preserves governance.

---

# 12777. Condition Watch

Runtime Automation concept maps naturally.

---

# 12778. Signpost Monitor can periodically check:

```text id="jbvn9b"
future condition
```

---

# 12779. But Foresight Engine stores semantic meaning,

not just polling schedule.

---

# 12780. Example

Signpost:

```text id="i81xcp"
EU funding call opens
```

---

# 12781. Trigger:

```text id="q1k3e4"
Funding Program Review
```

---

# 12782. Another:

```text id="nslelj"
critical dependency price > threshold
```

---

# 12783. Trigger:

```text id="s0ma3z"
Provider Alternative Review
```

---

# 12784. Another:

```text id="6ht4kd"
supplier lead time > 6 months
```

---

# 12785. Trigger:

```text id="auv42h"
procurement strategy review
```

---

# 12786. Signal → Signpost distinction

Signal:

```text id="095z6u"
something seems to be changing
```

---

# 12787. Signpost:

```text id="6eq6mr"
specific observable condition
used for future decisions
```

---

# 12788. Trend → Signpost relationship

Trend hypothesis may generate:

```text id="k3qlhv"
monitoring signposts
```

---

# 12789. Example

Trend:

```text id="dqmu8x"
local AI accelerating
```

---

# 12790. Signposts:

```text id="r6d8rr"
quality threshold
hardware requirement threshold
provider count
```

---

# 12791. Mission Relevance Mapping

Every signal should map to:

```text id="z5y9kv"
Mission
Strategic Goal
Capability
Dependency
Option
```

---

# 12792. Relevance types:

```text id="cqt0l3"
ENABLES
THREATENS
ACCELERATES
DELAYS
CREATES_OPTION
CLOSES_OPTION
CHANGES_COST
CHANGES_RISK
```

---

# 12793. These may be application-level relation types.

---

# 12794. Example

Signal:

```text id="m3y4ah"
new low-cost edge GPU
```

---

# 12795. Relevance:

```text id="fyte8z"
CREATES_OPTION
for local perception stack
```

---

# 12796. Another

Signal:

```text id="bu900n"
API provider raises price
```

---

# 12797. Relevance:

```text id="zuv3dg"
CHANGES_COST
for research pipeline
```

---

# 12798. Another

Signal:

```text id="6qjqpb"
new regulation restricts data transfer
```

---

# 12799. Relevance:

```text id="069ka7"
THREATENS
cloud-dependent workflows
```

---

# 12800. Relevance must be explainable

---

# 12801. System should answer:

```text id="2myhjh"
Why are you showing me this signal?
```

---

# 12802. Example answer structure:

```text id="2ou402"
Signal affects Capability C,
which is required by Program P,
which supports Mission M.
```

---

# 12803. This prevents irrelevant technology-news feeds.

---

# 12804. Signal Impact Graph

```text id="8hp5gs"
Signal
↓
Capability
↓
Program
↓
Mission
```

---

# 12805. Could propagate impact.

---

# 12806. But propagation ≠ certainty

---

# 12807. Each edge may have:

```text id="26mkk9"
evidence
confidence
```

---

# 12808. Strategic Impact Types

```text id="mbqz6j"
LOCAL
PROGRAM
PORTFOLIO
MISSION
SYSTEMIC
```

---

# 12809. LOCAL

Affects one Project.

---

# 12810. PROGRAM

Several Projects in Program.

---

# 12811. PORTFOLIO

Changes resource/option structure.

---

# 12812. MISSION

Potentially changes mission pathway.

---

# 12813. SYSTEMIC

Affects many Missions/nodes.

---

# 12814. Systemic label should require evidence,

not sensational framing.

---

# 12815. Impact does not equal urgency

---

# 12816. Some high-impact changes have:

```text id="vpmwla"
long lead time
```

---

# 12817. Urgency dimensions:

```text id="w6q3i0"
time window
reversibility
decision lead time
```

---

# 12818. Example

New standard announced,

effective in 24 months.

---

# 12819. High impact,

moderate immediate urgency.

---

# 12820. Another

Funding deadline in 10 days.

---

# 12821. Lower structural impact,

high time urgency.

---

# 12822. Keep dimensions separate.

---

# 12823. Signal Prioritization

Could use Pareto dimensions:

```text id="gug5ku"
mission relevance
impact scope
time sensitivity
evidence strength
novelty
```

---

# 12824. Avoid one opaque priority score initially.

---

# 12825. Novelty

Signal should distinguish:

```text id="2rc5gu"
new observation
```

from:

```text id="fuvjgd"
known condition repeated
```

---

# 12826. Duplicate signals should consolidate.

---

# 12827. But recurrence can strengthen trend evidence.

---

# 12828. Signal Memory

Need remember:

```text id="g22835"
we saw this before
```

---

# 12829. Example

Repository was evaluated 6 months ago.

---

# 12830. New signal only meaningful if:

```text id="23grg7"
version changed materially
benchmark improved
license changed
```

---

# 12831. This prevents repeated rediscovery.

---

# 12832. Signal Change Detection

Compare:

```text id="4y1j72"
current observation
vs
previous known state
```

---

# 12833. Emit:

```text id="8vj8p4"
NEW
UPDATED
REVERSED
UNCHANGED
```

---

# 12834. Strategic intelligence should emphasize:

```text id="h39b3e"
what changed
```

---

# 12835. Not repeat full known background.

---

# 12836. Weak Signal Clustering

Observations may use different language.

---

# 12837. Example:

```text id="h6tsoe"
embodied foundation models
robot foundation models
vision-language-action models
```

---

# 12838. Semantic clustering can connect,

```text id="c9l25q"
Что требует решения?
```

---

# 14050. Для AI Agent он отвечает:

```text id="2qbnlv"
What is current state?
What may I act on?
What is blocked?
What evidence is missing?
```

---

# 14051. Для руководителя Program:

```text id="rgkzgu"
Where is capability progress blocked?
```

---

# 14052. Для инженера:

```text id="y358lr"
Which technical dependency failed?
```

---

# 14053. Для исследователя:

```text id="kz4g4t"
Which critical Claims remain unresolved?
```

---

# 14054. Для аудитора:

```text id="01dmjv"
Who authorized this change and why?
```

---

# 14055. Это превращает множество подсистем

в:

```text id="r8txyk"
одну наблюдаемую операционную среду
```

---

# 14056. Следующий фундаментальный слой

После появления Command Center становится возможен следующий шаг:

> **не просто наблюдать отдельные подсистемы, а формально описать весь жизненный цикл данных и информации — от сырого сигнала, файла, сообщения или сенсора до Observation, Claim, Evidence, Knowledge, Decision и Action.**

---

# 14057. Следующий логичный модуль:

# **Universal Data, Perception & Evidence Fabric v0.1**

Он объединит:

```text id="fuuevg"
Files
Documents
Web
Databases
APIs
Sensors
Cameras
Audio
Telemetry
Human Input
```

в единый pipeline:

```text id="wtf11y"
Raw Input
↓
Parsing
↓
Observation
↓
Entity Resolution
↓
Semantic Extraction
↓
Claim
↓
Evidence
↓
Verification
↓
World State
```

---

# 14058. Это особенно важно для ранних идей о:

```text id="q37dbu"
миллионах камер
роботах
оптоволоконных сенсорах
документах
GitHub
научных статьях
ERP/API
```

---

# 14059. Вместо отдельных ingestion-систем для каждого источника появится:

```text id="230rvw"
Universal Perception Fabric
```

---

# 14060. И система сможет одинаково строго различать:

```text id="3v6b2h"
что было получено
что было распознано
что было предположено
что было проверено
```

независимо от того, пришла информация из PDF, камеры, датчика, API, человека или AI-модели.
contents.title: System-Wide Observability, Explainability & Operational Command Center v0.1

contents.content: Да

Продолжаю с **14061**. Теперь строим слой, который унифицирует документы, API, базы данных, сенсоры, камеры, аудио, телеметрию и человеческий ввод в одну доказательную цепочку — от сырого сигнала до проверенного состояния мира.

# Universal Data, Perception & Evidence Fabric v0.1

## 14061. Главный переход

До сих пор разные Observatory и Runtime-модули получали данные разными путями:

```text
HN posts
GitHub repositories
Research papers
Funding calls
Runtime telemetry
Physical sensors
Human input
```

Теперь нужен единый принцип:

```text
Любой внешний вход
должен пройти
явную цепочку преобразований
до World State.
```

---

# 14062. Основная архитектурная формула

```text
RAW
↓
PARSED
↓
OBSERVED
↓
RESOLVED
↓
INTERPRETED
↓
CLAIMED
↓
EVIDENCED
↓
VERIFIED
↓
WORLD STATE
```

---

# 14063. Ключевой invariant

```text
Raw Input ≠ Fact
```

---

# 14064. Ещё один

```text
Parsed Data ≠ Observation
```

---

# 14065. Ещё один

```text
Observation ≠ Interpretation
```

---

# 14066.

```text
Interpretation ≠ Verified Claim
```

---

# 14067. Это должно работать одинаково для:

```text
PDF
web page
API response
database row
camera frame
microphone signal
pressure sensor
human statement
AI output
```

---

# 14068. Таким образом вместо десятков отдельных ingestion philosophies появляется:

# Universal Perception Fabric

---

# 14069. Но "perception" здесь используется широко

Не только:

```text
computer vision
```

а:

```text
machine acquisition of externally supplied information
```

---

# 14070. Поэтому лучшее полное название:

# Universal Data, Perception & Evidence Fabric

---

# 14071. Source Layer

Первый уровень:

```text
SOURCE
```

---

# 14072. Source может быть:

```text
FILE
WEB
API
DATABASE
MESSAGE
SENSOR
CAMERA
AUDIO
VIDEO
HUMAN
AGENT
DEVICE
```

---

# 14073. Но Source не обязательно новый Resource subtype для каждого случая

---

# 14074. Например:

```text
camera
```

может быть RESOURCE.

А конкретный frame:

```text
ARTIFACT / raw observation input
```

---

# 14075. API provider:

```text
RESOURCE
```

API response:

```text
ARTIFACT / RawSource snapshot
```

---

# 14076. Document source

Например PDF:

```text
Artifact
```

---

# 14077. Его конкретная ingestion version должна быть immutable snapshot

---

# 14078. Source Snapshot

Минимум:

```text
source identity
retrieval time
content hash
media type
provenance
```

---

# 14079. Example

```yaml
source:
  type: web
  uri: ...
  retrieved_at: ...
  sha256: ...
```

---

# 14080. Для API

Также:

```text
request parameters
endpoint version
response status
```

---

# 14081. Для sensor input

Также:

```text
sensor_id
timestamp
sampling rate
unit
calibration context
```

---

# 14082. Для human input

Также:

```text
author/resource identity
time
communication context
```

если это допустимо и необходимо.

---

# 14083. Source Snapshot нужен потому, что внешний источник может измениться

---

# 14084. Web page сегодня:

```text
Version A
```

завтра:

```text
Version B
```

---

# 14085. Без snapshot невозможно ответить:

```text
На основании чего система сделала вывод вчера?
```

---

# 14086. Но хранить полную копию каждого источника можно не всегда

Из-за:

```text
license
copyright
privacy
storage
```

---

# 14087. Поэтому Snapshot Policy configurable

---

# 14088. Возможные режимы:

```text
FULL
METADATA_ONLY
HASH_ONLY
EXCERPT
EXTERNAL_REFERENCE
```

---

# 14089. FULL

Храним допустимую полную копию.

---

# 14090. METADATA_ONLY

Храним описание и ссылку.

---

# 14091. HASH_ONLY

Доказываем, какой объект был обработан,

но не сохраняем содержимое.

---

# 14092. EXCERPT

Храним ограниченный разрешённый фрагмент.

---

# 14093. EXTERNAL_REFERENCE

Содержимое остаётся во внешней системе.

---

# 14094. Provenance должна сохраняться независимо от режима.

---

# 14095. Acquisition Layer

Следующий этап:

```text
Acquire
```

---

# 14096. Acquisition отвечает:

```text
получили ли мы данные корректно?
```

---

# 14097. Не:

```text
правдивы ли они?
```

---

# 14098. Example

HTTP 200 и валидный JSON означает:

```text
acquisition success
```

---

# 14099. Но содержимое может быть:

```text
wrong
stale
malicious
```

---

# 14100. Поэтому ingestion success ≠ epistemic success.

---

# 14101. Acquisition Result

```python
class AcquisitionResult(BaseModel):
    source_ref: str
    status: str
    content_hash: str | None
    retrieved_at: datetime
    artifact_id: UUID | None
```

---

# 14102. Acquisition statuses

```text
SUCCESS
PARTIAL
FAILED
DENIED
UNAVAILABLE
```

---

# 14103. PARTIAL

Например:

```text
PDF downloaded
but embedded attachments unavailable
```

---

# 14104. DENIED

Permission/access policy prevented retrieval.

---

# 14105. UNAVAILABLE

Source unreachable.

---

# 14106. Again:

```text
UNAVAILABLE ≠ nonexistent
```

---

# 14107. Parsing Layer

Raw content becomes structured representation.

---

# 14108. Example PDF

```text
PDF bytes
↓
text blocks
tables
images
metadata
```

---

# 14109. Example HTML

```text
HTML
↓
main content
headings
links
metadata
```

---

# 14110. Example sensor stream

```text
raw signal
↓
samples
windows
features
```

---

# 14111. Parsing Output remains:

```text
Artifact
```

---

# 14112. Parsed artifact is not canonical fact.

---

# 14113. Example parser error

PDF contains:

```text
1,000
```

Parser outputs:

```text
1000
```

Fine.

Но если table alignment broken:

```text
10
```

may attach to wrong row.

---

# 14114. Therefore parser confidence/quality can matter.

---

# 14115. Parser Metadata

```text
parser
version
input artifact
output artifact
warnings
```

---

# 14116. This allows reproducibility.

---

# 14117. Multiple parser outputs may coexist

---

# 14118. Example

PDF parsed by:

```text
Parser A
Parser B
```

---

# 14119. If results disagree:

```text
Parsing Conflict
```

---

# 14120. Can trigger:

```text
human/secondary verification
```

---

# 14121. Media-aware parsing

Different media require different adapters.

---

# 14122. Text:

```text
token/section/span extraction
```

---

# 14123. Image:

```text
objects
regions
text
geometry
```

---

# 14124. Audio:

```text
segments
speaker labels if appropriate
transcript
acoustic events
```

---

# 14125. Video:

```text
frames
tracks
temporal events
```

---

# 14126. Sensor:

```text
time-series
events
features
```

---

# 14127. But parsed representation should retain reference to original modality.

---

# 14128. Example

Visual claim:

```text
object at coordinates x,y
```

should be traceable to:

```text
frame/time/region
```

---

# 14129. Source Span generalization

Для текста:

```text
page
line
span
```

---

# 14130. Для image:

```text
bounding box
```

---

# 14131. Для video:

```text
time interval
track
frame range
```

---

# 14132. Для audio:

```text
time interval
```

---

# 14133. Для sensor:

```text
sample/time window
```

---

# 14134. Это можно назвать:

# Evidence Locator

---

# 14135. Generic locator

```python
class EvidenceLocator(BaseModel):
    artifact_id: UUID
    locator_type: str
    locator_data: dict
```

---

# 14136. Locator types:

```text
TEXT_SPAN
PAGE_REGION
IMAGE_REGION
TIME_RANGE
SAMPLE_RANGE
ROW_RANGE
JSON_PATH
```

---

# 14137. Это очень важно для multimodal provenance.

---

# 14138. Observation Layer

Теперь из parsed data извлекается:

```text
Observation
```

---

# 14139. Observation означает:

```text
система зафиксировала некоторый наблюдаемый сигнал
```

---

# 14140. Например camera:

```text
red object detected at region R
```

---

# 14141. Это ещё не:

```text
"это аварийный огнетушитель"
```

---

# 14142. Sensor:

```text
pressure = 312 kPa
```

---

# 14143. Это Observation.

---

# 14144. Interpretation:

```text
pressure exceeds operating threshold
```

---

# 14145. Claim:

```text
System X is operating outside normal pressure range
```

---

# 14146. Verification may require:

```text
second sensor
calibration
rules
```

---

# 14147. Это separation of levels.

---

# 14148. Observation representation

Core root EVENT может использоваться для temporal observation,

или Claim with source_mode=OBSERVED,

depending semantics.

---

# 14149. Recommended distinction

Use:

```text
Event
```

for:

```text
something occurred at time T
```

---

# 14150. Use Claim with:

```text
source_mode = OBSERVED
```

for:

```text
structured assertion derived directly from observation
```

---

# 14151. Example

Event:

```text
sensor reading received
```

Claim:

```text
temperature = 82°C at T
```

---

# 14152. This preserves both transport and semantic state.

---

# 14153. Observation confidence

Sensors and models can be uncertain.

---

# 14154. Example vision model:

```text
forklift probability 0.82
```

---

# 14155. This does not mean:

```text
82% true
```

in a universal epistemic sense.

---

# 14156. It is model confidence under its calibration context.

---

# 14157. Therefore metadata should identify:

```text
model
version
calibration
threshold
```

---

# 14158. Sensor uncertainty similarly:

```text
measurement tolerance
```

---

# 14159. Units mandatory

```text
°C
Pa
mm
m/s
```

---

# 14160. Numeric observation without unit is incomplete if unit matters.

---

# 14161. Unit normalization

Input:

```text
5 bar
```

canonical:

```text
500 kPa
```

---

# 14162. But original unit should remain in provenance.

---

# 14163. Conversion procedure versioned.

---

# 14164. Time Synchronization

Multisensor perception requires:

```text
consistent timestamps
```

---

# 14165. Sources may have:

```text
device time
server receipt time
event time
```

---

# 14166. Distinguish:

```text
observed_at
received_at
processed_at
```

---

# 14167. Especially important for distributed physical systems.

---

# 14168. Clock skew

Could cause:

```text
false event ordering
```

---

# 14169. Need:

```text
clock quality metadata
```

where relevant.

---

# 14170. For ordinary documents this complexity not needed.

---

# 14171. Fabric should be modality-aware,

not force all sources to carry sensor-grade fields.

---

# 14172. Entity Resolution Layer

Observation often mentions:

```text
something
```

that must map to canonical entity.

---

# 14173. Example document:

```text
OpenAI
```

---

# 14174. Entity Resolver maps to:

```text
Resource UUID
```

---

# 14175. Camera:

```text
vehicle track 183
```

may map to:

```text
Forklift Resource UUID
```

---

# 14176. RFID:

```text
tag ABC123
```

maps to asset.

---

# 14177. Human says:

```text
the north pump
```

Resolver may map to physical Resource.

---

# 14178. Entity Resolution states

```text
EXACT
CONFIRMED
CANDIDATE
AMBIGUOUS
UNRESOLVED
```

---

# 14179. UNKNOWN identity ≠ guessed identity.

---

# 14180. Never silently merge ambiguous entities.

---

# 14181. Cross-modal Entity Resolution

Interesting case:

```text
camera object
+
RFID signal
+
database record
```

may refer to same physical asset.

---

# 14182. Fusion can propose:

```text
same entity
```

---

# 14183. But should store:

```text
mapping evidence
```

---

# 14184. Identity confidence separate from content confidence.

---

# 14185. Example

We are highly confident:

```text
pressure reading = 312 kPa
```

but unsure:

```text
which pump produced it
```

---

# 14186. Need represent independently.

---

# 14187. Semantic Extraction Layer

Once source/object context known,

extract:

```text
entities
relations
claims
constraints
events
```

---

# 14188. For text,

LLM may help.

---

# 14189. For sensor data,

rules/ML models may help.

---

# 14190. For structured API,

deterministic mapping preferred.

---

# 14191. Principle:

```text
Use deterministic transformation
when semantics are already explicit.
```

---

# 14192. Example

API returns:

```json
{"temperature_c": 82}
```

No LLM needed.

---

# 14193. Example research paragraph:

```text
The method improved recall by 12%...
```

LLM/parser may extract claim.

---

# 14194. Extraction Adapter

Generic interface:

```python
class SemanticExtractor(Protocol):
    async def extract(
        self,
        artifact: Artifact,
        context: Context
    ) -> ExtractionResult:
        ...
```

---

# 14195. Extraction Result

```text
Candidate Entities
Candidate Claims
Candidate Relations
Unknowns
Warnings
```

---

# 14196. Candidate is critical word.

---

# 14197. Extraction does not directly write canonical truth.

---

# 14198. Promotion Pipeline remains:

```text
Candidate
↓
Schema Validation
↓
Semantic Validation
↓
Policy
↓
Canonical Object
```

---

# 14199. Multimodal Fusion

Now multiple observations can support one Claim.

---

# 14200. Example robot gripper

Inputs:

```text
camera
force sensor
joint encoder
optical tactile fiber
```

---

# 14201. Camera says:

```text
object moved
```

---

# 14202. Force sensor says:

```text
contact force increased
```

---

# 14203. Joint encoder says:

```text
gripper closed 3 mm
```

---

# 14204. Optical sensor says:

```text
localized pressure distribution changed
```

---

# 14205. Fusion hypothesis:

```text
object is being grasped
```

---

# 14206. That is not raw observation.

---

# 14207. It is:

```text
INFERENCE
```

supported by multiple observations.

---

# 14208. This is exactly where tactile sensing ideas integrate.

---

# 14209. Sensor Fusion Graph

```text
Observation A
Observation B
Observation C
↓
Inference Claim
```

---

# 14210. If one sensor disagrees:

```text
conflict preserved
```

---

# 14211. Example

Vision:

```text
object stationary
```

Encoder:

```text
motion detected
```

---

# 14212. Could indicate:

```text
slippage
sensor lag
misclassification
```

---

# 14213. Do not average disagreement away blindly.

---

# 14214. Fusion Strategy Types

```text
RULE
STATISTICAL
ML
CAUSAL
HYBRID
```

---

# 14215. Fusion Procedure itself versioned.

---

# 14216. Multimodal Evidence

One Claim may have Evidence from:

```text
document
sensor
camera
human
simulation
```

---

# 14217. Evidence types remain explicit.

---

# 14218. Example

Claim:

```text
machine vibration abnormal
```

Evidence:

```text
accelerometer
audio spectrum
maintenance log
```

---

# 14219. Cross-modal agreement can strengthen evidence.

---

# 14220. But correlated sensors may share same failure mode.

---

# 14221. Example

Two software-derived signals from same camera

are not fully independent.

---

# 14222. Evidence Independence Graph useful.

---

# 14223. Observation Dependency

Track:

```text
derived_from sensor/device/source
```

---

# 14224. Example

Vision model A and B both process same frame.

---

# 14225. Two model outputs ≠ two independent physical observations.

---

# 14226. This mirrors source independence logic in Foresight.

---

# 14227. Data Quality Layer

Before semantic promotion evaluate:

```text
completeness
validity
freshness
consistency
```

---

# 14228. But avoid one Data Quality Score.

---

# 14229. Better dimensions separately.

---

# 14230. Example

Dataset:

```text
complete: high
freshness: low
schema validity: high
```

---

# 14231. Different use cases care differently.

---

# 14232. Data Quality Claim

Could be contextual.

---

# 14233. Example

```text
Dataset suitable for historical analysis
```

but:

```text
not suitable for live control
```

---

# 14234. Same data,

different fitness-for-use.

---

# 14235. Fitness-for-Use

Important concept.

---

# 14236. Data is not simply:

```text
good/bad
```

---

# 14237. It may be:

```text
adequate for task A
insufficient for task B
```

---

# 14238. Therefore task requirements should specify:

```text
freshness
precision
coverage
resolution
```

---

# 14239. Perception Capability Contract

Example:

```yaml
capability: vehicle_position_tracking

requirements:
  update_rate_hz: 5
  max_position_error_m: 0.5
  max_data_age_ms: 500
```

---

# 14240. Then current sensor system can be checked.

---

# 14241. If update rate 1 Hz:

```text
capability insufficient
```

even if sensor technically works.

---

# 14242. This connects Data Fabric with Capability Engine.

---

# 14243. Perception Gap

Derived when:

```text
World State needs observation
but sensing/data coverage insufficient
```

---

# 14244. Types:

```text
NO_SOURCE
LOW_FREQUENCY
LOW_PRECISION
STALE
BLIND_AREA
IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED
```

---

# 14245. Example factory

Robot path planner needs:

```text
current human occupancy
```

---

# 14246. Camera coverage blind zone exists.

---

# 14247. This is:

```text
Perception Gap
```

---

# 14248. Not planning bug.

---

# 14249. World model should explicitly know:

```text
area state UNKNOWN
```

---

# 14250. UNKNOWN must influence control policy.

---

# 14251. Example safety policy:

```text
if occupancy UNKNOWN
→ restrict autonomous movement
```

---

# 14252. This is much safer than treating UNKNOWN as empty.

---

# 14253. Critical invariant

```text
Not observed
≠
Absent.
```

---

# 14254. This applies everywhere:

```text
camera
database
web
human reports
```

---

# 14255. Example

No job posting for skill X

does not mean:

```text
no demand exists
```

---

# 14256. Example

No sensor detection

does not necessarily mean:

```text
no object exists
```

---

# 14257. Coverage metadata is therefore essential.

---

# 14258. Observation Coverage

For sensor domain:

```text
spatial
temporal
modal
```

---

# 14259. For web/research:

```text
source
language
geography
time
```

---

# 14260. Same abstract concept:

# Coverage

---

# 14261. Universal Coverage Model

Could describe:

```text
What part of target domain
can this source observe?
```

---

# 14262. Example camera:

```text
polygon + field of view
```

---

# 14263. Research database:

```text
disciplines + publishers + years
```

---

# 14264. GitHub:

```text
public repositories reachable via API
```

---

# 14265. Human observer:

```text
declared/local scope
```

---

# 14266. This lets system reason about blind spots systematically.

---

# 14267. Data Lineage

Every derived object should support:

```text
Where did this come from?
```

---

# 14268. Example:

```text
Mission dashboard metric
```

might derive from:

```text
Projects
→ Actions
→ sensor/API observations
```

---

# 14269. Lineage Graph

```text
Raw Source
↓
Parsed Artifact
↓
Observation
↓
Claim
↓
Derived View
```

---

# 14270. This is universal data lineage.

---

# 14271. Lineage differs from Evidence Graph

---

# 14272. Data lineage says:

```text
how data transformed
```

---

# 14273. Evidence graph says:

```text
what supports/refutes a Claim
```

# 14848. Options:

```text
query database
search paper
ask expert
run experiment
measure sensor
```

---

# 14849. This is universal evidence acquisition.

---

# 14850. Evidence Acquisition Planner

Input:

```text
Unknown Claim
```

---

# 14851. Output:

```text
possible observation/evidence actions
```

---

# 14852. Compare:

```text
cost
time
expected information value
```

---

# 14853. This connects directly to VOI.

---

# 14854. Example

Need know:

```text
whether machine supports protocol X
```

---

# 14855. Options:

```text
read manual
query device
contact vendor
test connection
```

---

# 14856. Different evidence strengths/costs.

---

# 14857. System can recommend acquisition path.

---

# 14858. But high-impact physical experiment may require approval.

---

# 14859. Observation as Action

Some observations are passive:

```text
read API
```

---

# 14860. Others require active intervention:

```text
send test signal
open machine
run experiment
```

---

# 14861. Active measurement can affect system.

---

# 14862. Therefore classify:

```text
PASSIVE_OBSERVATION
ACTIVE_MEASUREMENT
EXPERIMENT
```

---

# 14863. Active measurement goes through action governance.

---

# 14864. Example network probe

may have side effects.

---

# 14865. Example physical tensile test

destroys sample.

---

# 14866. Thus:

```text
measurement ≠ always read-only
```

---

# 14867. This is an important architectural nuance.

---

# 14868. Destructive Testing

Procedure should mark:

```text
IRREVERSIBLE
```

---

# 14869. Sample consumption tracked in Resource Economy.

---

# 14870. Measurement produces Evidence Artifact.

---

# 14871. Instrument Digital Twin

Instrument Resource can expose:

```text
measurement capabilities
calibration
availability
```

---

# 14872. User can ask:

```text
Where can we measure property X?
```

---

# 14873. Capability Resolver returns labs/instruments.

---

# 14874. Then booking/execution produces Evidence.

---

# 14875. This closes virtual-to-physical scientific loop.

---

# 14876. Data Fabric and Scientific Method

Research cycle:

```text
Hypothesis
↓
Measurement Plan
↓
Data
↓
Observation
↓
Analysis
↓
Evidence
↓
Claim Update
```

---

# 14877. Same Fabric supports this natively.

---

# 14878. Experiment Dataset

Should link:

```text
experiment Action
instrument
procedure
raw data
processed data
```

---

# 14879. This makes reproducibility much stronger.

---

# 14880. Analysis code itself:

```text
Artifact/Software Resource
```

---

# 14881. Derived plot:

```text
Artifact
```

---

# 14882. Conclusion:

```text
Claim
```

---

# 14883. This clear separation is excellent for science.

---

# 14884. Data Fabric and Legal/Humanities Documents

Same principles work.

---

# 14885. Example legal document:

```text
PDF
↓
paragraphs
↓
legal propositions
↓
citations
↓
Claims
```

---

# 14886. But interpretation:

```text
legal conclusion
```

should remain inference/context-specific.

---

# 14887. Example humanities corpus:

```text
texts
↓
themes
↓
interpretive Claims
```

---

# 14888. Evidence semantics differ,

but core still usable.

---

# 14889. Thus Universal Fabric spans:

```text
natural sciences
engineering
social sciences
law
humanities
operations
```

---

# 14890. It doesn't force same verification method.

---

# 14891. Verification Profile defines domain method.

---

# 14892. Data Fabric vs Ontology

Data Fabric does not decide ontology truth.

---

# 14893. It maps inputs into candidate semantic structures.

---

# 14894. Ontology Engine/Review governs concept mappings.

---

# 14895. This prevents ingestion from silently redefining vocabulary.

---

# 14896. Example new external term:

```text
agentic workflow
```

---

# 14897. Extractor may propose mapping to existing Concept.

---

# 14898. If ambiguous:

```text
Capability Proposal Queue
```

---

# 14899. Do not automatically create thousands of near-duplicate concepts.

---

# 14900. Terminology Observatory

Could detect emerging terms.

---

# 14901. Foresight may use:

```text
new vocabulary frequency
```

as weak signal.

---

# 14902. But term frequency ≠ technology maturity.

---

# 14903. Again Data Fabric supplies observations,

Foresight interprets.

---

# 14904. Data Fabric and Search

Unified search can operate across:

```text
raw artifacts
semantic objects
```

---

# 14905. But results should identify layer.

---

# 14906. Example search result:

```text
Document
Claim
Concept
Observation
```

---

# 14907. User should know whether result is:

```text
source material
```

or:

```text
canonical semantic knowledge
```

---

# 14908. Search ranking should not mix without labels.

---

# 14909. Retrieval for Agents

Agent context builder should prefer:

```text
canonical Claims
+
supporting source excerpts
```

---

# 14910. Not dump raw data by default.

---

# 14911. But for extraction/research tasks,

raw artifacts may be required.

---

# 14912. Context Builder decides by task.

---

# 14913. This reduces token/attention load.

---

# 14914. Evidence-aware RAG

Retrieval pipeline:

```text
Query
↓
Semantic objects
↓
Claims
↓
Evidence
↓
Source spans
```

---

# 14915. Better than:

```text
nearest text chunks only
```

---

# 14916. Vector retrieval still useful,

but as candidate generation.

---

# 14917. Then semantic/evidence filters.

---

# 14918. This is more reliable for long-lived knowledge systems.

---

# 14919. Claim-Centric Retrieval

User asks:

```text
Does technology X support Y?
```

---

# 14920. Retrieve:

```text
Claims about X PROVIDES Y
```

---

# 14921. Then Evidence.

---

# 14922. Not merely paragraphs mentioning X and Y.

---

# 14923. This is a major architecture advantage.

---

# 14924. Observation-Centric Retrieval

User asks:

```text
What happened to machine X yesterday?
```

---

# 14925. Retrieve:

```text
Events/observations
```

---

# 14926. Different query path.

---

# 14927. Artifact-Centric Retrieval

User asks:

```text
Show original report
```

---

# 14928. Retrieve Artifact.

---

# 14929. Query intent matters.

---

# 14930. Universal Data API

Potential endpoints:

```text
POST /api/v1/sources
```

---

# 14931.

```text
POST /api/v1/ingestion/jobs
```

---

# 14932.

```text
GET /api/v1/ingestion/jobs/{id}
```

---

# 14933.

```text
GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/lineage
```

---

# 14934.

```text
GET /api/v1/claims/{id}/evidence
```

---

# 14935.

```text
GET /api/v1/coverage
```

---

# 14936.

```text
GET /api/v1/perception/gaps
```

---

# 14937.

```text
POST /api/v1/evidence/acquire
```

---

# 14938.

```text
GET /api/v1/conflicts
```

---

# 14939. Streaming endpoint:

```text
POST /api/v1/observations
```

for controlled ingest,

though high-throughput streams may use dedicated broker gateway later.

---

# 14940. CLI

```text
inno source add
```

---

# 14941.

```text
inno ingest run <source>
```

---

# 14942.

```text
inno lineage <artifact>
```

---

# 14943.

```text
inno evidence show <claim>
```

---

# 14944.

```text
inno coverage
```

---

# 14945.

```text
inno perception gaps
```

---

# 14946.

```text
inno conflicts
```

---

# 14947. Worker Commands

```text
SOURCE_ACQUIRE
PARSE_ARTIFACT
SEMANTIC_EXTRACT
ENTITY_RESOLVE
EVIDENCE_PROMOTE
CONFLICT_DETECT
COVERAGE_REFRESH
```

---

# 14948. Storage Blueprint

```text
PostgreSQL
  semantic metadata
  claims
  provenance
  source indexes

Object Store
  files
  media
  large datasets

Time-Series Store
  dense telemetry

Search/Vector Index
  derived retrieval
```

---

# 14949. Kafka/stream broker not required for MVP

---

# 14950. Initial streaming can use:

```text
PostgreSQL
worker queue
HTTP/webhook ingestion
```

---

# 14951. Add dedicated streaming infrastructure only when volume requires.

---

# 14952. This follows earlier principle:

```text
simple infrastructure
strong semantics
```

---

# 14953. MVP Scope

Do not begin with millions of cameras.

---

# 14954. First MVP sources:

```text
Web/HTML
PDF
GitHub/API
manual JSON
```

---

# 14955. Then add one physical sensor source.

---

# 14956. Good demonstration:

```text
temperature sensor
```

---

# 14957. Full path:

```text
sensor reading
↓
Observation
↓
Claim
↓
Threshold verification
↓
Capability/state update
↓
Command Center
```

---

# 14958. Second physical demonstration:

```text
camera object detection
```

---

# 14959. But output only:

```text
object presence
```

not complex person identification.

---

# 14960. Third:

```text
tactile/pressure simulation data
```

for robot sensor pipeline.

---

# 14961. This validates multimodal architecture without premature scale.

---

# 14962. MVP Feature 1

# RawSource + Artifact Lineage

---

# 14963. Feature 2

# Evidence Locator

for:

```text
text span
JSON path
time range
```

---

# 14964. Feature 3

# Candidate Claim Promotion

---

# 14965. Feature 4

# Entity Resolution Queue

---

# 14966. Feature 5

# Conflict View

---

# 14967. Feature 6

# Coverage/Unknown View

---

# 14968. Feature 7

# One sensor ingestion path

---

# 14969. Feature 8

# Evidence-aware retrieval

---

# 14970. DoD 1

PDF ingested.

Claim can be traced back to:

```text
page/span
```

---

# 14971. DoD 2

GitHub API data ingested.

Repository Resource maintains:

```text
external GitHub identity
```

---

# 14972. DoD 3

Same source reingested unchanged.

No semantic duplicates.

---

# 14973. DoD 4

Changed source creates new snapshot.

---

# 14974. DoD 5

Conflicting Claims coexist.

---

# 14975. DoD 6

UNKNOWN remains UNKNOWN.

---

# 14976. DoD 7

Simulation data never enters BASE_WORLD as observed truth.

---

# 14977. DoD 8

Restricted source cannot leak through public summary.

---

# 14978. DoD 9

Incoming document cannot execute instructions.

---

# 14979. DoD 10

Source outage marks:

```text
observation capability degraded
```

not domain absence.

---

# 14980. DoD 11

Late observation correctly placed in temporal history.

---

# 14981. DoD 12

Evidence independence is not inflated by derived copies.

---

# 14982. DoD 13

Physical observation has unit and timestamp.

---

# 14983. DoD 14

Calibration state influences measurement assurance.

---

# 14984. DoD 15

Evidence acquisition can create Task/Experiment.

---

# 14985. Architecture Invariants

```text
Raw Input ≠ Fact.
```

---

# 14986.

```text
Parsed Data ≠ Observation.
```

---

# 14987.

```text
Observation ≠ Interpretation.
```

---

# 14988.

```text
Interpretation ≠ Verification.
```

---

# 14989.

```text
Not Observed ≠ Absent.
```

---

# 14990.

```text
Unavailable Source ≠ Nonexistent Object.
```

---

# 14991.

```text
Two Derived Reports ≠ Two Independent Sources.
```

---

# 14992.

```text
Simulation ≠ Observation.
```

---

# 14993.

```text
Synthetic Data ≠ Real-World Evidence.
```

---

# 14994.

```text
Data Content ≠ Command.
```

---

# 14995.

```text
Source Signature ≠ Truth.
```

---

# 14996.

```text
Installed Sensor ≠ Verified Perception Capability.
```

---

# 14997.

```text
Data Availability ≠ Data Freshness.
```

---

# 14998.

```text
Data Completeness ≠ Fitness for Every Task.
```

---

# 14999.

```text
Transferred Data ≠ Transferred Knowledge.
```

---

# 15000. Ещё один большой архитектурный рубеж

К **15000** сформировалась полная цепочка:

```text
WORLD
↓
SENSING / DATA ACQUISITION
↓
OBSERVATION
↓
SEMANTIC INTERPRETATION
↓
CLAIMS
↓
EVIDENCE
↓
WORLD MODEL
↓
REASONING
↓
DECISION
↓
ACTION
↓
NEW OBSERVATION
```

---

# 15001. Это уже замкнутая cyber-physical-information architecture

---

# 15002. Причём один и тот же принцип работает для:

```text
GitHub repository
scientific article
grant
job posting
camera
pressure sensor
robot
ERP database
human message
```

---

# 15003. Разница находится на периферии:

```text
adapter
parser
extractor
verification
```

---

# 15004. Core остаётся одинаковым.

---

# 15005. Это серьёзно упрощает расширение Innovation OS

---

# 15006. Новый источник не требует:

```text
новой независимой информационной системы
```

---

# 15007. Требуется:

```text
Source Adapter
+
Semantic Mapping
+
Verification Profile
```

---

# 15008. Затем он сразу получает:

```text
provenance
evidence
conflict handling
world integration
command-center visibility
```

---

# 15009. Именно это превращает набор интеграций в:

# Information Operating Fabric

---

# 15010. И одновременно создаёт мост между:

```text
Internet information
Enterprise information
Scientific information
Physical world sensing
```

---

# 15011. Следующий фундаментальный вопрос

После появления Universal Data & Perception Fabric становится очевидно, что в системе будут:

```text
миллионы объектов
миллиарды observations
тысячи агентов
множество независимых узлов
```

И возникает следующая проблема:

> **как распространять вычисление, хранение, reasoning и agent execution по множеству машин, edge-узлов, облаков, лабораторий и организаций так, чтобы объекты сохраняли идентичность, состояние и causal/provenance связь независимо от физического расположения вычислений?**

---

# 15012. Следующий логичный модуль:

# **Distributed Semantic Compute, Edge Intelligence & Execution Fabric v0.1**

Он объединит:

```text
Cloud
Edge
Local Devices
GPU Nodes
Lab Computers
Robots
Federated Organizations
AI Agents
```

---

# 15013. Его центральный вопрос:

```text
Где должен выполняться каждый Action?
```

---

# 15014. Не просто:

```text
на каком сервере есть CPU
```

а:

```text
где находятся данные?
где разрешена обработка?
где есть нужная capability?
какая latency допустима?
какая стоимость?
какие hardware requirements?
какие security boundaries?
```

---

# 15015. Он введёт единый resolver:

```text
Action
+
Capability Requirements
+
Data Locality
+
Policy
+
Latency
+
Cost
↓
Execution Placement
```

---

# 15016. Тогда Innovation OS сможет распределять работу между:

```text
central cloud
local PC
ARM edge box
robot controller
GPU server
partner node
```

не меняя semantic meaning самого Action.

---

# 15017. Это станет следующим мостом:

```text
Semantic World
↔
Distributed Physical Compute
```

и позволит действительно масштабировать Virtual Technopark от одного сервера до федерации лабораторий, машин, роботов и AI-инфраструктуры.
contents.title: Universal Data, Perception & Evidence Fabric v0.1

contents.content: Следующее продолжение логично начать с **15018** — **Distributed Semantic Compute, Edge Intelligence & Execution Fabric v0.1**.
Да

Продолжаю с **15018**. Теперь строим слой распределённого исполнения: как Innovation OS выбирает **где** выполнять Action — в облаке, на локальном ПК, ARM-edge узле, GPU-сервере, лабораторной машине, роботе или федеративном партнёрском узле — с учётом данных, latency, hardware, стоимости, политики и доверия.

# Distributed Semantic Compute, Edge Intelligence & Execution Fabric v0.1

## 15018. Главный переход

До сих пор Innovation OS знает:

```text id="dk81ns"
WHAT should be done
WHY it should be done
WHAT capabilities are required
WHAT evidence is needed
```

Теперь нужен следующий вопрос:

```text id="kyi01m"
WHERE should computation actually happen?
```

---

# 15019. В обычной distributed system это часто задача scheduler

Он рассматривает:

```text id="pg6lxh"
CPU
RAM
GPU
load
```

Для Innovation OS этого недостаточно.

---

# 15020. Потому что Action может требовать одновременно

```text id="exbt55"
Capability
Hardware
Data
Permission
Location
Latency
Trust
Cost
```

---

# 15021. Поэтому требуется

# Semantic Execution Placement

---

# 15022. Базовая формула

```text id="zclkp9"
Action
+
Capability Requirements
+
Data Locality
+
Hardware Requirements
+
Policy Constraints
+
Latency Requirements
+
Cost Constraints
+
Availability
↓
Candidate Execution Nodes
↓
Feasibility Filtering
↓
Placement Options
↓
Execution
```

---

# 15023. Ключевой принцип

```text id="bcnytz"
Task ≠ Machine
```

---

# 15024. Action описывает:

```text id="41etnh"
что должно быть выполнено
```

---

# 15025. Execution Placement определяет:

```text id="5puyw9"
где это будет выполнено
```

---

# 15026. Поэтому Project/Action Graph должен оставаться:

```text id="ktdyms"
hardware-independent
```

настолько, насколько позволяет задача.

---

# 15027. Пример

Action:

```text id="phxh8c"
Extract tables from 500 PDFs
```

---

# 15028. Он может быть выполнен:

```text id="8zfp7a"
local CPU
local GPU
cloud GPU
partner node
```

---

# 15029. Семантика Action не меняется.

---

# 15030. Меняется:

```text id="9ml3a7"
Execution Binding
```

---

# 15031. Execution Node

Новый core root не нужен.

Execution Node — это:

```text id="0gdzgo"
RESOURCE
```

с соответствующими capabilities.

---

# 15032. Types могут быть application taxonomy:

```text id="8se99a"
CLOUD_NODE
SERVER
WORKSTATION
EDGE_NODE
MOBILE_DEVICE
ROBOT
LAB_CONTROLLER
GPU_NODE
FEDERATED_NODE
```

---

# 15033. Node identity должна быть стабильной

---

# 15034. Hostname/IP ≠ identity

---

# 15035. Потому что:

```text id="pl0fv9"
IP changes
hostname changes
VM migrates
```

---

# 15036. Internal UUID remains canonical.

---

# 15037. External identities могут включать:

```text id="z8n5lm"
hostname
cloud instance ID
device serial
federation node ID
```

---

# 15038. Compute Capability

Node may PROVIDE:

```text id="x66nhm"
x86_compute
arm64_compute
cuda_gpu
rocm_gpu
webassembly_runtime
container_runtime
local_llm
```

---

# 15039. Hardware detail не должен быть только free-text.

---

# 15040. Example capability claims:

```text id="kfn6rt"
Node A PROVIDES arm64_linux
Node B PROVIDES cuda_compute
Node C PROVIDES browser_execution
```

---

# 15041. Но:

```text id="yvp9qx"
GPU exists
≠
required software stack works
```

---

# 15042. Поэтому verified compute capability тоже проходит:

```text id="hukjmp"
DECLARED
EVIDENCED
VERIFIED
OPERATIONAL
```

---

# 15043. Example

Node has NVIDIA GPU.

Но CUDA driver broken.

---

# 15044. State:

```text id="ifvzw3"
hardware present = YES
cuda capability = DEGRADED
```

---

# 15045. Очень важное разделение

```text id="4eqhci"
Hardware Inventory
≠
Executable Capability
```

---

# 15046. Node Manifest

```yaml id="6h9myu"
node:
  id: edge-017
  architecture: arm64
  memory_gb: 32
  accelerators:
    - npu
  operating_system: linux

capabilities:
  - container_execution
  - local_vision_inference
  - semantic_event_generation
```

---

# 15047. Manifest — declaration.

---

# 15048. Runtime verification determines what is actually available.

---

# 15049. Node Health

Dimensions:

```text id="5a2kwl"
reachable
compute
storage
network
capability
security
```

---

# 15050. Avoid universal:

```text id="9d4o4p"
node health = 87%
```

---

# 15051. Example

```yaml id="s1s4la"
reachable: true
cpu_capacity: available
gpu_capability: degraded
network: healthy
storage: low
```

---

# 15052. Placement Engine can reason dimensionally.

---

# 15053. Execution Requirement

Action needs machine-readable requirements.

---

# 15054. Example

```yaml id="h6eu4j"
execution_requirements:
  capabilities:
    - python_runtime
    - pdf_table_extraction

  architecture:
    any_of:
      - amd64
      - arm64

  memory_gb:
    minimum: 8

  network:
    internet_required: false

  data_locality:
    required_context: confidential-documents
```

---

# 15055. Hard vs soft requirements again important.

---

# 15056. Hard:

```text id="cx1z1t"
must run inside EU
```

---

# 15057. Soft:

```text id="yx1pwa"
prefer local execution
```

---

# 15058. Placement pipeline

```text id="6sn5ov"
Candidate Nodes
↓
Hard Constraints
↓
Capability Verification
↓
Data Access
↓
Policy
↓
Capacity
↓
Latency / Cost / Resilience
↓
Placement Options
```

---

# 15059. Hard NO means:

```text id="yg6m13"
node removed
```

---

# 15060. UNKNOWN hard constraint means:

```text id="12l8uw"
INVESTIGATE
```

not PASS.

---

# 15061. Example

Action handles restricted data.

Node jurisdiction UNKNOWN.

---

# 15062. Correct result:

```text id="jbdqb6"
not eligible until resolved
```

---

# 15063. Data Locality

Это одна из главных причин распределённого execution.

---

# 15064. Иногда дешевле переместить computation к data,

а не data к computation.

---

# 15065. Especially for:

```text id="rfbpwy"
large video
industrial telemetry
confidential datasets
```

---

# 15066. Pattern:

# Compute-to-Data

```text id="qjzvcu"
Action Package
↓
Data Node
↓
Local Execution
↓
Result/Evidence
```

---

# 15067. Raw data остаётся локально.

---

# 15068. Возвращается:

```text id="5lw198"
semantic result
aggregate
artifact reference
evidence reference
```

---

# 15069. Это критично для федеративной архитектуры.

---

# 15070. Data Movement Cost

Placement should consider:

```text id="ujfnv7"
size
bandwidth
latency
```
