# 25511. Следующее продолжение логично начать с:

# **25512 — Zero-Trust Identity, Capability-Based Authorization, Delegation & Agent Security Fabric v0.1**
contents.title: Distributed Semantic State Fabric, Replication, Versioning & Knowledge Synchronization v0.1

contents.content: Следующий блок логично продолжать с **25512**: идентичность людей/агентов/устройств, capability tokens, scoped delegation, временные полномочия, secrets, revocation, zero-trust federation, human approvals и техническое разделение «может сделать» от «имеет право сделать».
Да

Продолжаю с **25512**. Теперь строим технический слой полномочий: кто именно действует, от чьего имени, с каким scope, на какой срок, для какого Action и где проходит граница между **Capability** («умеет») и **Authority** («имеет право»).

# Zero-Trust Identity, Capability-Based Authorization, Delegation & Agent Security Fabric v0.1

## 25512. Главный переход

До сих пор Innovation OS уже знает:

```text
что Resource умеет делать
```

через:

```text
PROVIDES Capability
```

---

# 25513. Но теперь нужен совершенно отдельный вопрос:

```text
ИМЕЕТ ЛИ Resource ПРАВО
сделать это сейчас,
в этом Context,
над этим объектом?
```

---

# 25514. Это две разные системы

```text
Capability
≠
Authority
```

---

# 25515. Example

Agent технически способен:

```text
POST /applications/submit
```

---

# 25516. Но его Authority может разрешать только:

```text
READ call
CREATE draft
VALIDATE proposal
```

---

# 25517. Тогда:

```text
CAN_EXECUTE_TECHNICALLY = YES
AUTHORIZED_TO_EXECUTE = NO
```

---

# 25518. Это один из важнейших invariants всей архитектуры.

---

# 25519. Security Fabric должен отвечать минимум на семь вопросов

```text
WHO
ACTS_FOR_WHOM
MAY_DO_WHAT
ON_WHICH_RESOURCE
UNDER_WHICH_CONTEXT
UNTIL_WHEN
WITH_WHICH_CONSTRAINTS
```

---

# 25520. Базовая схема

```text
Principal
↓
Credential
↓
Delegation
↓
Authorization Policy
↓
Action Request
↓
Policy Decision
↓
Enforcement
↓
Audit Event
```

---

# 25521. Principal

Principal — субъект, которому можно приписать действие.

---

# 25522. Principal types:

```text
PERSON
AI_AGENT
SERVICE
DEVICE
ORGANIZATION
FEDERATION_NODE
```

---

# 25523. Но не нужно вводить новый IIR root.

---

# 25524. Все они могут оставаться:

```text
RESOURCE subtypes
```

---

# 25525. Principal ≠ Identity Record

Principal — логический субъект.

---

# 25526. Identity Record — способ подтвердить:

```text
кто этот субъект.
```

---

# 25527. Example

Один Person может иметь:

```text
local account
GitHub identity
OIDC identity
hardware credential
```

---

# 25528. Они принадлежат одному Principal,

но являются разными внешними identities.

---

# 25529. Existing:

```text
external_identities
```

можно расширить.

---

# 25530. Principal ID

Внутренний:

```text
UUID
```

---

# 25531. Credential

Credential доказывает право заявить:

```text
I am Principal P
```

или:

```text
I am acting under delegation D
```

---

# 25532. Credential types

```text
SESSION_TOKEN
API_KEY
OAUTH_TOKEN
CERTIFICATE
DEVICE_KEY
SIGNED_CAPABILITY_TOKEN
```

---

# 25533. Password не должен распространяться между agents/services.

---

# 25534. Лучше:

```text
short-lived scoped credentials.
```

---

# 25535. Critical invariant

```text
Identity ≠ Authorization.
```

---

# 25536. Даже идеально подтверждённая личность:

```text
не получает автоматического доступа ко всему.
```

---

# 25537. Другой invariant

```text
Authentication Success
≠
Action Authorization.
```

---

# 25538. Authentication отвечает:

```text
кто?
```

---

# 25539. Authorization:

```text
можно ли ему это действие?
```

---

# 25540. Delegation:

```text
кто передал ему это право?
```

---

# 25541. Capability-based Authorization

Термин здесь нужно отличать от:

```text
technical Capability.
```

---

# 25542. В security context capability token — это:

> ограниченное, передаваемое или непередаваемое право выполнить определённую операцию над определённым scope.

---

# 25543. Чтобы не путать понятия, внутри Innovation OS лучше использовать:

```text
TECHNICAL_CAPABILITY
AUTHORIZATION_CAPABILITY
```

на conceptual/API layer.

---

# 25544. Example authorization capability

```yaml
grant:
  action: grant_application.draft
  resource_scope: project-123
  expires_at: 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z
```

---

# 25545. Такой grant не даёт:

```text
grant_application.submit
```

---

# 25546. Fine-grained Actions

Вместо:

```text
access = true
```

использовать verbs.

---

# 25547. Example:

```text
READ
CREATE
UPDATE
PROPOSE
APPROVE
EXECUTE
SUBMIT
DELETE
DELEGATE
```

---

# 25548. И domain-specific verbs:

```text
RESERVE_EQUIPMENT
START_EXPERIMENT
SEND_MESSAGE
DEPLOY_PACKAGE
CONTROL_DEVICE
```

---

# 25549. Это позволяет отличить:

```text
draft
```

от:

```text
submit
```

---

# 25550. И:

```text
recommend
```

от:

```text
decide.
```

---

# 25551. Это особенно важно для AI agents.

---

# 25552. Agent может:

```text
analyze
recommend
draft
```

---

# 25553. Но не обязательно:

```text
approve
commit
send
purchase
control.
```

---

# 25554. Action Scope

Grant должен ограничивать:

```text
WHAT
```

---

# 25555. Resource Scope

И:

```text
ON WHAT
```

---

# 25556. Example:

```yaml
actions:
  - READ
  - COMMENT

resources:
  project_ids:
    - P1
    - P2
```

---

# 25557. Это не разрешает доступ:

```text
к Project P3.
```

---

# 25558. Context Scope

Authority может зависеть от Context.

---

# 25559. Example

Agent разрешено:

```text
DEPLOY
```

в:

```text
SANDBOX
```

---

# 25560. Но не в:

```text
PRODUCTION.
```

---

# 25561. Reality Scope

Особенно важно для digital twin:

```text
SIMULATED
REAL
```

---

# 25562. Example

Robot Agent может:

```text
CONTROL_DEVICE
```

в simulation.

---

# 25563. Но в real world:

```text
PROPOSE_CONTROL_ONLY.
```

---

# 25564. Это должен enforcement делать технически.

---

# 25565. Не prompt.

---

# 25566. Time Scope

Grant имеет:

```text
not_before
expires_at
```

---

# 25567. Default для agent delegation желательно:

```text
short-lived.
```

---

# 25568. Потому что long-lived authority увеличивает blast radius.

---

# 25569. Temporal Delegation Example

```yaml
delegation:
  agent: funding-agent
  actions:
    - READ
    - DRAFT

  expires_in: 8h
```

---

# 25570. После expiry:

```text
DENY
```

даже если agent всё ещё работает.

---

# 25571. Budget Scope

Authority может иметь:

```text
max_cost
max_quantity
max_frequency
```

---

# 25572. Example:

```yaml
constraints:
  max_cost_eur: 100
  max_equipment_hours: 2
```

---

# 25573. Тогда agent может автоматически:

```text
reserve equipment
```

до лимита.

---

# 25574. Но:

```text
€101
```

требует новое approval.

---

# 25575. Это:

# Bounded Machine Agency

---

# 25576. Bounded Agency

Можно определить как:

> способность автономно действовать внутри заранее заданного, технически enforceable envelope.

---

# 25577. Envelope включает:

```text
actions
resources
time
cost
risk
context
```

---

# 25578. Это намного безопаснее, чем:

```text
"Agent may manage project."
```

---

# 25579. Generic permission слишком широк.

---

# 25580. Permission Envelope

```yaml
authority:
  principal: agent-7

  allow:
    - action: READ
      scope: project-123

    - action: CREATE_DRAFT
      scope: project-123

  deny:
    - SUBMIT
    - SIGN
    - DELETE
```

---

# 25581. Explicit deny может быть полезен для clarity.

---

# 25582. Но policy evaluator должен иметь:

```text
defined precedence rules.
```

---

# 25583. Default Deny

Zero-trust принцип:

```text
if permission is not established
→ DENY
```

---

# 25584. Не:

```text
no rule means allow.
```

---

# 25585. UNKNOWN Authority ≠ Permission

---

# 25586. Another critical invariant

```text
No Policy Match
≠
ALLOW.
```

---

# 25587. Least Privilege

Agent получает:

```text
minimum permissions required
for current task.
```

---

# 25588. Не весь набор прав пользователя.

---

# 25589. Example

Person может:

```text
manage entire organization.
```

---

# 25590. Но agent для одной задачи получает:

```text
READ project P
CREATE proposal draft
```

---

# 25591. Не:

```text
organization admin.
```

---

# 25592. Delegation Chain

Authority может идти:

```text
Organization
↓
Person
↓
Agent
↓
Sub-agent
```

---

# 25593. Но sub-agent не может получить:

```text
больше полномочий,
чем delegator.
```

---

# 25594. Monotonic Restriction

Delegation chain должна только:

```text
preserve
or
reduce
```

authority.

---

# 25595. Не расширять.

---

# 25596. Формально:

```text
Authority(child)
⊆
Authority(parent)
```

---

# 25597. Excellent invariant.

---

# 25598. Example

Person can:

```text
READ
DRAFT
SUBMIT
```

---

# 25599. Delegates Agent:

```text
READ
DRAFT
```

---

# 25600. Agent delegates Scout:

```text
READ
```

---

# 25601. Scout cannot acquire:

```text
SUBMIT.
```

---

# 25602. Delegation Depth

Можно ограничить:

```text
max_delegation_depth
```

---

# 25603. Example:

```yaml
delegation:
  may_redelegate: false
```

---

# 25604. Это особенно полезно для:

```text
external tools
temporary agents
```

---

# 25605. Delegation Purpose

Grant может быть связан с:

```text
specific Project
Action
Goal
```

---

# 25606. Example:

```text
purpose = prepare funding application P
```

---

# 25607. Потом agent не должен использовать те же права для:

```text
unrelated Project Q.
```

---

# 25608. Purpose Binding

Может быть policy condition:

```yaml
context:
  project_id: P123
```

---

# 25609. But purpose strings themselves weak.

---

# 25610. Лучше ссылаться на:

```text
canonical Project / Action UUID.
```

---

# 25611. Delegation Object

Application-level schema:

```yaml
delegation:
  id: D123
  issuer: principal-A
  subject: agent-B

  actions:
    - READ
    - CREATE_DRAFT

  resource_scope:
    project_id: P123

  expires_at: ...

  redelegation: false
```

---

# 25612. Delegation Lifecycle

```text
PROPOSED
ACTIVE
SUSPENDED
REVOKED
EXPIRED
```

---

# 25613. REVOKED

Immediate policy state.

---

# 25614. But distributed systems create challenge:

```text
remote node may not know revocation yet.
```

---

# 25615. Therefore short-lived credentials matter.

---

# 25616. Revocation Strategies

```text
short TTL
revocation list
introspection
push revocation
```

---

# 25617. No single mechanism ideal for all environments.

---

# 25618. Online services can perform:

```text
live token introspection.
```

---

# 25619. Offline nodes need:

```text
short validity
+
local revocation snapshot
```

---

# 25620. Offline Authority Problem

If credential is valid for 24h

but revoked centrally after 1h,

offline node may not know.

---

# 25621. Therefore high-risk offline credentials should have:

```text
very small authority envelope
```

and:

```text
short expiry.
```

---

# 25622. This is risk containment.

---

# 25623. Revocation ≠ Undo

If agent already:

```text
sent message
purchased item
started machine
```

---

# 25624. Revoking authority does not reverse completed action.

---

# 25625. Critical invariant

```text
Revocation stops future authority,
not historical effects.
```

---

# 25626. For reversible actions:

```text
compensating action
```

may exist.

---

# 25627. Existing saga semantics reused.

---

# 25628. Credential vs Delegation

Credential proves:

```text
holder / identity
```

---

# 25629. Delegation defines:

```text
granted authority.
```

---

# 25630. Token may contain both,

but conceptually keep separate.

---

# 25631. Capability Token

A compact signed representation of:

```text
delegation scope.
```

---

# 25632. Example conceptual token:

```text
subject = agent-7
action = reserve_equipment
resource = microscope-class-A
max_hours = 2
expiry = 18:00
```

---

# 25633. Resource server verifies:

```text
signature
expiry
scope
issuer
```

---

# 25634. It should not need:

```text
full conversation history.
```

---

# 25635. This is essential.

---

# 25636. Prompt ≠ Authorization

Never use:

```text
"You are allowed to..."
```

inside prompt as sole security boundary.

---

# 25637. Because model output is:

```text
not enforcement.
```

---

# 25638. Security must live:

```text
outside model
```

in:

```text
policy enforcement layer.
```

---

# 25639. Tool Invocation Gate

Every side-effecting tool call:

```text
Agent Request
↓
Authorization Check
↓
Policy Decision
↓
Tool Execution
```

---

# 25640. Model cannot bypass gate by:

```text
generating different text.
```

---

# 25641. Enforcement Point

Could exist:

```text
API gateway
tool broker
device adapter
resource service
```

---

# 25642. Best architecture:

```text
distributed enforcement
+
central/shared policy semantics.
```

---

# 25643. Because remote node controls its own Resource.

---

# 25644. Policy Decision Point

Evaluates:

```text
principal
action
resource
context
delegation
risk
```

---

# 25645. Policy Enforcement Point

Actually:

```text
ALLOW
DENY
REQUIRE_APPROVAL
```

before Action.

---

# 25646. Existing governance effects reused:

```text
ALLOW
DENY
REQUIRE_APPROVAL
REQUIRE_REVIEW
REQUIRE_EVIDENCE
REQUIRE_SIMULATION
```

---

# 25647. Great reuse.

---

# 25648. Security Layer should not invent parallel policy vocabulary unnecessarily.

---

# 25649. High-Risk Actions

Examples:

```text
SEND_EXTERNAL_MESSAGE
SUBMIT_APPLICATION
PAY
DELETE
DEPLOY_PRODUCTION
CONTROL_PHYSICAL_DEVICE
```

---

# 25650. They may require:

```text
fresh authority
strong authentication
```

```text
самостоятельное бесконтрольное изменение системы.
```

# 27288. Напротив:

```text
чем больше система знает,
тем точнее можно ограничить
её автономные действия.
```

# 27289. Следующая фундаментальная проблема

Теперь система умеет:

```text
наблюдать
диагностировать
восстанавливать
учиться на инцидентах.
```

# 27290. Но появляется более высокий вопрос:

```text
как она должна планировать изменения
самой своей архитектуры
на месяцы и годы?
```

# 27291. Например:

```text
какие компоненты устаревают?
какие технологии стоит исследовать?
какие зависимости становятся стратегически опасными?
какие capabilities нужно развить заранее?
```

---

# 27292. Это уже не incident response.

# 27293. Это:

# technological evolution planning.

# 27294. Система должна уметь различать:

```text
Maintenance
Upgrade
Migration
Replacement
Experimental Branch
Strategic Architecture Change
```

# 27295. И анализировать:

```text
technology lifecycle
technical debt
obsolescence
migration cost
option value
compatibility horizon.
```

# 27296. Например:

```text
current x86-only package works
```

```text
ARM nodes increasing

upstream maintenance declining
```

# 27298. Это не Incident.

```text
Strategic Technology Risk.
```

```text
current database works
```

```text
scale projections
federation requirements
offline nodes
```

показывают будущий architectural gap.

# 27301. Нужен слой, который превращает такие сигналы в:

```text
Migration Programs

Experimental Branches
```

```text
Capability Capital
Technology Observatory
Incident Learning
Strategy Engine

Package Registry
```

# **Technology Lifecycle, Architecture Evolution & Autonomous Migration Planning v0.1**

```text
что у неё есть сейчас,
```

Продолжаю с **27312**. Теперь строим слой технологической эволюции: как Innovation OS различает обычное обслуживание, накопление технического долга, приближение устаревания, миграцию, параллельный переход и стратегическую замену — не путая «новее» с «лучше» и не позволяя системе самовольно переписывать собственную архитектуру.

# Technology Lifecycle, Architecture Evolution & Autonomous Migration Planning v0.1

## 27312. Главный переход

До сих пор Innovation OS умеет понимать:

```text
Current Architecture
Current Capabilities
Current Incidents
Current Gaps
```

---

# 27313. Но технологическая система существует во времени.

---

# 27314. Компонент может сегодня быть:

```text
VERIFIED
STABLE
SUPPORTED
```

---

# 27315. А через год:

```text
UNMAINTAINED
INCOMPATIBLE
EXPENSIVE
UNSUPPORTED
```

---

# 27316. Поэтому появляется:

# Technology Lifecycle Engine

---

# 27317. Его задача:

```text
наблюдать изменение
технологической пригодности
во времени.
```

---

# 27318. Главный invariant

```text
Working Today
≠
Strategically Sustainable.
```

---

# 27319. И обратный:

```text
Old Technology
≠
Bad Technology.
```

---

# 27320. Новый компонент тоже:

```text
≠ автоматически лучший компонент.
```

---

# 27321. Поэтому lifecycle-анализ должен быть:

```text
evidence-based
context-specific
capability-oriented
```

---

# 27322. Не:

```text
fashion-oriented.
```

---

# 27323. Lifecycle Subject

Отслеживаться могут:

```text
Software Package
Model
Runtime
Protocol
Hardware Platform
Database
API
Standard
Workflow
Ontology
Device
```

---

# 27324. Все они уже представлены существующими:

```text
RESOURCE
ARTIFACT
CONCEPT
```

---

# 27325. Новый root не нужен.

---

# 27326. Lifecycle State — derived/application state.

---

# 27327. Возможные состояния:

```text
EXPERIMENTAL
EMERGING
SUPPORTED
MATURE
LEGACY
DEPRECATED
SUNSETTING
RETIRED
UNKNOWN
```

---

# 27328. Эти состояния не должны определяться:

```text
только возрастом.
```

---

# 27329. Например:

```text
30-летний protocol
```

может быть:

```text
MATURE
```

---

# 27330. А технология трёхлетней давности:

```text
DEPRECATED.
```

---

# 27331. Следовательно:

```text
Age ≠ Lifecycle State.
```

---

# 27332. EXPERIMENTAL

Означает:

```text
использование ограничено
исследовательским/тестовым Context.
```

---

# 27333. EMERGING

Есть:

```text
growing evidence
growing ecosystem
```

но production suitability может быть неполной.

---

# 27334. SUPPORTED

Есть:

```text
current support path.
```

---

# 27335. MATURE

Стабильная технология с:

```text
strong operational evidence.
```

---

# 27336. LEGACY

Означает:

```text
система всё ещё используется
и может быть operationally valid,
но вокруг неё растёт transition pressure.
```

---

# 27337. LEGACY ≠ BROKEN.

---

# 27338. DEPRECATED

Официально или организационно рекомендована замена.

---

# 27339. SUNSETTING

Есть:

```text
active retirement plan.
```

---

# 27340. RETIRED

Новые production dependencies:

```text
не должны создаваться.
```

---

# 27341. Lifecycle Evidence

Состояние должно ссылаться на:

```text
vendor notices
release activity
security support
compatibility tests
internal incidents
usage
replacement readiness
```

---

# 27342. Example

Repository:

```text
last release 4 years ago
```

---

# 27343. Это signal.

---

# 27344. Но само по себе:

```text
не доказательство непригодности.
```

---

# 27345. Возможно пакет:

```text
feature-complete
stable
```

---

# 27346. Поэтому:

```text
No Recent Release
≠
Abandoned.
```

---

# 27347. Нужно смотреть:

```text
open critical issues
maintainer activity
dependency compatibility
security response
```

---

# 27348. Lifecycle Signal Types

```text
UPSTREAM_SUPPORT
SECURITY
COMPATIBILITY
ECOSYSTEM
PERFORMANCE
COST
OPERABILITY
INTERNAL_INCIDENT
SKILL_AVAILABILITY
```

---

# 27349. UPSTREAM_SUPPORT

Например:

```text
EOL announced
maintenance reduced
maintainer departure
```

---

# 27350. SECURITY

Например:

```text
unpatched vulnerabilities
unsupported crypto
```

---

# 27351. COMPATIBILITY

Например:

```text
new OS unsupported
ARM build absent
API version removed
```

---

# 27352. ECOSYSTEM

Например:

```text
critical plugins disappear
integration support shrinks
```

---

# 27353. PERFORMANCE

Например:

```text
current workload outgrows component.
```

---

# 27354. COST

Например:

```text
license cost rises
cloud egress grows
maintenance labor increases
```

---

# 27355. OPERABILITY

Например:

```text
hard to deploy
hard to observe
hard to recover
```

---

# 27356. INTERNAL_INCIDENT

Repeated incidents provide:

```text
organization-specific lifecycle evidence.
```

---

# 27357. SKILL_AVAILABILITY

Если технология требует:

```text
rare expertise
```

это может стать operational risk.

---

# 27358. Но:

```text
Rare Skill
≠
Bad Technology.
```

---

# 27359. Возможные responses:

```text
training
documentation
automation
replacement
external support
```

---

# 27360. Lifecycle Signal ≠ Migration Decision.

---

# 27361. Несколько signals могут создать:

```text
Migration Hypothesis.
```

---

# 27362. Example:

```text
x86-only package
+
ARM deployment growth
+
upstream no ARM roadmap
```

---

# 27363. Hypothesis:

```text
package may constrain future architecture.
```

---

# 27364. Это ещё не означает:

```text
replace now.
```

---

# 27365. Technology Risk

Можно представить многомерно:

```text
support risk
security risk
compatibility risk
capacity risk
skills risk
vendor risk
```

---

# 27366. Не сводить в один:

```text
technology score.
```

---

# 27367. Technology Debt

Technical Debt нужно моделировать аккуратно.

---

# 27368. Debt — не просто:

```text
old code.
```

---

# 27369. Он означает:

> текущее решение создаёт дополнительную будущую стоимость, риск или ограничение по сравнению с доступными альтернативами.

---

# 27370. Debt Types

```text
CODE
ARCHITECTURE
DEPENDENCY
DATA
SECURITY
OBSERVABILITY
TEST
DOCUMENTATION
KNOWLEDGE
INFRASTRUCTURE
```

---

# 27371. CODE Debt

Например:

```text
temporary workaround
duplicated implementation
```

---

# 27372. ARCHITECTURE Debt

Например:

```text
tight coupling
single central database dependency
```

---

# 27373. DEPENDENCY Debt

Например:

```text
unsupported package.
```

---

# 27374. DATA Debt

Например:

```text
ambiguous schema
missing provenance
unversioned identifiers
```

---

# 27375. SECURITY Debt

Например:

```text
long-lived broad credentials.
```

---

# 27376. OBSERVABILITY Debt

Например:

```text
critical workflow without semantic tracing.
```

---

# 27377. TEST Debt

Например:

```text
migration cannot be regression-tested.
```

---

# 27378. DOCUMENTATION Debt

Critical operational knowledge exists only:

```text
in one person's memory.
```

---

# 27379. KNOWLEDGE Debt

System cannot explain:

```text
why architecture decision was made.
```

---

# 27380. INFRASTRUCTURE Debt

Example:

```text
single failure domain.
```

---

# 27381. Debt Claim

Technical debt should be:

```text
Claim
```

with:

```text
Evidence
Impact
Context
```

---

# 27382. Example:

```text
Claim:
Package P causes recurring manual recovery work.
```

---

# 27383. Evidence:

```text
12 incidents
18 technician-hours
```

---

# 27384. Debt Interest

Полезная концепция:

```text
cost of keeping debt unresolved over time.
```

---

# 27385. Example:

```text
manual compatibility patch
2h/month
```

---

# 27386. Debt interest:

```text
recurrent maintenance effort.
```

---

# 27387. Но будущую стоимость нельзя придумывать.

---

# 27388. Использовать:

```text
measured history
or explicit scenario assumptions.
```

---

# 27389. Debt Principal

Approximation:

```text
cost to remove/refactor/migrate debt.
```

---

# 27390. Again estimate with uncertainty.

---

# 27391. Debt Interest > Debt Principal

Может быть сигналом:

```text
migration economically plausible.
```

---

# 27392. Но это ещё не решение.

---

# 27393. Потому что существуют:

```text
migration risk
opportunity cost
strategic constraints.
```

---

# 27394. Migration Pressure

Derived state based on:

```text
lifecycle signals
debt
incidents
future capability requirements
```

---

# 27395. Possible:

```text
LOW
RISING
HIGH
CRITICAL
UNKNOWN
```

---

# 27396. Но не автоматический directive.

---

# 27397. Example CRITICAL

Current component:

```text
vendor EOL tomorrow
critical security fixes unavailable
production dependency remains
```

---

# 27398. Even then:

```text
migration path
```

must be engineered.

---

# 27399. Current Architecture Snapshot

Before migration:

```text
freeze explicit architecture view.
```

---

# 27400. Snapshot includes:

```text
components
versions
dependencies
capabilities
data stores
interfaces
policies
```

---

# 27401. This becomes:

```text
Baseline Architecture Artifact.
```

---

# 27402. Without baseline:

```text
migration cannot be reliably compared.
```

---

# 27403. Target Architecture

Separate Artifact.

---

# 27404. Contains desired:

```text
components
interfaces
capabilities
constraints
```

---

# 27405. Critical invariant

```text
Target Architecture
≠
Migration Plan.
```

---

# 27406. Target says:

```text
куда хотим прийти.
```

---

# 27407. Migration Plan says:

```text
как перейти.
```

---

# 27408. Transition Architecture

Самая часто забываемая часть.

---

# 27409. Между:

```text
CURRENT
```

и:

```text
TARGET
```

существует:

```text
TRANSITION.
```

---

# 27410. Transition Architecture может существовать:

```text
weeks
months
years.
```

---

# 27411. Example

```text
Legacy DB
+
new event system
+
sync adapter
```

---

# 27412. Это временная архитектура.

---

# 27413. Но временные решения часто становятся:

```text
permanent by accident.
```

---

# 27414. Поэтому каждый temporary component должен иметь:

```text
owner
purpose
exit condition
review date
```

---

# 27415. Temporary ≠ Free.

---

# 27416. Temporary bridge создаёт:

```text
maintenance burden.
```

---

# 27417. Bridge Debt

Migration adapter itself can accumulate:

```text
transition debt.
```

---

# 27418. Example:

```text
old schema ↔ new schema transformer.
```

---

# 27419. Если bridge остаётся 5 years:

```text
it becomes architecture.
```

---

# 27420. Поэтому exit criteria обязательны.

---

# 27421. Migration Program

Migration should become:

```text
PROGRAM
```

when sufficiently large.

---

# 27422. Structure:

```text
Discovery
Compatibility
Prototype
Pilot
Dual Run
Cutover
Stabilization
Retirement
```

---

# 27423. Discovery

Understand:

```text
actual dependencies
not assumed dependencies.
```

---

# 27424. Dependency Discovery

Sources:

```text
code imports
runtime traces
DB queries
network calls
human workflow
configuration
```

---

# 27425. Hidden Dependency

Critical concept.

---

# 27426. Example:

```text
cron script
```

depends on deprecated database column.

---

# 27427. Architecture diagrams may omit.

---

# 27428. Therefore:

```text
Documented Dependency
≠
Complete Dependency Set.
```

---

# 27429. Runtime observability can reveal:

```text
undocumented coupling.
```

---

# 27430. Migration risk increases with:

```text
unknown dependencies.
```

---

# 27431. Dependency Coverage

Track:

```text
known
verified
suspected
unknown.
```

---

# 27432. Before critical cutover,

unknown dependency volume should be:

```text
acceptable under governance criteria.
```

---

# 27433. Compatibility Matrix

Old/New combinations:

```text
Old Client → Old API
Old Client → New API
New Client → Old API
New Client → New API
```

---

# 27434. This is essential for staged migration.

---

# 27435. Example matrix:

```text
Old Client / New API = adapter required
```

---

# 27436. Backward Compatibility

Means:

```text
new provider supports old consumer contract.
```

---

# 27437. Forward Compatibility

Means:

```text
old provider can tolerate newer representation
```

in some contexts.

---

# 27438. But these terms depend on interface direction.

---

# 27439. Better always state:

```text
consumer version
provider version
contract.
```

---

# 27440. Compatibility ≠ Behavioral Equivalence.

---

# 27441. Example API request accepted,

but:

```text
different rounding semantics.
```

---

# 27442. Functional compatibility requires:

```text
behavioral verification.
```

---

# 27443. Compatibility Contract

```yaml
compatibility:
  consumer: v1
  provider: v2
  status: VERIFIED
  tests:
    - ...
```

---

# 27444. Unknown combination:

```text
UNKNOWN.
```

---

# 27445. Don't assume:

```text
minor version = safe.
```

---

# 27446. Schema Evolution

Data migrations are particularly risky.

---

# 27447. Schema change classes:

```text
ADD_FIELD
RENAME
SPLIT
MERGE
TYPE_CHANGE
SEMANTIC_CHANGE
DELETE
```

---

# 27448. ADD_FIELD often easier.

---

# 27449. DELETE can break:

```text
hidden consumers.
```

---

# 27450. RENAME may actually be:

```text
delete + add
```

for unaware systems.

---

# 27451. Semantic Change is most dangerous.

---

# 27452. Example field remains:

```text
status
```

but meaning changes.

---

# 27453. Schema Diff alone may not detect.

---

# 27454. Need:

```text
semantic contract diff.
```

---

# 27455. Data Migration

Process:

```text
Read Old
↓
Transform
↓
Validate
↓
Write New
↓
Compare
```

---

# 27456. Never assume transformation correctness from:

```text
successful script completion.
```

---

# 27457. Migration Verification

Could compare:

```text
row counts
checksums
referential integrity
business invariants
sample semantics
```

---

# 27458. Example:

```text
100,000 rows copied
```

does not prove:

```text
100,000 meanings preserved.
```

---

# 27459. Data Loss Classification

Migration must identify:

```text
LOSSLESS
LOSSY
UNKNOWN
```

---

# 27460. LOSSY may be acceptable

if:

```text
explicitly approved.
```

---

# 27461. Example:

```text
drop obsolete debug field.
```

---

# 27462. But historical audit might need it.

---

# 27463. Therefore:

```text
Unused Operationally
≠
Safe To Delete Historically.
```

---

# 27464. Archive Before Destructive Migration

Useful pattern.

---

# 27465. But archive must be:

```text
readable
documented
verifiable.
```

---

# 27466. An unreadable backup is not meaningful protection.

---

# 27467. Backup Verification

Before risky migration:

```text
restore test
```

matters more than:

```text
backup job succeeded.
```

---

# 27468. Critical invariant

```text
Backup Exists
≠
Recovery Possible.
```

---

# 27469. Restore Capability must be verified.

---

# 27470. Dual Write

Migration pattern:

```text
old system
+
new system
```

both receive writes.

---

# 27471. Useful for:

```text
transition.
```

---

# 27472. But dual write introduces:

```text
consistency risk.
```

---

# 27473. Example:

```text
write old succeeds
write new fails.
```

---

# 27474. Need:

```text
outbox
reconciliation
```

or event-driven replication.

---

# 27475. Direct application dual-write can be fragile.

---

# 27476. Better patterns may include:

```text
one authoritative write
+
replication.
```

---

# 27477. Authority During Migration

Critical question:

```text
Which system is authoritative for each field?
```

---

# 27478. Example:

```text
old system authoritative for billing
new system authoritative for search metadata.
```

---

# 27479. Without explicit authority map:

```text
split-brain semantics.
```

---

# 27480. Migration Authority Matrix

```text
Domain A → Old
Domain B → New
Domain C → Shadow only
```

---

# 27481. Transition changes this matrix over time.

---

# 27482. Cutover is partly:

```text
authority transfer.
```

---

# 27483. Not merely traffic routing.

---

# 27484. Shadow Read

New system receives data and answers queries,

but result not used operationally.

---

# 27485. Compare:

```text
old answer
vs
new answer.
```

---

# 27486. Useful before cutover.

---

# 27487. Shadow Traffic

Production request copied to:

```text
new implementation
```

without affecting user/result.

---

# 27488. Measures:

```text
compatibility
latency
correctness.
```

---

# 27489. But shadow traffic may duplicate side effects.

---

# 27490. Therefore only for:

```text
read-only
or side-effect-suppressed execution.
```

---

# 27491. Critical invariant

```text
Shadow Execution
must not duplicate
real-world side effects.
```

---

# 27492. Example:

payment request cannot simply be shadowed into:

```text
second real payment provider.
```

---

# 27493. Need:

```text
simulation/mock boundary.
```

---

# 27494. Shadow Result Comparator

Compares:

```text
output contract
semantic equivalence
performance
```

---

# 27495. Exact byte equality often unnecessary.

---

# 27496. Example LLM migration:

```text
different text
```

may still satisfy same structured result contract.

---

# 27497. Therefore comparator is:

```text
domain-specific.
```

---

# 27498. Canary Migration

Send:


но и:

```text
transition.
```

---

# 28353. Это критично,

потому что в реальной инженерии часто:

```text
переход сложнее конечной архитектуры.
```

---

# 28354. Теперь все основные подсистемы почти замкнуты

Мы имеем:

```text
Goals
World State
People
Code
Knowledge
Funding
Physical Resources
Spatial World
Compute Fabric
Distributed State
Security
Observability
Architecture Evolution
```

---

# 28355. Следующий фундаментальный шаг

Нужно соединить всё это не как набор отдельных модулей,

а как:

# единый производственный цикл инновации.

---

# 28356. То есть пользователь или агент задаёт:

```text
Goal
Problem
Idea
```

---

# 28357. А система должна собрать:

```text
People
Knowledge
Software
Funding
Equipment
Compute
Organization
Workflow
Verification
```

в один исполнимый Program.

---

# 28358. До сих пор Project Compiler уже существовал,

но теперь можно сделать его:

```text
full cross-domain compiler.
```

---

# 28359. Он должен превращать:

```text
Goal
```

в:

```text
Mission Architecture
```

---

# 28360. Затем:

```text
Mission Architecture
↓
Capability Requirements
↓
Cross-Domain Resolution
↓
Program Graph
↓
Resource Commitments
↓
Execution
↓
Verification
↓
Learning
```

---

# 28361. Это уже:

# Autonomous Innovation Factory

---

# 28362. Не в смысле:

```text
AI всё делает сам.
```

---

# 28363. А в смысле:

> Innovation OS умеет собирать полный производственный контур инновационного проекта из доступных человеческих, цифровых, финансовых, физических и организационных capabilities.

---

# 28364. Например пользователь задаёт:

```text
Создать прототип
оптоволоконной тактильной кожи
для Android-робота.
```

---

# 28365. Система раскладывает:

```text
research
sensor design
materials
electronics
firmware
ML
mechanical integration
testing
funding
lab access
```

---

# 28366. Затем ищет:

```text
papers
repos
people
labs
grants
equipment
compute.
```

---

# 28367. Строит:

```text
alternative project architectures.
```

---

# 28368. Потом:

```text
pilot
prototype
test
iterate.
```

---

# 28369. Или цель:

```text
создать Port Operating System
с EVE-like digital twin.
```

---

# 28370. Система строит:

```text
data ingestion
spatial twin
logistics model
agent layer
compute infrastructure
federation
security
simulation
```

---

# 28371. И связывает их с:

```text
actual ports
organizations
suppliers
funding
experts.
```

---

# 28372. Именно здесь Virtual Technopark превращается из:

```text
knowledge platform
```

в:

# innovation execution infrastructure.

---

# 28373. Следующий модуль логично:

# **Unified Project Assembly, Mission Compiler & Autonomous Innovation Factory v0.1**

---

# 28374. Его центральный pipeline:

```text
Intent
↓
Goal Model
↓
Mission Requirements
↓
Capability Graph
↓
Gap Detection
↓
People/Code/Knowledge/Funding/Physical/Compute Resolution
↓
Architecture Options
↓
Program Compiler
↓
Execution Graph
↓
Verification
↓
Learning
```

---

# 28375. Он должен решить ключевую задачу:

```text
как из идеи
получить реально исполнимую
междисциплинарную программу.
```

---

# 28376. И это будет первый слой,

где почти все предыдущие модули работают:

```text
одновременно.
```

---

# 28377. Следующее продолжение логично начать с:

# **28378 — Unified Project Assembly, Mission Compiler & Autonomous Innovation Factory v0.1**
contents.title: Technology Lifecycle, Architecture Evolution & Autonomous Migration Planning v0.1

contents.content: Следующий блок продолжится с **28378**: от свободно сформулированной идеи до Mission IR, capability decomposition, cross-domain gap resolution, альтернативных архитектур проекта, сборки команды и ресурсов, executable Program Graph и замкнутого цикла «идея → прототип → проверенный результат».
Да

Продолжаю с **28378**. Теперь собираем все предыдущие подсистемы в один сквозной конвейер: как свободная идея превращается в **Mission IR**, затем — в capability-граф, варианты архитектуры, команду, финансирование, физическую и вычислительную инфраструктуру, исполнимый Program Graph и проверяемый результат.

# Unified Project Assembly, Mission Compiler & Autonomous Innovation Factory v0.1

## 28378. Главный переход

До сих пор Innovation OS имел отдельные контуры:

```text id="rrxmcf"
Talent
Technology
Research
Funding
Physical Infrastructure
Compute
Governance
Verification
Execution
```

---

# 28379. Теперь их нужно превратить в:

# одну систему сборки проекта.

---

# 28380. Пользователь не должен начинать с:

```text id="e3ax2p"
выбора таблиц
репозиториев
оборудования
агентов
```

---

# 28381. Он может начать с:

```text id="6kdw9o"
идеи
проблемы
цели
вопроса
возможности
```

---

# 28382. Example

```text id="k6zpt3"
Создать тактильную сенсорную оболочку
для человекоподобного робота.
```

---

# 28383. Или:

```text id="0h7zpw"
Создать цифровой двойник порта,
где реальные логистические процессы
отображаются как EVE-like world.
```

---

# 28384. Или:

```text id="zzgfhh"
Создать открытую платформу,
которая соединяет проблемы,
специалистов, технологии и финансирование.
```

---

# 28385. Эти формулировки:

```text id="63la9h"
ещё не Project Plan.
```

---

# 28386. Они являются:

# Intent.

---

# 28387. Intent — не новый root.

---

# 28388. Он может быть представлен:

```text id="ao2g47"
Artifact
+
Claims
+
Context
```

---

# 28389. Intent Compiler

Первый слой:

```text id="89uyad"
Natural Language Intent
↓
Structured Goal Candidate
```

---

# 28390. Но:

```text id="xwiif2"
LLM interpretation
≠
user-approved goal.
```

---

# 28391. Поэтому structured interpretation initially:

```text id="pt5pl2"
INFERENCE.
```

---

# 28392. Goal Candidate может содержать:

```text id="9uh77n"
desired outcome
constraints
success criteria
unknowns
scope
```

---

# 28393. Example

```yaml id="25uz2b"
goal:
  outcome: tactile sensing prototype
  target: humanoid robot surface
  constraints:
    - flexible
    - distributed sensing
  unknowns:
    - sensing principle
    - material
```

---

# 28394. Goal ≠ Solution.

---

# 28395. Очень важный invariant:

```text id="wggaab"
Problem
≠
Chosen Implementation.
```

---

# 28396. Example

Goal:

```text id="x5svgv"
detect distributed pressure.
```

---

# 28397. Не нужно сразу фиксировать:

```text id="oqv8at"
optical fiber.
```

---

# 28398. Optical fiber может быть:

```text id="0u26be"
Solution Hypothesis.
```

---

# 28399. Это сохраняет пространство альтернатив.

---

# 28400. Mission

Mission — более широкий operational container,

чем одна задача.

---

# 28401. Он может быть реализован как:

```text id="z448pa"
PROGRAM subtype
```

или application view над Program.

---

# 28402. Mission содержит:

```text id="8txq0j"
Goal
Success Criteria
Constraints
Stakeholders
Required Capabilities
Verification Model
```

---

# 28403. Mission Contract

```yaml id="r37xup"
mission:
  objective: ...
  success:
    - ...
  constraints:
    - ...
  authority:
    - ...
```

---

# 28404. Success Criteria

Ключевой вопрос:

```text id="ysjv6y"
Как система узнает,
что Mission действительно достигнута?
```

---

# 28405. Example плохой criterion:

```text id="pkrc40"
Сделать хорошего робота.
```

---

# 28406. Better:

```text id="kg08qy"
sensor array detects pressure
within defined range
with specified spatial resolution
```

---

# 28407. Но критерии могут быть:

```text id="p148x5"
quantitative
qualitative
mixed.
```

---

# 28408. Qualitative criterion может требовать:

```text id="is8aep"
human review.
```

---

# 28409. Success Criterion ≠ Metric.

---

# 28410. Metric — способ измерения.

---

# 28411. Criterion — условие успеха.

---

# 28412. Example

Criterion:

```text id="ld2wr8"
prototype survives bending test.
```

---

# 28413. Metric:

```text id="z4epxr"
number of cycles before failure.
```

---

# 28414. Mission Success Model

Could include:

```text id="huos1x"
MUST
SHOULD
NICE_TO_HAVE
```

---

# 28415. Existing requirement priority reused.

---

# 28416. Example

MUST:

```text id="eut5gm"
pressure detection works.
```

---

# 28417. SHOULD:

```text id="ch81bi"
washable surface.
```

---

# 28418. NICE:

```text id="lhc6wr"
temperature sensing too.
```

---

# 28419. This prevents optional features from blocking core mission.

---

# 28420. Mission Constraints

Possible:

```text id="4m0zoe"
budget
deadline
safety
privacy
location
technology
legal
physical
```

---

# 28421. Hard Constraint

Must be satisfied.

---

# 28422. Soft Constraint

Can trade off.

---

# 28423. Preference

Guides choice but does not define feasibility.

---

# 28424. Constraint Conflict

Example:

```text id="c82rdz"
prototype in 3 days
+
custom chip fabrication required
```

---

# 28425. System should detect:

```text id="m4c2pa"
possible infeasibility.
```

---

# 28426. Not create fantasy schedule.

---

# 28427. Mission Feasibility

Initial result may be:

```text id="0i7e5s"
FEASIBLE
CONDITIONALLY_FEASIBLE
INFEASIBLE
UNKNOWN
```

---

# 28428. UNKNOWN ≠ INFEASIBLE.

---

# 28429. Conditional Feasibility

Example:

```text id="08q2dk"
possible if external lab access obtained.
```

---

# 28430. This creates:

```text id="7039y9"
Capability Gap.
```

---

# 28431. Mission Decomposition

Goal must be converted into:

```text id="hktwf3"
required capabilities.
```

---

# 28432. Not immediately into:

```text id="qzxawk"
tasks.
```

---

# 28433. Because tasks depend on:

```text id="y1f7d1"
chosen architecture.
```

---

# 28434. Example

Need:

```text id="iy1qxv"
TACTILE_SENSING
```

---

# 28435. Possible implementations:

```text id="i6pxmf"
resistive
capacitive
optical
piezoelectric
fluidic
```

---

# 28436. Task graph differs dramatically.

---

# 28437. Therefore compiler sequence:

```text id="e4rplk"
Goal
↓
Capability Requirements
↓
Architecture Options
↓
Tasks
```

---

# 28438. Not:

```text id="7hsrqo"
Goal
↓
Tasks
↓
Architecture
```

by default.

---

# 28439. Capability Decomposer

Takes:

```text id="c4bppg"
desired outcome
```

and proposes:

```text id="wrypvu"
functional capabilities.
```

---

# 28440. Example tactile skin:

```text id="m40guh"
SENSE_PRESSURE
LOCALIZE_CONTACT
READ_SENSOR_ARRAY
INTERPRET_SIGNAL
INTEGRATE_WITH_ROBOT
VERIFY_PERFORMANCE
```

---

# 28441. Each becomes:

```text id="d0s1xa"
CONCEPT semantic_role=capability.
```

---

# 28442. Required Capability can itself decompose.

---

# 28443. Example:

```text id="6hps5w"
VERIFY_PERFORMANCE
```

requires:

```text id="uj8hxk"
FORCE_MEASUREMENT
TEST_FIXTURE
DATA_ANALYSIS
```

---

# 28444. Thus build:

# Capability Requirement Graph.

---

# 28445. Graph edges:

```text id="eibrlp"
REQUIRES
DEPENDS_ON
ENABLES
```

---

# 28446. Requirement Leaf

A leaf is capability sufficiently concrete to resolve against:

```text id="v8n4rq"
providers.
```

---

# 28447. Example:

```text id="r2epvw"
3D_PRINT_FLEXIBLE_ENCLOSURE
```

may be leaf.

---

# 28448. But decomposition depth depends on:

```text id="ub30jl"
planning context.
```

---

# 28449. Excess decomposition can create:

```text id="ggz58v"
micro-task explosion.
```

---

# 28450. Therefore compiler needs:

```text id="ud6x15"
planning granularity.
```

---

# 28451. Granularity Modes

```text id="vybfhl"
STRATEGIC
PROGRAM
PROJECT
EXECUTION
```

---

# 28452. STRATEGIC

Capabilities like:

```text id="473xle"
manufacturing
AI perception
funding.
```

---

# 28453. EXECUTION

Capabilities like:

```text id="42j63j"
compile firmware
run calibration test.
```

---

# 28454. Same Mission,

different projections.

---

# 28455. Mission IR

Now define explicit intermediate representation:

# Mission Intermediate Representation

---

# 28456. Mission IR contains:

```text id="03knvt"
Goal
Success Criteria
Capability Graph
Constraints
Unknowns
Context
```

---

# 28457. Example:

```yaml id="yhjagj"
mission_ir:
  goal: robot tactile skin prototype

  required_capabilities:
    - tactile_sensing
    - signal_readout
    - mechanical_integration
    - validation

  unknowns:
    - sensing_technology
```

---

# 28458. Mission IR is:

```text id="e2ccyh"
versioned Artifact.
```

---

# 28459. Why Artifact?

Because it can be:

```text id="htszui"
reviewed
compared
locked
recompiled.
```

---

# 28460. Mission IR v1

May be speculative.

---

# 28461. After research:

```text id="pl7fby"
Mission IR v2.
```

---

# 28462. Version history preserved.

---

# 28463. Mission Compilation is iterative.

---

# 28464. Not one-shot:

```text id="q1vxg5"
prompt → perfect plan.
```

---

# 28465. Better:

```text id="uyjam8"
compile
discover
learn
recompile.
```

---

# 28466. Unknown Registry

Mission IR explicitly tracks:

```text id="r490o5"
unknowns.
```

---

# 28467. Example:

```text id="l8prf7"
Can optical fiber resolve 5 mm contact location?
```

---

# 28468. Unknown becomes:

```text id="4zo0x0"
Knowledge Gap.
```

---

# 28469. Research Observatory resolves.

---

# 28470. Another unknown:

```text id="cd59am"
Is suitable fabrication equipment available locally?
```

---

# 28471. Physical Observatory resolves.

---

# 28472. Another:

```text id="yaz0dx"
Who can design readout electronics?
```

---

# 28473. Talent Resolver.

---

# 28474. Another:

```text id="y12vs1"
How to finance prototype?
```

---

# 28475. Funding Resolver.

---

# 28476. Thus Mission Compiler converts ambiguity into:

# typed gaps.

---

# 28477. Gap Taxonomy

Existing:

```text id="wkl1oi"
Human
Software
Knowledge
Funding
Organization
Physical
Material
Capacity
Logistics
Compute
Authority
```

---

# 28478. Plus:

```text id="ab7kcf"
Verification Gap
```

---

# 28479. Example:

```text id="34uwx6"
prototype can be built
but no test method exists.
```

---

# 28480. That is not ordinary knowledge gap only.

---

# 28481. It is:

```text id="g6cm8z"
verification capability missing.
```

---

# 28482. Mission cannot be considered complete without:

```text id="0j5ngd"
success verification.
```

---

# 28483. Verification-First Planning

Before implementation,

ask:

```text id="n45oex"
How will success be demonstrated?
```

---

# 28484. This can alter architecture.

---

# 28485. Example

Need pressure sensor accuracy ±5%.

---

# 28486. Then test rig requires:

```text id="ipp7yy"
reference load cell
calibration fixture.
```

---

# 28487. These become requirements early.

---

# 28488. Avoid pattern:

```text id="at60n4"
build first
invent validation later.
```

---

# 28489. Verification Contract

For each critical capability:

```yaml id="8lna3j"
verification:
  capability: tactile_sensing
  method: calibrated_force_test
  pass_condition: ...
```

---

# 28490. Verification method may itself require:

```text id="7brrmu"
resources.
```

---

# 28491. Thus verification enters Resource Resolver.

---

# 28492. Architecture Option Generation

Once capabilities defined,

system can construct:

```text id="g2phsv"
alternative provider combinations.
```

---

# 28493. Example sensing architecture:

```text id="42qs8k"
Option A:
fiber optic

Option B:
capacitive matrix

Option C:
piezoresistive textile
```

---

# 28494. Each option has:

```text id="ynj8tz"
capabilities
dependencies
unknowns
test requirements
```

---

# 28495. Architecture Option ≠ Product Recommendation.

---

# 28496. It is technical path.

---

# 28497. Option Graph

```text id="a3fef3"
Mission
├─ Architecture A
├─ Architecture B
└─ Architecture C
```

---

# 28498. Each branch gets:

```text id="awyxyr"
Gap Set.
```

---

# 28499. Example A requires:

```text id="0usv88"
optical interrogator.
```

---

# 28500. B requires:

```text id="n9rhrw"
dense electrode fabrication.
```

---

# 28501. C requires:

```text id="ya7cl5"
conductive elastomer process.
```

---

# 28502. Thus feasibility differs.

---

# 28503. Option Elimination

Hard constraints can eliminate.

---

# 28504. Example:

```text id="2zfv0v"
must tolerate electromagnetic environment
```

may affect choices.

---

# 28505. But elimination must cite:

```text id="tycvso"
constraint + evidence.
```

---

# 28506. LLM should not silently discard branch.

---

# 28507. Option status:

```text id="4venpv"
OPEN
BLOCKED
INFEASIBLE
DEFERRED
SELECTED_FOR_PILOT
REJECTED
```

---

# 28508. `REJECTED`

means:

```text id="lysaop"
not selected in this Mission Context.
```

---

# 28509. Keep evidence for future reuse.

---

# 28510. Pareto Project Architectures

Compare dimensions:

```text id="99l7mh"
time
cost
risk
control
capability coverage
verification burden
```

---

# 28511. No opaque overall score.

---

# 28512. Example:

```text id="ef99pc"
A faster but expensive.
B cheaper but research-heavy.
C easier to manufacture but less sensitive.
```

---

# 28513. Human/governance decides trade-off where needed.

---

# 28514. Autonomous selection allowed only if:

```text id="jgc10n"
policy defines decision rule.
```

---

# 28515. Example:

```text id="jnlmgi"
choose cheapest option
meeting all MUST requirements
under €500
```

---

# 28516. Then machine decision can be deterministic/explainable.

---

# 28517. Architecture Lock

Selected project architecture stored as:

```text id="hhbyex"
architecture.lock
```

---

# 28518. Similar to:

```text id="so53j5"
project.lock.
```

---

# 28519. Contains:

```text id="rkt6k6"
selected providers/contracts
versions
assumptions
```

---

# 28520. But provider not always specific Resource yet.

---

# 28521. Example:

```text id="h27guu"
requires CNC capability
```

can remain unresolved until schedule time.

---

# 28522. Therefore lock may contain:

```text id="kjzwpi"
capability contract
```

instead of concrete provider.

---

# 28523. Late Binding

Very important.

---

# 28524. Bind Resource:

```text id="hcg50i"
as late as practical
```

when availability uncertain.

---

# 28525. Example:

```text id="atdqfp"
which exact 3D printer?
```

can be resolved near execution.

---

# 28526. Early Binding

Necessary where:

```text id="hmssvv"
design depends on provider-specific constraints.
```

---

# 28527. Example:

```text id="yzgkw8"
PCB fab minimum trace width.
```

---

# 28528. Then provider characteristics influence design.

---

# 28529. Binding Strategy

Each requirement can specify:

```text id="avfx0x"
EARLY
LATE
JUST_IN_TIME
```

---

# 28530. This reduces unnecessary rigidity.

---

# 28531. Cross-Domain Resolver

Now central engine:

```text id="o1vmvg"
Capability Requirement
↓
Resolver Router
```

---

# 28532. Router chooses:

```text id="8dbv94"
Talent
GitHub
Research
Funding
Physical
Compute
Federation
```

---

# 28533. One requirement may need:

```text id="t9phfm"
multiple resolvers.
```

---

# 28534. Example:

```text id="x4ey9d"
optical tactile sensing prototype
```

requires:

```text id="fhyz1y"
knowledge
person
lab
software
material
```

---

# 28535. Therefore use:

# Composite Capability Resolution.

---

# 28536. Composite Provider Bundle

Example:

```text id="b1a72n"
Researcher
+
Fiber sensor paper
+
DAQ software
+
Optical interrogator
+
Lab time
```

---

# 28537. Bundle collectively:

```text id="5hp7au"
PROVIDES
prototype capability.
```

---

# 28538. No single Resource does.

---

# 28539. This is one of most important project assembly concepts.

---

# 28540. Bundle Constraints

Need check:

```text id="x7011c"
time compatibility
location compatibility
interfaces
authority
budget
```

---

# 28541. Example:

lab available in Germany,

expert available remotely,

equipment requires on-site operator.

---

# 28542. Feasible bundle may require:

```text id="rbm4lm"
local technician
+
remote expert.
```

---

# 28543. Resource Composition

Could be:

```text id="j8ubnp"
SEQUENTIAL
PARALLEL
JOINT
ALTERNATIVE
```

---

# 28544. SEQUENTIAL

Researcher designs,

manufacturer builds.

---

# 28545. PARALLEL

Firmware and enclosure developed simultaneously.

---

# 28546. JOINT

Operator + machine needed together.

---

# 28547. ALTERNATIVE

Two possible labs.

---

contents.content: Следующий блок логично продолжать с **29318**: портфель тысяч Missions, обнаружение дублирования, shared capability demand, общая инфраструктура, межпроектные зависимости, portfolio bottlenecks, shared services, capability-investment proposals и переход от «автоматизации одного проекта» к «операционной системе целой инновационной экосистемы».

Продолжаю с **29318**. Теперь поднимаемся от управления отдельной Mission к уровню всей экосистемы: как тысячи проектов совместно формируют спрос на capabilities, где возникает дублирование, какие ресурсы стоит сделать общими и как портфель координировать без превращения системы в централизованный «директорат».

# Innovation Portfolio Intelligence, Shared Capability Planning & Ecosystem-Level Resource Orchestration v0.1
